title: public-preview.quarto-hub.com in maintenance since Oct 29 – approved account rejected on quarto-hub.com
description:
Since October 29, https://public-preview.quarto-hub.com returns HTTP 503 with the page "Quarto Hub is undergoing maintenance". My account was approved for the public preview, but signing in at https://quarto-hub.com fails with "Your account is not authorized to access this hub."

Is there an expected date for the preview to return, or should approved preview users move to another address? Thanks!

title: No diagnostic for Quarto 1 ```{mermaid} and ```{dot} cells: they silently render as code blocks
description:
q2 does not support Quarto 1 diagram cells, ```` ```{mermaid} ```` and ```` ```{dot} ````. The [Diagrams guide](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/main/docs/guides/authoring/diagrams.qmd) says so under "Differences from Quarto 1". But q2 gives no diagnostic when it meets one. The cell renders as a code block, and the braces end up in the class name. In a migrated project, every diagram silently becomes its source code, and only a person who looks at the page finds out.

A diagnostic like [`Q-2-50`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/main/docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-50.qmd), which q2 already gives for the Quarto 1 ```` ```{{python}} ```` escape, would help migrations a lot.

## Versions

- q2 0.40.0 and 0.41.0-nightly.20261105 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison

## Repro

`index.qmd`, with no `_quarto.yml`:

````markdown
---
title: Diagram
---

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Draft] --> B[Review]
```
````

```bash
q2 render index.qmd
```

## Expected

A warning that names the line, says that q2 does not run ```` ```{mermaid} ```` cells, and suggests ```` ```mermaid ```` (the Diagrams guide's fix). For ```` ```{dot} ````, a warning that Graphviz diagrams are not available yet.

(Quarto 1.11.7 draws the diagram: `<pre class="mermaid mermaid-js">`, plus the Mermaid scripts.)

## Actual (q2)

The log has only `Rendering single file: …/index.qmd`. No warning. The output is a code block:

```html
<pre class="{mermaid} code-with-copy">
```

The same happens with ```` ```{dot} ````: no warning, and `<pre class="{dot} code-with-copy">`.

## Notes

- The class value `{mermaid}` (with the braces) also looks unintended, whether or not a diagnostic is added.
- In one real migration, a docs site had 33 ```` ```{mermaid} ```` diagrams on 14 pages. The render was clean, and the only signal was a text comparison with the Quarto 1 site.

title: Built-in highlighting for ```qmd (and ```markdown / ```md) code blocks with q2's own qmd parser
description:
q2 has no built-in highlighting for Quarto markdown in code blocks: ```` ```qmd ````, ```` ```markdown ````, and ```` ```md ```` render as plain `<pre>` with no `sourceCode` wrapper. Documentation about Quarto and about publishing tools shows a lot of qmd and markdown. q2 already has its own qmd parser, `tree-sitter-qmd`, so it is the natural grammar for these blocks.

## Versions

- q2 0.41.0 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison

## Repro

`index.qmd`, with no `_quarto.yml`:

``````markdown
---
title: qmd highlighting
engine: markdown
---

`````qmd
---
title: "Report"
format: html
---

## Results

Some **bold** text and a [link](https://example.com).

```{python}
#| echo: false
print("hello")
```
`````

````markdown
## Results

Some **bold** text.
````
``````

```bash
q2 render index.qmd
```

## Quarto 1.11.7

- ```` ```qmd ````: not highlighted (`<pre class="qmd">`). Pandoc's highlighter does not know `qmd`.
- ```` ```markdown ````: highlighted with Pandoc's Markdown syntax (`<pre class="sourceCode markdown">`, heading tokens).

## q2 0.41.0

Both blocks are `<pre class="qmd code-with-copy">` and `<pre class="markdown code-with-copy">`, with no spans and no `div.sourceCode` wrapper.

## Request

Highlight `qmd`, with `markdown` and `md` as aliases, using q2's own parser: front matter, headings, emphasis, links, code cells and their `#|` options, shortcodes, and divs. Ideally, embedded code cells and YAML front matter are highlighted with the matching built-in grammars, like an injection.

## Notes

I tried the user-grammar route first. `tree-sitter build --wasm` on `crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown` gives a 1.1 MB WASM file. It loads from `_quarto/grammars/` only under the name `markdown`, because the WASM exports `tree_sitter_markdown` and the user-grammar loader derives the language function from the file name, so it cannot register `qmd`. With the bundled `queries/highlights.scm`, only `**strong**` and some punctuation get spans. Headings, links, front matter, and the nested code cell stay plain. A built-in, native path seems better than asking projects to vendor a large WASM build of q2's own parser.

title: Code block language matching is case-sensitive: ```R and ```Dockerfile are not highlighted
description:
q2 matches a code block's language class to a grammar case-sensitively. ```` ```R ```` and ```` ```Dockerfile ```` are not highlighted, though ```` ```r ```` and ```` ```dockerfile ```` are. Quarto 1 (Pandoc) matches language names case-insensitively and writes the lowercase name on the output, so ```` ```R ```` renders as `<pre class="sourceCode r">`.

## Versions

- q2 0.41.0 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison

## Repro

`index.qmd`, with no `_quarto.yml`:

`````markdown
---
title: Language case
---

```R
x <- 1
```

```r
x <- 1
```

```{.R filename="example.R"}
x <- 1
```
`````

```bash
q2 render index.qmd
```

## Expected (Quarto 1.11.7)

All three blocks are highlighted as R:

```html
<pre class="sourceCode r code-with-copy">
<pre class="sourceCode r code-with-copy">
<pre class="sourceCode R code-with-copy" data-filename="example.R">
```

(Quarto 1 lowercases the class for a bare ```` ```R ```` fence but keeps `R` on the `{.R}` attribute form. It highlights both.)

## Actual (q2 0.41.0)

Only the lowercase block is highlighted:

```html
<pre class="R code-with-copy">          <!-- no spans -->
<pre class="sourceCode r">                <!-- highlighted -->
<pre class="R code-with-copy" data-filename="example.R">   <!-- no spans -->
```

## Notes

- The same applies to user grammars from `_quarto/grammars/`: a grammar in `dockerfile/` does not highlight ```` ```Dockerfile ````.
- `quarto-highlight` does not lowercase the class anywhere before the lookup (`Registry::highlight`, `UserGrammars::contains` and `highlight`). Lowercasing the class for the lookup only would highlight all three blocks and keep the author's class on the element.

title: Code blocks in a language without a grammar get no div.sourceCode wrapper, so they lose the code-block box
description:
When q2 has no grammar for a code block's language, it writes a bare `<pre class="<lang> code-with-copy">`, with no `div.sourceCode` wrapper and no `sourceCode` classes. The theme draws the code-block box (background, border, padding) on `div.sourceCode`, so these blocks render as plain text on the page background. Quarto 1 (Pandoc) wraps every block whose language its highlighter knows in `div.sourceCode`, even when it adds no colors. An example is ```` ```default ````.

So a migrated site loses the code-block box on every block in a language outside q2's grammar set, not only the colors.

## Versions

- q2 0.41.0 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison
- Chrome, 1280×800 viewport, default theme

## Repro

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: Example
```

`index.qmd`:

`````markdown
---
title: Code styling
---

```ini
[Widget]
; Turn the widget on.
Enabled = true
```

```default
/opt/widget/1.0/bin/widget
```

```bash
echo "highlighted in both"
```
`````

```bash
q2 render
```

## Expected (Quarto 1.11.7)

All three blocks are `div.sourceCode` > `pre.sourceCode.<lang>`, and all three have the box. Computed style of each `div.sourceCode`: background `rgba(233, 236, 239, 0.65)`, border `1px solid`. The `default` block has the box but no colors.

```html
<pre class="sourceCode ini code-with-copy">
<pre class="sourceCode default code-with-copy">
<pre class="sourceCode bash code-with-copy">
```

## Actual (q2 0.41.0)

```html
<pre class="ini code-with-copy">
<pre class="default code-with-copy">
<pre class="sourceCode bash">
```

Only the `bash` block has the box. The `ini` and `default` blocks have background `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and no border.

## Notes

- Quarto 1 still leaves blocks with **no** language, and languages its highlighter does not know (for example `text`, `nginx`), without the wrapper. So "wrap every block that has a language class" would box a few blocks that Quarto 1 does not. To me that looks like the better default, but it is a choice.
- Scale, from one real documentation site (about 2,070 code blocks): 617 blocks lost the box after the migration. They were `ini` 466, `default` 113, `markdown` 24, `toml` 5, and a few each of `dockerfile`, `xml`, `powershell`, `apache`, `conf`, and `txt`.
- A user grammar in `_quarto/grammars/<lang>/` fixes this for one language, because a highlighted block gets the wrapper. But that does not help `default`, which has nothing to highlight.

title: Navbar item is not marked active on pages in its sidebar section (Quarto 1 marks it)
description:
On a website, a navbar item is marked active only on the page that it links to. Quarto 1 also marks it active on every page in the sidebar that contains that page, so readers can see which section of the site they are in.

## Versions

- q2 0.40.0 and 0.41.0-nightly.20261105 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison

## Repro

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: Example
  navbar:
    left:
      - text: Home
        href: index.qmd
      - text: Guide
        href: guide/index.qmd
  sidebar:
    - title: Guide
      contents:
        - guide/index.qmd
        - guide/install.qmd
```

`index.qmd`, `guide/index.qmd`, and `guide/install.qmd` each have a `title:` and one paragraph.

```bash
q2 render
```

## Expected (Quarto 1.11.7)

In `_site/guide/install.html`, the Guide link is active, because `guide/index.qmd` is in the sidebar of the current page:

```html
<a class="nav-link" href="../index.html">
<a class="nav-link active" href="../guide/index.html" aria-current="page">
```

## Actual (q2)

In `_site/guide/install.html`, no navbar link is active:

```html
<a href="../index.html" class="nav-link">
<a href="index.html" class="nav-link">
```

In `_site/guide/index.html`, the Guide link is active, as expected. Neither page has `aria-current="page"` on the active link.

## Notes

Quarto 1 marks the active link in its website post-processing of each rendered page. It walks the `a.nav-link` elements in order and marks the **first** link whose `href` is the current page, or whose `href` is also a link in the page's `.sidebar-navigation`. It adds both `class="active"` and `aria-current="page"`, then stops.

q2's `mark_active` (`crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/navigation_active.rs`), called from `navbar_generate.rs`, marks an item only when `href == page_source`.

On a large docs site, this means the navbar never shows the current section on any page except the section landing pages.

title: Sidebar does not scroll the active item into view on page load
description:
On a website with a long sidebar, Quarto 1 scrolls the sidebar so that the active item is visible when a page loads. q2 does not: the sidebar always starts at the top, so on a page far down the list the reader cannot see where the page is in the navigation.

## Versions

- q2 0.40.0 and 0.41.0-nightly.20261105 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison
- Chrome, 1280×800 viewport

## Repro

A website with 41 pages in one sidebar. `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: Example
  sidebar:
    - title: Pages
      contents:
        - index.qmd
        - page-01.qmd
        - page-02.qmd
        # ... through page-40.qmd
```

Each `page-NN.qmd` has `title: Page NN` and one paragraph.

```bash
q2 render
```

Open `_site/page-35.html` in a browser at 1280×800.

## Expected (Quarto 1.11.7)

The sidebar is scrolled so that "Page 35" is visible:

```
scrollTop: 326, scrollHeight: 1126, clientHeight: 800
active item "Page 35" at top: 647 px, visible
```

## Actual (q2)

The sidebar is not scrolled. "Page 35" is below the visible part of the sidebar:

```
scrollTop: 0, scrollHeight: 1132, clientHeight: 800
active item "Page 35" at top: 979 px, not visible
```

The active item itself is correct (`a.active` on "Page 35"). Only the scroll is missing.

## Notes

Quarto 1 does this in the browser, in `site_libs/quarto-nav/quarto-nav.js` ("Scroll the active navigation item into view, if necessary"). A `ResizeObserver` on `nav#quarto-sidebar` waits until the sidebar has its final height. Then, if `li.sidebar-item a.active` is below the visible area, it sets `navSidebar.scrollTop` to the item's `offsetTop`. The `quarto-nav.js` that q2 writes does not have this block.

title: Listing preview of exactly max-description-length characters is truncated (Quarto 1 keeps it whole)
description:
When a listing item has no `description:`, both engines use the first paragraph of the item's page as the preview and truncate it to `max-description-length` (default 175). Quarto 1 keeps a paragraph of exactly 175 characters whole. q2 truncates it to 170 characters plus `…`.

## Versions

- q2 0.40.0 and 0.41.0-nightly.20261105 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison

## Repro

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: Example
```

`index.qmd`:

```yaml
---
title: Items
listing:
  contents: items
  sort: title
  type: table
  fields: [title, description]
---
```

`items/exactly-175.qmd` has `title: Exactly 175` and a first paragraph of exactly 175 characters, with no markup. `items/exactly-176.qmd` is the same with 176 characters. The paragraph text is plain words, for example:

```markdown
Every the quick widget passes every review before it ships to the next team the quick widget passes every review before it ships to the next team the quick widget passes ever.
```

(That line is the 175-character paragraph.)

```bash
q2 render
```

## Expected (Quarto 1.11.7)

| Item | Description length | Ends with |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly 175 | 175 | `…the quick widget passes ever.` (whole paragraph) |
| Exactly 176 | 170 | `…the quick widget passes…` |

## Actual (q2)

| Item | Description length | Ends with |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly 175 | 170 | `…the quick widget passes…` |
| Exactly 176 | 170 | `…the quick widget passes…` |

## Notes

The doc comment on `truncate_text_at_space` (`crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/helpers.rs`) says that a string of exactly `max` characters is truncated, because Quarto 1's `trimLength` compares with a strict `<`. That is true of `trimLength` alone. But in the preview path, Quarto 1 never calls `trimLength` for such a string. Its `truncateNode` helper, which the listing description substitution uses, walks the text nodes of the first paragraph. It calls `truncateText` only when `currentLength + textNodeLen > maxLen`, so text of exactly `maxLen` characters is kept whole.

Changing the guard in the preview path (`post_render_upgrade/reader.rs`) to "truncate when longer than `max`" would match Quarto 1. Whether the feed path (`feed/reader_ext.rs`) should match too depends on what Quarto 1 does for feeds. I did not check that.

title: page-footer items wrap onto separate lines: footer list has class "nav" (Quarto 1: "list-unstyled")
description:
q2 renders each `page-footer` region as `<ul class="nav footer-items">`. Quarto 1 uses `<ul class="footer-items list-unstyled">`. Bootstrap's `.nav` sets `flex-wrap: wrap`, so items in one footer region wrap onto separate lines. A common footer, a logo followed by a copyright line, renders on two lines in q2 and on one line in Quarto 1.

## Versions

- q2 0.40.0 and 0.41.0-nightly.20261105 (macOS, arm64)
- Quarto 1.11.7, for comparison
- Chrome, 1280×800 viewport

## Repro

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: Example
  page-footer:
    left:
      - text: '![Example](images/logo.svg){width="65px"}'
        href: https://example.com
      - Copyright © 2015-2026 Example Corporation. All Rights Reserved.
    center: Example Product 1.0
    right:
      - text: Support
        href: https://example.com/support
      - text: Docs
        href: https://example.com/docs
```

`index.qmd` has a title and one paragraph. `images/logo.svg` is any 130×30 SVG.

```bash
q2 render
```

## Expected (Quarto 1.11.7)

```html
<div class="nav-footer-left">
  <ul class="footer-items list-unstyled">
```

The logo and the copyright are on one line. Computed style of the `<ul>`: `display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: nowrap`. Both `<li>` elements have top 727 px; their left edges are 17 px and 93 px.

## Actual (q2)

```html
<div class="nav-footer-left">
  <ul class="nav footer-items">
```

The copyright wraps below the logo. Computed style of the `<ul>`: `display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: wrap`. The `<li>` elements have tops 681 px and 719 px, and both have left edge 30 px.

## Notes

A project can work around it with CSS: `.nav-footer .footer-items { flex-wrap: nowrap; }` puts the two items back on one line (tops 681 px and 681 px). But the footer layout differs from Quarto 1 with no change to the project. If `.nav` is on the list deliberately, for example for the `.nav-link` styles, `flex-wrap: nowrap` on `.nav-footer .footer-items` in the built-in theme would keep the Quarto 1 layout.

title: Navbar dropdown menus on the right side are missing `dropdown-menu-end`
description:
## Problem A dropdown menu in `website.navbar.right` opens aligned to the left edge of its toggle. A menu near the right edge of the page then runs past the edge, and its spacing looks wrong. Quarto 1 adds Bootstrap's `dropdown-menu-end` class to menus in the right navbar section, so the menu aligns to the right edge of its toggle (`navitem.ejs`: `dropdown-menu<%- align === 'end' ? ' dropdown-menu-end' : '' %>`). q2 does not add this class. ## To reproduce ```yaml website: navbar: right: - text: Help menu: - text: Item one href: https://example.com - text: Item two href: https://example.com ``` 1. Render the site with `q2 render`. 2. Open a page and click **Help**. Expected: `
    `, and the menu stays in the page. Actual: `
      `, and the menu runs past the right edge. ## Environment - q2 0.40.0-nightly.20261104 (compared with Quarto 1.10.18) - macOS - Found with the `posit-dev/product-doc-theme@q2` extension, which adds a right-side Help menu

title: Website headings have no anchor links (the Quarto 1 hover link icon)
description:
## Problem In a q2 website, section headings are not clickable. In Quarto 1, a link icon shows when you hover over a heading, so readers can copy a link to that section. In q2, no icon shows. The sections have IDs, so links such as `#events` work. The missing part is the hover anchor link. Quarto 1 adds it with anchor.js (from `quarto-html-after-body.ejs` / `quarto.js`), and q2 does not load that script. ## To reproduce 1. Render a website that has `##` headings: `q2 render` 2. Open a page and hover over a heading. Expected: a link icon shows next to the heading (Quarto 1 behavior). Actual: no icon shows, and the heading is not a link. Rendered output, for reference: ```html

Events

``` There is no anchor script in the page `

title: hub-client: allow user display names longer than 50 characters
description:
# Goal

`updateUserName` accepts display names longer than 50 characters, so an embedding app can label a collaborator with their full name without cutting it.

Done when:

- `isValidUserName` allows a larger maximum (or one an embedder can rely on for full names, e.g. 100+ characters).
- The presence and attribution UI handles long names without breaking layout (e.g. ellipsis).

# Why

- **Embedders pass real full names.** The Posit Connect Quarto Hub editor (connect-satellites `quartohub`) labels each collaborator with their Connect first and last name. Names longer than 50 characters exist, and `updateUserName` throws on them (`Invalid user name: must be 1-50 characters`), which would stop the editor from opening.
- **The current workaround drops information.** The embedder cuts the name to 50 characters before calling `updateUserName`, so long names show cut off in attribution and on cursors.

# References

- `hub-client/src/services/storage/utils.ts` (`isValidUserName`)
- `hub-client/src/services/userSettings.ts` (`updateUserName`)
- `hub-client/src/services/presenceService.ts` (where the name is shown)
- Issue: quartohub: attribute edits to the Connect user instead of a per-browser id posit-dev/connect-satellites#88

title: Citations in HTML stay as `@key` when `bibliography` is set
description: ### Bug description A document with `bibliography: refs.bib` and a `[@doe2020]` citation renders to HTML with the citation left as the text `@doe2020`. There is no reference list, no warning, and the exit code is 0. Quarto 1 runs citeproc whenever a bibliography is set. q2 has a citeproc filter that works, but for HTML it only runs when the `filters` list names it. The filter is reached only through the resolved `filters` list: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/filter_resolve.rs#L53-L91 The one place that turns `citeproc: true` into a list entry runs for Pandoc-hybrid formats only. Its comment says that HTML has its own citation path, but nothing resolves the citations of a single HTML document: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/user_filters.rs#L117-L127 Listing the filter may be the intended q2 syntax, since the book guide shows `filters: [citeproc]`. If so, it is documented only there, and the render gives no hint when citations stay unresolved. ### Steps to reproduce `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- format: html bibliography: refs.bib --- See [@doe2020]. ``` `refs.bib`: ```bibtex @article{doe2020, author = {Doe, Jane}, title = {A title}, journal = {A Journal}, year = {2020} } ``` Run q2 and Quarto 1 on it: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` Then count the reference entries: ```sh grep -c 'csl-entry' index.html ``` ### Actual behavior `grep` prints `0` for q2, and the body holds the citation as plain text: ```html @doe2020 ``` Quarto 1.12.0 prints `4` and writes the resolved citation: ```html (Doe 2020) ``` With `filters: [citeproc]`, q2 writes `(Doe 2020)` and the reference list, so the filter itself works. ### Expected behavior The citation reads `(Doe 2020)` and links to an entry in `#refs`, as in Quarto 1. Setting `bibliography` or `citeproc: true` should be enough for HTML. If listing the filter is the intended way, the guides could say so for every format, and q2 could warn when a citation is left as `@key`. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: A callout with an id loses its number in the default title
description:
### Bug description A callout with an id such as `nte-x` and no title gets the title "Note 1" in Quarto 1. q2 gives it the title "Note". The reference `@nte-x` reads "Note 1" in both engines, so the page names a number that the callout does not show. The default title is built from the callout type alone. The transform knows that the callout is a cross-reference target (`ref_type`), but it does not add the number: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/callout_resolve.rs#L240-L262 The comment in that block expects such a callout to carry a cross-reference prefix in its title, so the number seems meant to be there. ### Steps to reproduce `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- format: html --- ::: {#nte-x .callout-note} Body. ::: See @nte-x. ``` Run q2 and Quarto 1 on it: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 gives the callout the title "Note", while the link text has the number: ```html
Note
...

See Note 1.

``` Quarto 1.12.0 writes "Note 1" in both places. ### Expected behavior The title reads "Note 1", as in Quarto 1. The default title should use the same prefix and number as the cross-reference. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `theme: default` and `theme: pandoc` are rejected with Q-14-2
description:
### Bug description

The Quarto 1 guide lists `default`, `pandoc` and `none` next to the Bootswatch names:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/001d4331e337e86b0cf97e0956c445224280a28b/docs/output-formats/html-themes.qmd?plain=1#L10-L16

q2 accepts `none` and the Bootswatch names, but stops with `Q-14-2` (`Unknown theme name`) on `default` and on `pandoc`.
Quarto 1 renders both: `default` with plain Bootstrap, and `pandoc` with no Bootstrap at all:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/format/html/format-html-info.ts#L25-L28

`ThemeSpec::parse` accepts a file path, the `brand` marker, or a name that parses as a `BuiltInTheme`.
`default` and `pandoc` are none of these, so the parse returns `UnknownTheme`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-sass/src/themes.rs#L259-L280

The q2 HTML themes guide mentions only Bootswatch names, files and `none`, so a document that follows the Quarto 1 guide fails to render.

Related: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1034

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format:
  html:
    theme: default
---
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with:

```text
Error: [Q-14-2] Unknown theme name
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/q2-theme.WSn1/index.qmd:4:12 ]
   │
 4 │     theme: default
   │            ───┬───
   │               ╰───── `default` is not a recognized built-in theme and is not a path to a `.scss`/`.css` file.
───╯
ℹ Use one of the built-in Bootswatch names (e.g. `cosmo`, `darkly`), a path to a `.scss`/`.css` file, or `theme: none` to suppress Bootstrap?
```

`theme: pandoc` gives the same error.
Quarto 1.12.0 renders both and prints `Output created: index.html`.

### Expected behavior

`theme: default` renders with the default Bootstrap theme, and `theme: pandoc` renders without Bootstrap, as in Quarto 1.
`ThemeSpec::parse` could map `default` to no Bootswatch layer, and `pandoc` to the same path as `none` or to a Pandoc-style page.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: A theme `@import` finds Bootstrap's partial before the theme's own file
description:
### Bug description

I found this with the theme of my website, a project extension that imports its own `_mixins.scss`:

https://github.com/mcanouil/mickael.canouil.fr/blob/88f7349af2425156566f2e7ff984677dc46c0d0d/_extensions/mickaelcanouilfr/scss/mickaelcanouilfr.scss#L5

https://github.com/mcanouil/mickael.canouil.fr/blob/88f7349af2425156566f2e7ff984677dc46c0d0d/_extensions/mickaelcanouilfr/scss/_mixins.scss#L7

A custom theme that does `@import "mixins"` gets Bootstrap's `_mixins.scss` instead of the `_mixins.scss` next to it.
The import succeeds, so nothing warns.
The render fails later, when the theme calls one of its own mixins (`Undefined mixin`).

Quarto 1 puts the directory of each theme file ahead of the Bootstrap directories, so the theme's own partial wins:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/format/html/format-html-scss.ts#L136-L141

q2 passes the Bootstrap directories first, and Dart Sass takes the first match.
Any partial named like a Bootstrap one (`mixins`, `variables`, `functions`, `utilities`, `maps`) is affected.

The compiler starts from the default Bootstrap load paths and appends the theme directories after them:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs#L118-L121

The default paths are the Bootstrap and Sass utility resources:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-sass/src/resources.rs#L325-L330

### Steps to reproduce

`custom.scss`:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/
@import "mixins";
@include accent-box(red);
```

`_mixins.scss`:

```scss
@mixin accent-box($colour) {
  .accent-box {
    color: $colour;
  }
}
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format:
  html:
    theme: custom.scss
---
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with:

```text
Error: [Q-14-6] Theme SCSS compilation failed
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/q2-scss.vuLn/index.qmd:4:12 ]
   │
 4 │     theme: custom.scss
   │            ─────┬─────
   │                 ╰─────── compiling the theme SCSS bundle failed:
Error: Undefined mixin.
     ╷
9886 │ @include accent-box(red);
     │          ^^^^^^^^^^
     ╵
./stdin:9886:10
───╯
```

The hint that follows asks about theme variables, which is not the cause here.

Quarto 1 renders the page and prints `Output created: index.html`.

### Expected behavior

`@import "mixins"` resolves to the file next to the theme, as it does in Quarto 1, and the page renders.
Putting the theme directories before the Bootstrap directories in the load path list would do it.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: A Reveal.js format extension takes the Bootstrap theme path and loses Reveal.js
description:
### Bug description

I found this with one of my Reveal.js format extensions, which contributes `theme: [default, theme.scss]` to its `revealjs` format.
Quarto 1 renders the deck.
q2 stops with `Q-14-2` (`Unknown theme name`), because the extension format goes through the Bootstrap theme path, which only knows Bootswatch names.

Without `theme`, q2 renders the extension deck, but the page calls `Reveal.initialize` without loading `reveal.js` or any Reveal.js CSS, so the deck does not run.
The same settings work under `format: revealjs`.

The pipeline profile already maps an extension format such as `demo-revealjs` to Reveal.js through its base format:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/format.rs#L552-L559

The theme stage checks the raw target name instead, with `is_revealjs_target`, which matches only `revealjs` and `q2-slides`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs#L578-L591

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/format.rs#L481-L483

That branch both resolves the Reveal.js theme and registers the Reveal.js assets, so an extension deck gets neither.

### Steps to reproduce

`_extensions/demo/_extension.yml`:

```yaml
contributes:
  formats:
    revealjs:
      theme: default
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format: demo-revealjs
---

## Slide
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with:

```text
Error [Q-14-2]: Unknown theme name
`default` is not a recognized built-in theme and is not a path to a `.scss`/`.css` file.
ℹ Use one of the built-in Bootswatch names (e.g. `cosmo`, `darkly`), a path to a `.scss`/`.css` file, or `theme: none` to suppress Bootstrap?
```

Quarto 1 renders the deck and prints `Output created: index.html`.

### Expected behavior

The deck renders with the Reveal.js theme and assets, as it does for `format: revealjs`.
The theme stage, and the other `is_revealjs_target` callers such as `metadata_merge.rs`, could use the base format, as `PipelineProfile::from_format` does.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: `q2 render --no-execute` is rejected although the help text mentions it
description:
### Bug description

The help text of `q2 render --execute` reads "Execute code (--no-execute to skip execution)".
`q2 render index.qmd --no-execute` stops with `unexpected argument '--no-execute' found` and exit code 2.

The flag is declared as a plain `bool`, so clap only knows `--execute`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto/src/main.rs#L81-L83

Nothing reads `--execute` either.
The `Render` arm ignores the field and always passes `ExecutionPolicy::All`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto/src/main.rs#L1730-L1732

Quarto 1 skips code execution with `--no-execute`.
People use it to preview a layout, or to render on a machine without R or Python.
Without it, a document with a failing or slow code cell cannot be rendered for a quick check.

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
```{r}
1 + 1
```
````

With q2:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd --no-execute
```

With Quarto 1:

```sh
quarto render index.qmd --no-execute
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with exit code 2:

```text
error: unexpected argument '--no-execute' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--execute'
  tip: to pass '--no-execute' as a value, use '-- --no-execute'

Usage: q2 render --execute <INPUTS>... [-- <PANDOC_ARGS>...]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

### Expected behavior

The document renders and the R chunk is not executed, as in Quarto 1, where `index.html` does not contain `[1] 2`.
An engine-level execution policy already exists, because `q2 preview --static` narrows it, so the render command could set it from the flag.
If q2 does not plan to support the flag, the help text should not mention it.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: knitr: fig-width, fig-height and fig-format are silently ignored outside execute: and cell options
description:
## Problem

`fig-width`, `fig-height` and `fig-format` are silently ignored for knitr documents unless they are under `execute:` or set on the cell. No warning is emitted, so the figure simply comes out at the defaults (7×5 in, 672×480 px PNG).

`docs/guides/authoring/figures.qmd` previously told readers to set `fig-width` and `fig-height` "in the document header", which leads straight to this.

## Reproduction

```` markdown
---
title: t
fig-width: 9
fig-height: 4
fig-format: svg
---

```{r}
plot(1:3)
```
````

`q2 render` exits 0 with no warning and produces a 672×480 PNG instead of an SVG.

## Results by placement

Tested with q2 0.39.0 and R 4.6.0 on macOS:

| Where the options go | Result |
|---|---|
| Top level of the header | ignored, no warning |
| `format: html:` | ignored, no warning |
| `execute:` | works |
| Cell `#\|` comments | works |

## Cause

The knitr engine only overlays the `execute:` scope onto its defaults (`build_format_config` in `crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs`, which calls `overlay_document_scope` in `engine/knitr/format.rs`).

Only knitr was tested; Jupyter's behavior is unknown.

## Decision needed

Either honor these options at the top level and under `format: <fmt>:`, or warn when they appear there.

The docs passage has been corrected locally (not yet committed) to describe the `execute:` form and to state that the other placements have no effect. That wording would need to change if the options become honored.

title: Letter, roman and `#.` list markers are read as paragraphs
description:
### Bug description Pandoc reads `a)`, `A.`, `(i)` and `#.` at the start of a line as ordered list markers (the `fancy_lists` extension). Quarto 1 has it on by default, and writes `ol type="a"`, `ol type="A"`, `ol type="i"` or a plain `ol`. q2 only accepts digits in front of `.` or `)`, so every other marker stays text, with no warning. A q2 design note for the docx import work already records that qmd has no fancy list markers. That work reports the lost list style and leaves the parser as it is, so the note does not say whether q2 plans to support these markers: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/claude-notes/plans/2026-10-03-document-import-epic.md?plain=1#L44 Nothing tells a user, and a Quarto 1 document changes meaning without an error. The scanner sends a line to `parse_ordered_list_marker` only when it starts with a digit, and that function has no branch for letters, roman numerals or `#`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c#L1400-L1413 https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c#L3359-L3373 The marker is then stored as a number, and `process_list_marker` parses it as `usize`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/list_marker.rs#L25-L41 ### Steps to reproduce `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- format: html --- a) First b) Second ``` Run q2 and Quarto 1 on it: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 renders two paragraphs and the HTML has no `ol`: ```html

a) First

b) Second

``` Quarto 1.12.0 renders an ordered list: ```html

  1. First

  2. Second

``` ### Expected behavior The markers give ordered lists with the matching `type` attribute, as in Quarto 1. If q2 does not plan to support these markers, the notes on differences from Quarto 1 could say so, and q2 could warn when a line starts with one of them. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `reference-doc` in an extension format is not resolved against the extension
description:
### Bug description

A format extension that ships a Word reference document and names it as `reference-doc: ref.docx` fails with `[Q-5-30] reference-doc: ref.docx does not exist`.
The file sits next to `_extension.yml`, and Quarto 1 finds it there.

The extension guide says that bundled files are "referenced with paths relative to the extension directory", and that this applies to `contributes: formats:` too.
q2 resolves `reference-doc` against the document directory instead, because the key is in neither list of bundled-file keys:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/extension/paths.rs#L65-L72

The metadata merge only adjusts values that are already tagged as paths, and the marking pass for `reference-doc` does not run for the extension layers:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/metadata_merge.rs#L74-L78

The value stays a plain string, and pandoc looks for `ref.docx` next to the document.
An extension that bundles a `reference-doc` for `docx` or `pptx` stops at the first render, while `theme`, `css` and the `include-*` keys from the same manifest resolve correctly.

### Steps to reproduce

`_extensions/demo/_extension.yml`:

```yaml
title: Demo
contributes:
  formats:
    docx:
      reference-doc: ref.docx
```

`_extensions/demo/ref.docx` is any valid Word document.

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format: demo-docx
---

Body.
```

With q2:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
```

With Quarto 1:

```sh
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with exit code 1:

```text
Error [Q-5-30]: `reference-doc: ref.docx` does not exist
The `reference-doc` entry names a file that does not exist, so pandoc cannot use it. Resolved relative to the file that declared it (or the project root, for a leading `/`).
ℹ Check the path in the `reference-doc` entry, or add the missing file.

1 error
```

Quarto 1 writes `index.docx`.

### Expected behavior

The render writes `index.docx` with the styles of `ref.docx`, as Quarto 1 does.
The `reference-doc` key could be treated like the other bundled-file keys, so it resolves against the directory of `_extension.yml`.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: A table caption sits below the table instead of above it
description: ### Bug description A table with a `{#tbl-a}` caption renders with the caption below the table. Quarto 1 puts table and listing captions above, and figure captions below: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/resources/filters/mainstateinit.lua#L34-L57 q2 falls back to `bottom` for every reference type, so a listing with `lst-cap` moves too. The table also carries the `caption-top` class, so the markup contradicts itself. Only the position differs; the number, label and cross-reference match. q2 reads `cap-location` and `tbl-cap-location` from the float attributes only. The comment says that the metadata setting lands with the cap-location feature, and indeed `tbl-cap-location: top` in the front matter has no effect: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/crossref_render.rs#L738-L744 The attribute form, `{#tbl-a tbl-cap-location="top"}`, gives the Quarto 1 result on q2 today. ### Steps to reproduce `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- format: html --- | A | |---| | 1 | : Caption. {#tbl-a} ``` Run q2 and Quarto 1 on it: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 puts the `figcaption` after the table, with the class `quarto-float-caption-bottom`: ```html ...

title: An unknown key under `meta` in `_brand.yml` stops the render with Q-14-1
description:
### Bug description

I found this with the documentation site of minato, whose `_brand.yml` sets `meta.license`:

https://github.com/mcanouil/minato/blob/fb6efda509e7764753dc50ae7a9e6265a333e263/docs/_brand.yml#L1-L3

Quarto 1 renders it.
q2 stops with `Q-14-1`, because its `meta` type accepts only `name` and `link` and rejects every other key:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs#L104-L115

The brand.yml spec allows other keys under `meta`:

https://github.com/posit-dev/brand-yml/blob/ffd9b0aec3ce75385abfb911907d2679479b9350/docs/brand/meta.qmd?plain=1#L19

q2 says the same in its metadata reader, which keeps "custom fields under `meta`, which the spec allows" as plain strings:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta_annotations.rs#L95-L101

The q2 brand guide also says that Quarto does nothing with `meta` values, so the hard error is on a value that q2 never reads:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/docs/guides/authoring/brand.qmd?plain=1#L834-L851

### Steps to reproduce

`_brand.yml`:

```yaml
meta:
  license: MIT
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
brand: _brand.yml
format: html
---
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with:

```text
Error [Q-14-1]: Invalid theme configuration
failed to parse _brand.yml: meta: unknown field `license`, expected `name` or `link` at line 2 column 3
```

Quarto 1 renders the page and prints `Output created: index.html`.

### Expected behavior

The render succeeds and ignores the key, as Quarto 1 does.
`BrandMeta` could keep unknown keys, for example with a `#[serde(flatten)]` map, in place of `deny_unknown_fields`.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: An attribute key with a colon is a parse error
description:
### Bug description

I found this with the quarto-prism extension.
It reads attributes keyed `format:name`, uses the one that matches the output format, and drops the others:

https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-prism/blob/60b60d4797d6b36a4c1261d7617574df70702a83/example.qmd#L35-L37

In q2, an attribute key with a colon, such as `html:style`, stops the qmd parser with a generic `Parse error`.
Quarto 1 accepts the key and keeps it on the element, because Pandoc allows `-`, `_`, `:` and `.` in a key:

https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/b913622e1ff87c69ab8b1a606577122e220925cd/src/Text/Pandoc/Readers/Markdown.hs#L655-L658

The q2 key token comes from the external scanner.
It reads letters, digits, `_`, `%`, `.` and `-`, and a `:` makes it return false, so no key token is produced:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/tree-sitter-qmd/tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c#L2655-L2664

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format: html
---

::: {html:style="color: red;"}
Text.
:::
```

Run q2 and Quarto 1 on it:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd --to html
quarto render index.qmd --to html
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with a parse error and exit code 1:

```text
Rendering single file: /private/tmp/q2-attr.AgEH/index.qmd
warning: profile-pass skipped /private/tmp/q2-attr.AgEH/index.qmd: Error: Parse error
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/q2-attr.AgEH/index.qmd:5:6 ]
   │
 5 │ ::: {html:style="color: red;"}
   │      ──┬─
   │        ╰─── unexpected character or token here
───╯

1 error
```

It writes no `index.html`.
The message does not say that the key is the problem.
Quarto 1.12.0 exits with 0 and writes `<div html:style="color: red;">`.

### Expected behavior

The div parses and the attribute keeps its name, as in Quarto 1.
A filter or an extension can then read `html:style`.
The scanner could accept `:` inside a key, as Pandoc does.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: `include-in-header` text warns about raw HTML
description:
### Bug description

`include-in-header: text:` takes raw HTML by definition.
q2 writes the tag into the head, but it also prints the warning Q-2-9, "HTML element converted to raw HTML".
Quarto 1 prints nothing.
`include-before-body` and `include-after-body` with `text:` warn the same way.

In front matter, q2 parses every untagged YAML string as markdown, so the tag goes through the HTML element path that emits Q-2-9:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs#L432-L443

q2 already keeps some machine-facing keys out of that default, such as `listing.contents` and `link-external-filter`.
The table asks for one entry per key whose misreading is an observed bug, and the three `text` slots have none:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta_annotations.rs#L89-L121

Tagging the value `!str` silences q2, but Quarto 1.12.0 then stops with `unknown tag !<!str>`, so one file cannot serve both.

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      text: '<meta name="x" content="1">'
---

Body.
```

Run q2 and Quarto 1 on it:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd --to html
quarto render index.qmd --to html
```

### Actual behavior

q2 prints a warning, exits with 0, and writes the tag into the page:

```text
Warning: [Q-2-9] HTML element converted to raw HTML
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/q2-hdr.qVh0/index.qmd:5:14 ]
   │
 5 │       text: '<meta name="x" content="1">'
   │              ─────────────┬─────────────
   │                           ╰─────────────── HTML element converted to raw HTML
───╯
ℹ This tag opens a line and names a block-level element, so it is passed through as a raw HTML block
ℹ To be explicit, put it in a ```{=html} block — or write a Quarto div instead: ::: {.your-class}

1 warning
```

Quarto 1.12.0 also writes the tag, and prints no warning.

### Expected behavior

No warning, as in Quarto 1.
The `text` value of `include-in-header`, `include-before-body` and `include-after-body` (also under `format.*`) could get a plain-string entry in the annotation table.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: `syntax-highlighting` is ignored for HTML output
description:
### Bug description

I found this with the atelier project type, which sets a light and a dark palette for every site built on it:

https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-atelier/blob/6018267750d18c15c43d3babad799abc2b63bdb9/_extensions/atelier/_extension.yml#L66-L68

Quarto 1 names the option `syntax-highlighting` and keeps `highlight-style` as a deprecated alias:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/resources/schema/document-code.yml#L153-L168

q2 reads `syntax-highlighting` for Typst only.
For HTML it reads `highlight-style` alone, so a document that follows the current Quarto 1 name gets the default palette.
Nothing warns, and the render exits 0.

The HTML theme parser reads the `highlight-style` key and nothing else:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs#L1106-L1109

The Typst filter reads `syntax-highlighting` first and falls back to `highlight-style`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/pandoc_filters/typst_highlight.rs#L125-L130

A Typst smoke test already calls `highlight-style` the deprecated alias, so the new name is the intended one:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/typst/syntax-highlighting/highlight-style-alias.qmd?plain=1#L11-L14

The HTML themes guide documents only `highlight-style`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/docs/guides/formats/html/themes.qmd?plain=1#L112-L123

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
format:
  html:
    syntax-highlighting: github
---

```r
x <- 1
```
````

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
grep -rl '#d73a49' index_files
quarto render index.qmd
grep -rl '#d73a49' index_files
```

### Actual behavior

With q2 the grep finds no file.
The GitHub keyword colour `#d73a49` never appears in the CSS, which uses the default palette.
With Quarto 1 the grep lists `index_files/libs/quarto-html/quarto-syntax-highlighting-<hash>.css`.
Renaming the key to `highlight-style` gives q2 the colour.

### Expected behavior

The `github` palette applies, as in Quarto 1.
Reading `syntax-highlighting` first and falling back to `highlight-style` in the HTML parser, as the Typst filter does, would match.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: hub-client: "Expand markup" and "Expand preview" should hide the other pane instead of shrinking it
description:
# Goal

In the editor's document header, "Expand markup" and "Expand preview" hide the other pane instead of shrinking it. "Split equally" is unchanged.

Today each expand button moves the pane divider to its drag limit, which leaves the other pane at 15% of the editing area's width. The markup pane is the source editor on the left. The preview pane is the rendered document on the right.

Done means:

- After "Expand markup", only the markup pane is on screen. After "Expand preview", only the preview pane is. Nothing of the other pane remains, divider included.
- "Split equally" brings both panes back at 50/50, and the pane that was hidden shows the current content.
- The button for the current layout shows as active.
- The editor's diagnostics (error markers in the markup pane) keep updating while the preview is hidden.
- Files with no preview pane (images, plain-text files such as `.yml` or `.css`) behave as today: the buttons stay disabled and the editor stays visible.

# Why

A shrunk pane is a narrow strip that only makes sense to someone who already knows what it is.

- "Expand preview" leaves the markup as a 15% column of squashed raw text next to the rendered document. A user who knows little Markdown and works in the preview, where paragraphs can be edited in place (WYSIWYG), reads that column as noise.
- "Expand markup" has the mirror problem: the rendered document is squeezed into a narrow 15% column.
- A hidden pane gives the chosen pane the whole width, and the screen shows what the button says.
- The header's fullscreen-preview action is not a substitute: it also hides the header and the sidebar.

The presets mirror the drag limits today (see the comment above `SPLIT_PRESETS`). This issue suggests letting the two expand buttons go past them, while a drag keeps its 15–85% limits.

# References

Code pointers (main at f4a3853):

- `hub-client/src/components/ViewToggleControl.tsx`: the three buttons; `SPLIT_PRESETS` 0.85 / 0.5 / 0.15.
- `hub-client/src/components/DocumentTopBar.tsx`: renders the buttons from `splitFraction`, `onSetSplit` and `splitDisabled`.
- `hub-client/src/components/Editor.tsx`: `editorPaneFraction`, `handleSetSplitPreset` (does not clamp), the drag handler (clamps to 0.15–0.85), each pane's `flex`, and the `.pane-divider`.
- `hub-client/src/components/Editor.css`: `.pane`, `.pane-divider`, `.split-animating`.

One possible approach, from reading the code (not tried in a browser):

- Have the expand buttons send 1 (markup only) or 0 (preview only) instead of 0.85 or 0.15. A drag cannot produce either value, so they can identify the collapsed state.
- Hide the collapsed pane and the divider, for example with CSS keyed on that state.
- Hide the preview rather than unmount it: `PreviewRouter` feeds the editor's diagnostics (`onDiagnosticsChange`).
- The `viewMode` modes (`'markup'` and `'preview'` in `ViewModeContext.tsx`, with the `.view-mode-*` rules in `Editor.css`) are no shortcut: nothing calls `setViewMode`, and those rules shrink the other pane to a strip of roughly 120–220 px instead of hiding it.

title: pampa: a literal `$` in prose gives the generic "Parse error" instead of Q-2-23, and the span points at the end of the paragraph
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a second batch of parsing reports; sibling: #947 (footnote diagnostic).

## Problem

A literal `$` in prose fails the page with the generic fallback diagnostic:

```
Error: Parse error
   ╭─[ d1.qmd:1:10 ]
 1 │ Costs $5.
   │          ┬
   │          ╰── unexpected character or token here
───╯
```

There is no Q code and no hint. `Q-2-23` (Unclosed Inline Math) exists for exactly this: its docs page names currency as the most common cause and gives `\$` as the fix. It is not emitted here even though the document has no earlier errors, so #230 (dedup swapping a specific code for the generic one) does not explain it.

Requiring `\$` is a deliberate q2 choice, but it is a large compatibility break for prose about prices, regular expressions, and shell syntax. Pandoc's `tex_math_dollars` only opens math when a non-space follows the `$` and a matching close exists, so all of the inputs below are literal text in Quarto 1. A specific diagnostic that points at the `$` and says how to escape it would make the break much easier to live with.

## Repro

Every one of these fails with the generic error (single-file `q2 render x.qmd --to html`):

```markdown
Costs $5.
A lone $ sign.
Anchor with ^ and $ to match.
Use $1 here.
Use ${1} here.
Costs $5 or $6.
Use $(R RHOME) here.
```

`Costs \$5.` and `The price is $x$ dollars.` render fine.

Two further observations from reproducing:

1. **Q-2-23 never fires, even for genuinely unclosed math.** `Open $x here and never close.` and `Open $x+y here.` also give the generic `Parse error`. Nothing under `crates/pampa/src` or `crates/quarto-parse-errors/src` references `Q-2-23`; it exists only in `crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/Q-2-23.json` (and the generated table) and `qmd-syntax-helper`. So the corpus entry apparently never matches the parser state the grammar actually ends up in.

2. **The span points at the end of the paragraph, not at the `$`.** In `Costs $5.` the caret sits after the final `.` (column 10). In a 218-character paragraph with `$HOME` near the start, the caret is at column 218. In a long generated line, such as a settings reference, that makes the offending `$` very hard to find.

## Expected

- A `$` that cannot be closed within the block should produce `Q-2-23` with the `math-start` note pointing at the `$` itself, plus the `\$` hint, for both the "currency in prose" case and the genuinely unclosed-math case.
- Ideally the corpus case should be extended so prefixes like `Costs ` and `Use ` are covered, since the current corpus content for Q-2-23 is just `$\n`.

## Pointers

- Fallback diagnostic: `crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs` around line 314 (`DiagnosticMessageBuilder::error("Parse error")`), reached when no entry in the generated corpus table matches.
- Corpus entry: `crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/Q-2-23.json`.
- Docs: `docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-23.qmd`.

cc @atheriel

title: Default and grid listings show categories and reading time that Quarto 1 leaves out
description:
### Bug description A `default` or `grid` listing without a `fields:` key shows two extra parts in q2. Each item gets a category chip row and a "1 min read" line. Quarto 1 draws neither for the same input, so a site that moves to q2 gets a different card layout without changing any listing option. The q2 design note means to copy the Quarto 1 defaults from `hydrateListing`, but its table lists eleven fields, adding `categories`, `filename`, `file-modified` and `reading-time`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/claude-notes/plans/2026-05-06-listings-L2-data-model.md?plain=1#L398-L407 The code follows that table: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/config.rs#L996-L1026 Quarto 1 has six fields for `default` and five for `grid`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/project/types/website/listing/website-listing-read.ts#L138-L152 It adds `categories` only when the listing sets `categories:`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/project/types/website/listing/website-listing-read.ts#L646-L654 A defaulted field is kept in q2 when at least one item carries it. Every document has a reading time, so the line always appears, and any item with categories gets its chips: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/binding.rs#L92-L110 ### Steps to reproduce `_quarto.yml`: ```yaml project: type: website ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- listing: contents: posts --- ``` `posts/a.qmd`: ```qmd --- title: A categories: [alpha] --- Text. ``` With q2: ```sh q2 render grep -c 'listing-reading-time"' _site/index.html grep -c 'class="listing-category"' _site/index.html ``` With Quarto 1: ```sh quarto render grep -c 'listing-reading-time"' _site/index.html grep -c 'class="listing-category"' _site/index.html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 prints a count of 2 for the reading time and 1 for the category, with this markup: ```html
alpha

1 min read

``` Quarto 1 prints 0 for both. ### Expected behavior The item shows the title and description, as in Quarto 1. Categories appear when the author sets `categories: true` on the listing or lists `categories` in `fields:`. Reading time appears only when `fields:` names it. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `knitr: opts_chunk:` in the front matter is ignored
description:
### Bug description Quarto 1 passes the `knitr:` map of the front matter to knitr, so `knitr: opts_chunk: comment: "#>"` changes the prefix of every R output line. q2 ships the R script that reads this map, but the Rust side never gives it the `knitr:` metadata, so the option is dropped without a warning. The R script merges `format$metadata$knitr$opts_chunk` and `opts_knit` into the knitr options: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/resources/rmd/execute.R#L363-L373 `build_format_config` builds the config from the format and the `execute:` scope only. Nothing fills `metadata` from the document, so `is.list(format$metadata$knitr)` is false in R: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/mod.rs#L317-L323 Related: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1001 ### Steps to reproduce `index.qmd`: ````qmd --- knitr: opts_chunk: comment: "#>" --- ```{r} 1 + 1 ``` ```` With q2: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html ``` With Quarto 1: ```sh quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior The output block of `index.html` from q2: ```html 
[1] 2
``` ### Expected behavior The output block holds `#> [1] 2`, as Quarto 1 writes it (`#> [1] 2` in the HTML source). ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `pandoc.utils.stringify` turns a soft break and a line break into a newline
description:
### Bug description `pandoc.utils.stringify` writes a newline for `SoftBreak` and for `LineBreak` in q2. Quarto 1 writes a space for both. A paragraph that the author wrapped over two lines gives `first\nsecond` in q2 and `first second` in Quarto 1. Filters that put the result in an attribute, a file name, a hash or a one-line label see the newline. `pandoc.utils.stringify` calls the private helper `stringify_inline`, which maps both break inlines to `"\n"`, and `Space` to a space: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/utils.rs#L894-L896 I found no sign that the newline is intended. The Lua filter guide lists where q2 differs from Pandoc on purpose (environment variables, working directory, locale), and `stringify` is not among them. If the newline is a deliberate change, a note in that list would help filter authors. ### Steps to reproduce `filter.lua`: ```lua function Pandoc() local text = pandoc.utils.stringify(pandoc.Para({pandoc.Str("a"), pandoc.SoftBreak(), pandoc.Str("b")})) return pandoc.Pandoc(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str((text:gsub("\n", "\\n"))))) end ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- filters: - filter.lua --- x ``` Render it with q2 and with Quarto 1: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 writes the newline, which the filter shows as `\n`: ```text

a\nb

``` ### Expected behavior A space, as in Quarto 1: ```text

a b

``` ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `pandoc.utils.type` returns the element tag, not `Block` or `Inline`
description:
### Bug description `pandoc.utils.type` returns the concrete tag of an element in q2, such as `Para` or `Str`. Quarto 1 returns the class of the element: `Block` for every block and `Inline` for every inline. For an `Attr` value, q2 returns `LuaAttr`, which is the name of an internal Rust type. A filter that tests `pandoc.utils.type(x) == "Block"` or `== "Inline"` never matches in q2. `quarto.utils.type` is an alias, so it has the same result. The tag looks like a deliberate choice: the doc comment and the unit tests of the function expect `Para` and `Str`. But Pandoc documents `type` as the `__name` metafield, which is `Block` or `Inline` for elements, and the tag is already available as `elem.t` and `elem.tag` in both engines. `userdata_type_name` returns the tag for every `Inline` and `Block`, through `get_inline_type_name` and `get_block_type_name`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/utils.rs#L360-L394 An `Attr` has no case there, so the function falls back to the `__name` of its metatable, which is the Rust name: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/utils.rs#L326-L355 ### Steps to reproduce `filter.lua`: ```lua function Pandoc() return pandoc.Pandoc(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str(pandoc.utils.type(pandoc.Para({}))))) end ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- filters: - filter.lua --- x ``` Render it with q2 and with Quarto 1: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 writes the tag of the element: ```text

Para

``` For an inline, it writes `Str`, and for an `Attr`, it writes `LuaAttr`. ### Expected behavior The class of the element, as in Quarto 1: ```text

Block

``` An inline gives `Inline`, and an `Attr` gives `Attr`. If q2 keeps the tag on purpose, the Lua filter guide could list it with the other differences from Pandoc, and an `Attr` should still not report the Rust type name. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `quarto.project` paths are `nil` when a single file is rendered
description:
### Bug description In a single file render (no `_quarto.yml`), `quarto.project.directory`, `quarto.project.offset` and `quarto.project.output_directory` are `nil` in q2. Quarto 1 treats the directory of the document as the project, so the three values are strings. A filter that joins `quarto.project.directory` with a file name fails with `attempt to concatenate a nil value` when a user renders one document. The same filter works in a project render in q2. The host builds the Lua project table from `host_project`, which returns `None` when the render has no project. Its comment says that `quarto.project.directory` is nil outside a project in Quarto 1: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/lmd/dialect.rs#L123-L132 With `None`, the Lua table gets no `directory`, `offset` or `output_directory`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/host_context.rs#L88-L96 Quarto 1 does not do that. Without a project, `quarto render` falls back to a single file context, whose directory is the directory of the document, and exports it as `QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/command/render/render-shared.ts#L68-L77 `quarto.project.directory` reads that variable: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b9245f90c951fa2517f1a3c99920dc80fe90955f/src/resources/pandoc/datadir/init.lua#L607-L609 Related: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/939 ### Steps to reproduce There is no `_quarto.yml` in the directory. `filter.lua`: ```lua function Pandoc() return pandoc.Pandoc(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str(tostring(quarto.project.directory)))) end ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- filters: - filter.lua --- x ``` Render it with q2 and with Quarto 1: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 writes `nil` into the page: ```text

nil

``` `quarto.project.offset` and `quarto.project.output_directory` are `nil` too. ### Expected behavior Quarto 1 writes the directory of the document: ```text

/private/tmp/q2-proj.0O9g

``` `quarto.project.offset` is `.`, and `quarto.project.output_directory` is the directory of the document too. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `pandoc.utils.stringify` returns an empty string for a `Pandoc` document or a `Meta` table
description:
### Bug description `pandoc.utils.stringify` gives `""` when it receives a `Pandoc` document or a `Meta` table. Quarto 1 returns the plain text of the whole document, or of every value in the metadata. Filters that stringify `doc` or `doc.meta` to build a summary, a hash or a search index get no text in q2. Stringifying `doc.blocks`, one block, or one metadata value works. `stringify_value` handles both as plain Lua tables. The table branch reads only the array part, and a document (`blocks`, `meta`) or a metadata map has no array items, so the loop adds nothing: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/utils.rs#L843-L851 The doc comment of the function says that it mirrors Pandoc, which accepts a `Pandoc` and a `Meta`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/utils.rs#L795-L803 ### Steps to reproduce `filter.lua`: ```lua function Pandoc() local text = pandoc.utils.stringify(pandoc.Pandoc({pandoc.Para({pandoc.Str("built")})})) return pandoc.Pandoc(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str("[" .. text .. "]"))) end ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- filters: - filter.lua --- x ``` Render it with q2 and with Quarto 1: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 writes an empty string between the brackets: ```text

[]

``` The same happens for a `Meta` table. ### Expected behavior The text of the document, as in Quarto 1: ```text

[built]

``` A `Meta` table gives the text of its values. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `pandoc.system.os` is `macos` on macOS, where Pandoc gives `darwin`
description:
### Bug description `pandoc.system.os` holds the string that Rust names the operating system. On macOS that is `macos`. Pandoc takes the value from Haskell, which names the same system `darwin`. A filter that branches on `pandoc.system.os == "darwin"` takes the wrong path in q2, for example to choose `open` or `xdg-open`, or a path separator. I found this in an extension that runs the `_quarto.tests.run` checks from Lua. Its `current_os` helper accepts `darwin`, `linux`, `mingw32` and `windows`, so under q2 on macOS it returns `unknown`, and a test limited to `os: [darwin]` is skipped: https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-extension-test/blob/e727a66b5f7e9617c9160e676a33edc6f7944cea/_extensions/extension-test/_modules/frontmatter.lua#L189-L200 (work in progress framework to allow Quarto extensions testing. I did not find anyone using the system OS from Lua so far) q2 itself names macOS `darwin` for these rules: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-test/src/spec.rs#L565-L576 Pandoc documents the values as `darwin` (macOS), `freebsd`, `linux`, `linux-android`, `mingw32` (Windows), `netbsd` and `openbsd`: https://pandoc.org/lua-filters.html#pandoc.system.os Rust gives the same names except for three: `macos`, `windows` and `android`. I ran this on macOS only. The native runtime returns `std::env::consts::OS`, which is `macos` on macOS: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-system-runtime/src/native.rs#L422-L424 ### Steps to reproduce `filter.lua`: ```lua function Pandoc() return pandoc.Pandoc(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str(pandoc.system.os))) end ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- filters: - filter.lua --- x ``` Render it with q2 and with Quarto 1: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior On macOS, q2 writes `macos`: ```text

macos

``` ### Expected behavior On macOS, the page should hold `darwin`, which is what Pandoc gives and what Quarto 1 writes: ```text

darwin

``` A small map from the Rust name to the Pandoc name (`macos` to `darwin`, `windows` to `mingw32`, `android` to `linux-android`) would give the documented values. If q2 keeps the Rust names on purpose, the Lua filter guide could list this with the other differences from Pandoc. ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: A Typst project render cannot find the bibliography file in `output-dir`
description:
### Bug description

In a project with `output-dir: _site`, a Typst document with `bibliography: references.bib` and `citeproc: false` fails on q2, and Quarto 1 renders it.
The generated `_site/index.typ` contains `#bibliography(("references.bib"))`, but q2 never copies `references.bib` into `_site`, so `typst compile` cannot open it.

q2 already flushes the collected resource copies before the Typst compile step, which fixed the same failure for images:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/pipeline.rs#L803-L813

The collector that builds those copies walks the document AST for image targets.
A `bibliography:` value sits in the metadata, so no copy is queued for it:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/resource_collector.rs#L466-L478

With `citeproc: true` the failure does not appear, because q2 resolves the citations itself and no `#bibliography` call is written.
The cause is my reading of the source.
The run confirms the missing file, and I have not checked that a queued copy fixes it.

### Steps to reproduce

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  output-dir: _site
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
format: typst
bibliography: references.bib
citeproc: false
---

[@a]
```

`references.bib`:

```bibtex
@book{a, title={A}, author={B}, year={2000}}
```

With q2:

```sh
q2 render
```

With Quarto 1:

```sh
quarto render
```

### Actual behavior

q2 fails and leaves only `_site/index.typ`:

```text
Error [Q-21-3]: typst compile exited with exit status: 1:
error: file not found (searched at /private/tmp/q2-typst.AqB0/_site/references.bib)
    ┌─ _site/index.typ:438:14
    │
438 │ #bibliography(("references.bib"))
    │               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

Quarto 1 writes `_site/index.pdf`.

### Expected behavior

q2 copies `references.bib` next to `_site/index.typ` before it compiles, so `_site/index.pdf` is written, as in Quarto 1.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9).
- Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: The `debug` library is not available in Lua filters
description:
### Bug description The global `debug` is `nil` in a Lua filter, so a call to `debug.getinfo` stops the render. Extensions use this call to find the directory of the module that is running. For example, a `load_sibling` helper that several of my extensions vendor reads `debug.getinfo(1, "S").source`, then loads a neighbouring file with `require`. Three of the 40 extensions (all mine) I tested call `debug.getinfo` in their Lua files. Quarto 1 runs Lua through Pandoc, which exposes the full `debug` library. This is the Quarto 1 way of doing it, and a better way might be worth exploring in q2. Both engines already cover the common cases without `debug`, which I checked on q2 and on Quarto 1.12.0: - A relative `require("./b")` in a nested module loads the neighbouring `b.lua`. - `PANDOC_SCRIPT_FILE` gives the path of the filter script. - `quarto.utils.resolve_path` resolves a path against the filter directory. None of them gives a module its own path, and extensions that call `debug.getinfo` break today. The filter environment uses `Lua::new()`, which skips `debug` as unsafe, although the comment says native builds load everything: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs#L177-L192 The chunk name of the filter script is set without a leading `@`, so once `debug` is loaded, `source:sub(2)` would still drop the first character of the path: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs#L383-L386 ### Steps to reproduce `filter.lua`: ```lua function Pandoc() return pandoc.Pandoc(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str(debug.getinfo(1, "S").source))) end ``` `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- filters: - filter.lua --- x ``` Render it with q2 and with Quarto 1: ```sh q2 render index.qmd --to html quarto render index.qmd --to html ``` ### Actual behavior ```text Rendering single file: /private/tmp/q2-debug.Eqp8/index.qmd error: while rendering /private/tmp/q2-debug.Eqp8/index.qmd Error: Lua filter error: runtime error: [string "/private/tmp/q2-debug.Eqp8/filter.lua"]:2: attempt to index a nil value (global 'debug') stack traceback: [string "/private/tmp/q2-debug.Eqp8/filter.lua"]:2: in function 'Pandoc' 1 error ``` ### Expected behavior `debug.getinfo(1, "S").source` returns the path of the running chunk with a leading `@`, as in standard Lua. Quarto 1 writes it into the page: ```text

@filter.lua

``` ### Your environment - q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from a2a1cb9). - Quarto 1 for comparison: 1.12.0 (pre-release). - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `q2 add owner/repo@<sha>` fails for a commit SHA
description:
### Bug description

`q2 add` accepts `<gh-org>/<gh-repo>[/<subdir>][@<ref>]`, the URL of a `.zip` or `.tar.gz` archive, or a local archive or folder.
The `@<ref>` can be a tag or a branch, but not a commit.

For `@<ref>`, `parse_github` tries `archive/refs/tags/<ref>` and then `archive/refs/heads/<ref>`, and GitHub answers 404 to both when the ref is a commit SHA:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a2a1cb948b1aec42c93200b880dc73567160f691/crates/quarto-source-fetch/src/target.rs#L161-L173

GitHub serves a commit at `archive/<sha>.tar.gz`, with the full or the short SHA, so the archive exists.
Pinning a commit helps with an extension that has no releases, or when you want to try a fix before it's released.
Quarto 1 has the same gap.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir q2-sha && cd q2-sha
q2 add quarto-ext/fontawesome@6b520912a7b26a72e1b0826f6b201c2e69b2b3c7 --trust --no-prompt
q2 add quarto-ext/fontawesome@6b52091 --trust --no-prompt
```

For comparison, a tag and the full archive URL both install:

```sh
q2 add quarto-ext/fontawesome@v1.2.0 --trust --no-prompt
q2 add https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome/archive/6b52091.tar.gz --trust --no-prompt
```

### Actual behavior

```text
Error: Could not get an extension from quarto-ext/fontawesome@6b520912a7b26a72e1b0826f6b201c2e69b2b3c7
