could not download quarto-ext/fontawesome@6b520912a7b26a72e1b0826f6b201c2e69b2b3c7 on GitHub: tried 2 location(s): https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome/archive/refs/tags/6b520912a7b26a72e1b0826f6b201c2e69b2b3c7.tar.gz → HTTP 404; https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome/archive/refs/heads/6b520912a7b26a72e1b0826f6b201c2e69b2b3c7.tar.gz → HTTP 404
```

The short SHA fails the same way.
The URL form works, but `.quarto-source.yml` then records `kind: url` and the URL, not the repository and the commit.

### Expected behavior

The extension installs at that commit.
One way would be to add `archive/<ref>.tar.gz` as a third candidate after tags and heads.
The fetch loop already moves on after a non-2xx status, so a tag or a branch with the same name still wins.

### Your environment

- q2: `Q2 (quarto 2) 0.40.0-nightly.20261101` (nightly built from `a2a1cb9`).
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: hub-client: emoji reactions on paragraphs and comments
description:
### Summary

Add emoji reactions to paragraphs and comments.

### Request

Let me react to a paragraph or a comment with an emoji (thumbs up, checkmark, etc.), similar to reactions in GitHub or Google Docs.

### Impact

A lot of review feedback is just "agree", "done", or "seen". Today the only way to say that is a full reply, which makes threads longer and harder to scan. In one of our reviews, a reply literally read ":thumbsup: (sure wish we had emojis here lol)".

Reactions would also let an author see at a glance which points have agreement, without reading every reply.

### Related

- #893 covers `:emoji:` shortcodes in rendered text. This request is about reactions on content and comments.

title: hub-client: keep resolved comments visible
description:
### Summary

Resolving a comment (the checkmark) removes it entirely. Other collaborators can't see the comment, its replies, or that it was resolved.

### Request

Keep resolved comments visible in a de-emphasized state, for example collapsed or grayed out, with a way to expand and reopen them.

### Impact

In a review, the author resolves comments as they address them. Once a comment disappears, the reviewer can't confirm their point was handled or see how it was answered, and the discussion is lost for anyone reading the doc later.

### Related

- #642 (resolving leaves a visual halo in the block editor)
- #953 (undoing a resolve should be trivial). Visible resolved comments would make undo straightforward.

title: hub-client: @mention people in comments and text
description:
### Summary

Support @mentions in comments and in document text.

### Request

Typing `@` in a comment (or in the text) should let me pick a collaborator, and that person should be notified that they were mentioned.

### Impact

With several reviewers on a document, a question is often meant for one specific person. Right now I have to ping them separately in another tool and paste a link, which pulls the conversation out of the document.

### Related

- #980 (notifications) is needed for mentions to reach the person.

title: hub-client: notify me about new comments and replies
description:
### Summary

Notify me about new comments and replies. Today I only find out by opening the document.

### Request

Send notifications for:

- New comments on documents I own or have edited
- Replies to my comments
- Mentions, if #975 lands

In-app notifications would help; email would be even better, since I don't keep Quarto Hub open all day.

### Impact

Without notifications, a comment can sit unseen until the other person happens to open the document. To get a timely response, I currently have to follow up in another tool, which defeats the purpose of commenting in the doc.

title: hub-client: summary of changes since I last viewed a document or project
description:
### Summary

Show what changed in a document or project since I last viewed it.

### Request

When I open a document or project, offer a summary of changes since my last visit: which sections changed, who changed them, and which comments are new. Highlighting changed blocks in the document would work too.

### Impact

Reviewers usually come back after the author has addressed their comments. Without a summary, they have to re-read the whole document or step through Replay to find what changed, so a second review takes as long as the first, and changes are easy to miss.

title: hub-client: show custom front-matter fields, like `reviewers`, in the header
description:
### Summary

Only built-in front-matter fields show in the document header. Custom fields, like `reviewers`, don't.

### Request

Show custom front-matter fields in the header, or provide a way to choose which extra fields to display (for example a `header-fields` option).

### Impact

I use Quarto Hub for design reviews, and each doc lists its reviewers. Since custom fields don't show, I've been putting reviewers in `description`, which mixes two kinds of information and makes the description harder to use for its actual purpose.

title: Incremental writer drops a backslash hard break's newline when a sibling word is edited
description:
## Reproduction

At tag `v0.37.0` (and on `main` at `a37801fe4`), parse this QMD with `pampa::wasm_entry_points::qmd_to_pandoc`:

```
Last line\
next line.
```

(a backslash at the end of the first line, followed by a real newline). Append `Z` to the paragraph's first `Str` ("Last" -> "LastZ"), leaving the hard break untouched, then compute `quarto_ast_reconcile::compute_reconciliation(&original, &edited)` and call `pampa::writers::incremental::incremental_write`.

Output: `LastZ line\next line.\n` — read carefully, this is the six bytes `\`, `n`, `e`, `x`, `t` with **no** newline character between the backslash and `next`; the real newline that followed the backslash in the source is gone. The hard break becomes a literal backslash immediately followed by the text `next`, which changes the document (a reader parses `\n` there as an escape, not as `\` + a line break).

## Observed vs expected

Observed: the newline after the backslash is dropped.

Expected: `LastZ line\` + an actual newline + `next line.\n` — only `Last` changes to `LastZ`.

## Cause

Confirmed by inspecting the reconciliation plan and the inlines' resolved source spans directly.

q2's tree-sitter grammar parses a backslash hard break as two adjacent inlines: a `LineBreak` holding just the backslash, immediately followed by a `SoftBreak` holding the newline that follows it. By the time `compute_reconciliation` runs, though, the `SoftBreak` is already gone: a postprocessing pass in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs` (the "Step 0" hard-break cleanup in the combined inline filter) deletes any `SoftBreak` that immediately follows a `LineBreak`, to match Pandoc's own AST shape (Pandoc emits a single `LineBreak` for this construct, never a `LineBreak` + `SoftBreak` pair).

That cleanup drops the `SoftBreak` node but not its ownership of the newline byte: the remaining `LineBreak`'s `source_info` still only covers the backslash. So after postprocessing, the paragraph's inline list has a gap — the newline byte between the `LineBreak`'s span and whatever comes after it is not covered by any inline's source span at all.

This is invisible on an unedited document, because an unchanged block is copied verbatim as one single byte range (the block's own source span, not a concatenation of its inlines' spans). It only surfaces when some other inline in the same block is edited: `assemble_inline_content`'s `KeepBefore` arm (`crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs`) then reconstructs the block by copying each kept inline's own source span and concatenating them directly, with no gap-filling in between — an assumption that holds for every other inline in the paragraph (their spans really are contiguous) but not for the `LineBreak` left behind by the Step 0 cleanup.

## Fix

Fold the removed `SoftBreak`'s span into the kept `LineBreak`'s via `SourceInfo::combine` before discarding the node, the same way `merge_strs` elsewhere in `postprocess.rs` folds a merged-away `Str`'s span into the `Str` it merges into. The `LineBreak`'s `source_info` becomes a `Concat` of two contiguous `Original` pieces (the backslash, then the newline), whose `preimage_in` hull is the full two-byte range — closing the gap at its source, rather than teaching every span-concatenating consumer to fill gaps it shouldn't have to know about.

## Reproduction harness

```rust
let original_qmd = "Last line\\\nnext line.\n";
let original_ast = parse_qmd(original_qmd); // pampa::readers::qmd::read, keep_source_info = true
let mut edited = original_ast.clone();
// edited.blocks[0] (Paragraph).content[0] (Str "Last") -> push 'Z'
let plan = quarto_ast_reconcile::compute_reconciliation(&original_ast, &edited);
let result = pampa::writers::incremental::incremental_write(original_qmd, &original_ast, &edited, &plan).unwrap();
assert_eq!(result, "LastZ line\\\nnext line.\n"); // fails
```

title: hub-client: pressing Enter on a comment does nothing when Edit is off
description:
### Summary

With the Edit toggle off, the comment box still accepts text, but pressing Enter doesn't post the comment. There's no error or hint, so the comment is silently lost.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Turn off **Edit** (bottom right).
2. Select some text and add a comment.
3. Type a comment and press Enter.

**Expected:** The comment posts, or the comment option isn't offered while Edit is off.
**Actual:** Nothing happens. The text stays in the box and is never saved.

### Request

Either allow commenting while Edit is off (commenting without editing seems like a useful mode for reviewers), or hide the comment affordance in that mode so it's clear it isn't available.

### Impact

Anyone reviewing with Edit off can type out feedback and lose it without knowing. They may also assume it posted, so the author never sees it.

title: q2 mcp: can't upload a full-size screenshot because images go through the conversation as base64
description:
### Summary

The `q2 mcp` tools can't upload a full-size screenshot, because the image has to pass through the conversation as base64 text.

### Request

Add a way to upload a file without routing its contents through the conversation, for example a tool that takes a local file path (or a URL) and uploads it directly to the project.

### Impact

I use Claude with `q2 mcp` to write design and feedback docs, and those docs need screenshots. A normal screenshot is too large to send as base64, so today I rely on a separate upload script outside the MCP tools. Without it, Claude can only add small or downscaled images.

title: hub-client: links to `.html` files and `<iframe>`s don't work in the preview
description:
### Summary

Links to `.html` files and `<iframe>` elements that point at project files don't work in the preview, because the hub doesn't serve the project's HTML files.

### Request

Serve the project's HTML files so they can be linked to and embedded from documents.

### Impact

A simple way to share an interactive prototype is to keep a standalone `prototype.html` in the project and link to it from the design doc. Today that link goes nowhere, so reviewers can't open the prototype from the doc.

### Related

- #985 (scripts in raw HTML blocks)
- #881 (link validation doesn't check `.html` targets)

title: hub-client: share one document read-only, and see and limit who has access to a project
description:
### Summary

A share link to a single file opens the whole project with edit access, and there's no way to see who can sign in with it.

### Request

- Share a single document read-only.
- See who has access to a project.
- Remove someone's access.

### Impact

When I want one person to review one document, the share link gives them edit access to every file in the project. Since I can't see or revoke access, I don't know who can change my files, which makes me hesitant to share at all.

### Related

- #37 (clean up share flow)

title: Incremental writer drops an editorial mark's explicit attribute when a sibling word is edited
description:
## Reproduction

At tag `v0.37.0` (and on `main` at `a37801fe4`), parse this QMD with `pampa::wasm_entry_points::qmd_to_pandoc`:

```
Last [++ added]{author="Bob"} text.
```

Append `Z` to the paragraph's first `Str` ("Last" -> "LastZ"), leaving the `Insert` node untouched, then compute `quarto_ast_reconcile::compute_reconciliation(&original, &edited)` and call `pampa::writers::incremental::incremental_write`.

Output: `LastZ [++ added] text.\n` — the `{author="Bob"}` attribute is gone.

The same thing happens with `author` and `date` together, and with other attributes on `[-- ]` (Delete), `[!! ]` (Highlight) and `[>> ]` (EditComment) marks.

## Observed vs expected

Observed: the editorial mark's attribute is silently dropped even though the mark itself was not edited.

Expected: only `Last` changes to `LastZ`; `[++ added]{author="Bob"}` is preserved exactly.

## Cause

`extract_delimiter_space_info` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/text_helpers.rs` computes the `Insert`/`Delete`/`Highlight`/`EditComment` node's own source span (`adjusted_range`) from the opening and closing *delimiter* tokens only — specifically `last_delimiter_range.end` minus any trailing whitespace trimmed from inside the closing delimiter. It never considers that the node's actual grammar span (`node_location(node)`, passed in as `fallback_range`) extends past the closing delimiter when an explicit attribute follows it (`]{author="Bob"}`).

So the `Insert` node's recorded span covers only `[++ added]`, not the trailing `{author="Bob"}`. `write_insert`/`write_delete`/etc. in `crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs` write the attribute correctly when the node is freshly re-serialized (the `attr` field is still populated), but the incremental writer's job is precisely to *avoid* re-serializing nodes that didn't change — it copies the node's own source span verbatim instead (either as a block-level `KeepBefore` or, as in this repro, as an inline-level `KeepBefore` inside `assemble_inline_content` when a sibling inline was edited but the mark itself was not). Because that span stops before the attribute, the copy drops it.

## Suggested fix

In `extract_delimiter_space_info`, when the full node's end (`fallback_range.end`) extends past the closing delimiter's end, use the node's true end instead of `last_delimiter_range.end - trailing_ws_count` for `adjusted_range.end`. The two concerns are independent: trailing whitespace trimming only ever applies to bytes inside the closing delimiter token itself, strictly before any attribute that might follow it.

title: hub-client: `<script>` and hover handlers in `{=html}` blocks don't run in the preview
description:
### Summary

In the preview, `<script>` tags and hover handlers inside a `{=html}` block don't run. Only inline `onclick` handlers work.

### Request

Let scripts in raw HTML blocks run in the preview, or, if that isn't safe, offer a supported way to embed an interactive prototype (for example a sandboxed iframe).

### Impact

I write design docs that compare small UI prototypes, such as two variants of a picker. Reviewers need to hover and click through them to give useful feedback. Without scripts, I'm limited to static screenshots, and the most useful part of the review happens outside the doc.

### Related

- #43 (raw HTML safety, subsumed by #167)
- #986 (serving project HTML files, another way to share a prototype)

title: hub-client: `.lightbox` images don't open full size in the preview
description:
### Summary

Images with `.lightbox` don't open full size when clicked in the preview.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add an image with the lightbox class:

   ```markdown
   ![Prototype screenshot](prototype.png){.lightbox}
   ```

2. Click the image in the preview.

**Expected:** The image opens full size, as in Quarto HTML output.
**Actual:** Nothing happens.

### Request

Support `.lightbox` in the preview. If that's not planned, it would help if the Quarto 2 Figures guide (which documents `.lightbox` for HTML output) noted that the preview doesn't support it.

### Impact

My design docs are full of UI screenshots, and at the preview's column width the details are too small to read. Lightbox is the standard fix, so without it reviewers can't see what they're commenting on.

title: hub-client: replying to a comment left cut-off copies of nearby lines and broke the render
description:
### Summary

While I added a short reply to a comment, the editor inserted truncated copies of nearby lines in three places. I was the only person editing, and one of the stray lines broke rendering for the whole document.

### What happened

- A bullet was duplicated as a cut-off line.
- The heading "Code: where the changes go" was reduced to just "go".
- Three truncated copies of one sentence appeared.

The truncated bullet contained an unclosed `**`, so the document failed to render. File history shows the stray lines in my own edits, so they didn't come from another collaborator.

### Steps to reproduce

I don't have reliable repro steps. It happened while replying to an existing comment in a long document.

### Impact

The editor changed text I never touched, without any visible sign. I only noticed because the render failed. If the stray text had been valid markdown, it could easily have gone unnoticed and been shared with reviewers.

### Related

Possibly related to the incremental writer issues: #963, #964, #965.

title: hub-client: make file path links clickable in the editor
description:
### Summary

Links to other project files are clickable in the viewer, but not in the editor.

### Request

Let me follow a file link from the editor. A modifier click (for example Cmd/Ctrl+click, as in VS Code) is fine if a plain click needs to stay for placing the cursor.

### Impact

I spend most of my time in the editor. To follow a link today, I have to find it in the preview or browse to the file in the navigator, which slows down work on sets of linked documents (for example a design doc and its notes).

### Related

- #891 (preview links are no longer clickable)

title: hub-client: highlight an author's whole stretch of text on hover, by default
description:
### Summary

Hovering over text should highlight the full span written by that author, on by default.

### Request

When I hover over text, highlight the contiguous stretch written by the same author (and ideally show who it is). This should work without turning on authorship for the whole document.

### Impact

Turning on authorship colors the entire page, which makes the text harder to read. Most of the time I only want to know who wrote one paragraph, for example so I can ask them about it. A hover answers that in place and keeps the page clean otherwise.

### Related

- #115 / #190 added attribution in the Replay view. This request is for the normal editing view.

title: hub-client: show author initials, not only a color
description:
### Summary

Show author initials, not only a color, wherever authorship is displayed.

### Request

Pair each author's color with their initials in a small badge or avatar, in the text attribution view, on comments, and in the Authors list.

### Impact

Today I have to match a color against the Authors list to know who wrote something. With three or more collaborators, colors get hard to tell apart and remember, and color alone doesn't work for people with color vision deficiencies. Initials make attribution readable at a glance.

### Related

- Show who wrote each comment by default (separate issue, coming soon)

title: pampa: plural possessive apostrophes (`Dogs' toys`) are reported as Q-2-10 and fail the render
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a larger report; see #939 for the full list of siblings. ## Problem A plural possessive (`Dogs' toys`) is an apostrophe followed by a space. The inline parser reads it as a closing single quote, finds no opener, and reports `[Q-2-10] Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote`. The document then fails to render. Pandoc renders the same input as `

Dogs’ toys and cats’ toys.

`. The Connect docs hit this about 20 times, in ordinary prose such as "users' and groups' DNs". Escaping (`groups\'`) or typing `’` works around it, but neither should be needed for standard English. ## Repro ```markdown Dogs' toys and cats' toys. ``` ``` $ q2 render a.qmd --to html Error: [Q-2-10] Closed Quote Without Matching Open Quote ╭─[ a.qmd:1:6 ] 1 │ Dogs' toys and cats' toys. │ ┬┬ │ ╰──── No opening quote was found before this mark. If you meant an apostrophe, escape it with a backslash. │ │ │ ╰── A space is causing a quote mark to be interpreted as a quotation close. ... 2 errors $ echo $? 1 ``` My results on 0.36.0 differ slightly from the original report, which said a single possessive in a paragraph passes. Here every case fails, including the single one: | Input | Result | |---|---| | `Cats' toys.` | Q-2-10 | | `Dogs' toys and cats' toys.` | Q-2-10 ×2 | | Two possessives across a soft line break | Q-2-10 ×2 | | Two possessives in separate paragraphs | Q-2-10 ×2 | | `- Dogs' toys.` / `- Cats' toys.` as list items | Q-2-10 ×1 (first item only) | | `It's the cats' toys.` | Q-2-10 | | `Cats'` at end of block | OK | | `Dogs\' toys and cats\' toys.` | OK, renders `Dogs’ toys and cats’ toys.` | The list-item case reporting only the first item suggests error recovery drops the second diagnostic rather than that the second item parses; see also #230 and #232. ## Expected An apostrophe directly after a word character and followed by whitespace or punctuation, with no open single quote pending in the block, should be read as an apostrophe (right single quotation mark), as pandoc does. The `Q-2-10` doc page (`docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-10.qmd`) already describes contractions and possessives as the most common false positive, so this is a known sharp edge, but plural possessives are too common in prose to require escaping. Related: #221 (apostrophe after a code span trips Q-2-7). cc @atheriel

title: Incremental writer emits LF for a rewritten block or separator in a CRLF document
description:
## Reproduction

At tag `v0.37.0` (and on `main` at `a37801fe4`), on a CRLF (`\r\n`) document, make an edit that forces the incremental writer to rewrite a block from scratch rather than copy or splice it (for example, appending a brand-new paragraph with no original counterpart, or editing a paragraph in a way the inline-splice safety check rejects). Compute `quarto_ast_reconcile::compute_reconciliation(&original, &edited)` and call `pampa::writers::incremental::incremental_write`.

Minimal shape:

```
First paragraph.\r\n\r\nLast paragraph.\r\n
```

(all `\r\n`). After an edit that forces a block-level rewrite, the rewritten block and the separator immediately around it come out with `\n` instead of `\r\n`, while the rest of the file keeps `\r\n`.

A simpler case — editing a word in place inside a CRLF paragraph, where the result is handled by inline splicing rather than a full block rewrite — keeps `\r\n` correctly, because splicing copies bytes from the original rather than writing fresh text.

## Observed vs expected

Observed: a rewritten block, and the separators the incremental writer has to synthesize around it (rather than copy from the original gap), use bare `\n`, producing a document with mixed line endings.

Expected: a rewritten block and its separators use the same line-ending convention as the rest of the document.

## Cause

The standard QMD writer (`crates/pampa/src/writers/qmd.rs`) always emits bare `\n` — reasonably so, since most callers want platform-independent output. The incremental writer calls that standard writer whenever it has to rewrite a block from scratch (`write_block_to_string` in `crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs`), and falls back to a literal `"\n"` separator in `compute_separator` whenever it can't copy the original gap verbatim (one of the two adjacent entries is a rewrite). Neither function looks at the original document's line-ending convention.

## Suggested fix

Detect the document's line-ending convention once from `original_qmd` (e.g. "does it contain `\r\n`"), and when a block must be rewritten or a separator must be synthesized, convert/emit `\r\n` instead of `\n` in that case. The standard writer itself does not need to change — only the incremental writer's own freshly-generated text.

title: Incremental QMD writer drops bytes outside the first-to-last block range
description:
## Reproduction

At tag `v0.37.0` (and on `main` at `a37801fe4`), parse with `pampa::wasm_entry_points::qmd_to_pandoc`, compute `quarto_ast_reconcile::compute_reconciliation(&original, &original)` (no edit), and call `pampa::writers::incremental::incremental_write`.

Input A (33 bytes, front matter only, no body blocks):

```
---
title: Only front matter
---
```

Output: the empty string. The front matter is lost.

Input B (36 bytes):

```
First paragraph.

Last paragraph.


```

Output: 34 bytes; the two trailing blank lines after `Last paragraph.` are dropped. Editing any block in the document drops the trailing blank lines the same way — the bytes are not anchored to a block that survives editing.

## Observed vs expected

Observed: with no edits, the output differs from the input — it is missing either the whole document (when it has no blocks) or the bytes after the last block (when it has one or more).

Expected: with no edits, the output equals the input exactly. Bytes before the first block (when front matter is unchanged) and bytes after the last block are copied verbatim from the original, the same way the gap between two kept blocks already is.

## Cause

In `crates/pampa/src/writers/incremental.rs`:

- `assemble` walks the coarsened block list and emits a metadata prefix, then each block with its separator, but never emits anything for the region from the end of the last block to the end of the input. There is no "epilogue" step mirroring the "prefix" step.
- `emit_metadata_prefix` computes `first_block_start` as `None` when `original_ast.blocks` is empty, which means "no metadata prefix region" — so a document that is *entirely* front matter (zero body blocks) never has its front matter copied or rewritten at all.

## Suggested fix

In `assemble`, after the main block loop, append `original_qmd[last_block_end..]` where `last_block_end` is the original AST's last block's end offset (via `SourceInfo::preimage_in`), when that block list is non-empty. In `emit_metadata_prefix`, treat a blocks-empty document's "first block start" as `original_qmd.len()` instead of `None`, so the whole document is considered the candidate metadata-prefix region instead of being skipped outright.

title: hub-client: a project with no files shows an editable buffer that is not a file, and a broken preview message
description:
When a project has no files, the editor still renders an editable text buffer even though no file is selected (the document header says "No file selected"). Text typed there is not saved anywhere.

The preview pane next to it shows a broken message: "This .no currentFile path file can be edited in the editor".

Expected: with no file selected, show an empty state in place of the editor and the preview, for example "This project has no files yet. Create a file or pick one from the Files panel." with a New file action, and keep editing disabled until a file is created or picked.

Code pointers (v0.37.0):

- `hub-client/src/components/Editor.tsx` renders `<MonacoEditor>` even when `currentFile` is null.
- `ts-packages/preview-renderer/src/overlays/PreviewStaticInfoViews.tsx` builds the preview message from the empty path.

title: project-level `filters:` paths are resolved relative to each document directory, so pages in subdirectories fail
description:
Found while reproducing @atheriel's Connect-docs report on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Not part of the original report, but any project-level Lua filter in a multi-directory website hits it.

## Problem

A relative path in a project-level `filters:` list (in `_quarto.yml`, either top-level or under `format.html.filters`) is resolved against the **directory of each document being rendered**, not against the project root. Pages at the project root find the filter; pages in any subdirectory fail with `Failed to read filter '<subdir>/<filter>.lua'`.

Quarto 1 resolves filter paths so that a project-level entry works from every page (document directory first, then the project directory), so `filters: [hello.lua]` in `_quarto.yml` works for every page.

## Repro

```
_quarto.yml
index.qmd
hello.lua
sub/page.qmd
```

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
filters:
  - hello.lua
```

```lua
-- hello.lua
function Pandoc(doc) print("hello from filter") return doc end
```

```
$ q2 render
Rendering project: /.../filterpath (type: website)
hello from filter
error: while rendering /.../filterpath/sub/page.qmd
Error: Failed to read filter '/.../filterpath/sub/hello.lua': I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)
Rendered 1 of 2 files to /.../filterpath/_site — 1 error
```

Same result with `./hello.lua` and with the filter listed under `format.html.filters`.

## Expected

A relative filter path should resolve against the directory of the config file that declared it (project root for `_quarto.yml`, document directory for front matter), or at least fall back to the project root when the document-relative path does not exist, matching Quarto 1.

## Pointers

- `resolve_filter_path` in `crates/quarto-core/src/filter_resolve.rs` (around line 322) joins every relative path onto `document_dir` unconditionally; the existence probes above it (lines ~180 and ~207) also use `document_dir` only. The merged metadata has lost which config file the entry came from by then, so the fix may need the source info on the `filters` entry or a project-root fallback.

cc @atheriel

title: website: alias differing from its page only by case (Q-5-25) is a hard error; needs warning or opt-out for case-sensitive hosts
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a larger report; see #939 for the full list of siblings.

## Problem

An alias whose output path differs from a rendered page only by case is a hard error (`Q-5-25`) that halts the render. The check is deliberate and documented (`docs/errors/project/Q-5-25.qmd`): on case-insensitive filesystems the alias stub and the real page would be one file.

But URL paths are case-sensitive, and so are many deployment targets. Connect's docs are served from S3, where `R/index.html` and `r/index.html` are separate keys. Connect renamed some `viewer/R/` directories to `viewer/r/` and added aliases so the old URLs keep working; `https://docs.posit.co/connect/cookbook/content/integrations/msgraph/viewer/R/` serves such an alias redirect today. Quarto 1 renders these as ordinary redirect pages. Connect needs them for backwards compatibility, and with q2 there is currently no way to produce them at all.

## Repro

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
```

```yaml
# r/index.qmd
---
title: R example
aliases:
  - /R/
---
```

```
$ q2 render
Rendering project: /.../alias (type: website)
Error: [Q-5-25] Alias differs only by case from a rendered page
   ╭─[ r/index.qmd:4:5 ]
 4 │   - /R/
   │     ─┬─
   │      ╰─── `/R/` in `r/index.qmd` resolves to `R/index.html`, which differs only in capitalization from `r/index.html` rendered by `r/index.qmd`. macOS and Windows treat those as one file.
───╯
ℹ Rename the alias so it cannot collide with the page?
$ echo $?
1
```

The render stops there: no `Rendered N of N` summary, no `search.json`. Changing the alias to `/old-r/` renders fine and produces the redirect stub.

## Expected

The collision is real on case-insensitive filesystems, so a diagnostic makes sense, but it should not be fatal by default, or there should be an opt-in for case-sensitive targets. Options:

1. Downgrade Q-5-25 to a warning and still write the stub. On a case-insensitive filesystem the stub overwrites the page (or vice versa), which is bad, so this probably needs to pair with a runtime check of whether the output directory is actually case-insensitive (write a probe file and test).
2. Keep the error by default and add a project option (something like `website.aliases.case-sensitive: true`, name to be decided) that declares the deployment target case-sensitive and turns the error into a warning or silences it.
3. Both: warn when the output filesystem is case-sensitive, error only when it is not, and provide the option to override.

Option 3 seems most useful. Either way the error message should mention the escape hatch.

## Pointers

- The check is in `crates/quarto-core/src/project/aliases.rs` (case-folded bucket collision) and raised from `crates/quarto-core/src/project/website_post_render.rs` around line 1091.
- Tests: `crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/website_aliases.rs`.

cc @atheriel

title: hub-client: undoing a "resolve comment" action needs to be trivial

title: lua: `quarto.version` is hard-coded to the plain table `{0, 1, 0}`, not a comparable Version
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a larger report; see #939 for the full list of siblings.

## Problem

`quarto.version` is hard-coded to the plain Lua table `{0, 1, 0}`. In Quarto 1 it is a pandoc `Version` object, so filters compare it with `quarto.version >= "1.4"` or `pandoc.types.Version(...)`. In q2:

- the value is `0.1.0` regardless of the actual q2 version (0.36.0 here);
- it is a plain table, so comparisons fail with `attempt to compare string with table`;
- `pandoc.types` does not exist, so a filter cannot even wrap it itself.

A filter therefore has no reliable way to tell q2 from Quarto 1, or one q2 release from another.

## Repro

```lua
function Pandoc(doc)
  print("version values: " .. table.concat(quarto.version, "."))
  print("type: " .. pandoc.utils.type(quarto.version))
  local ok, r = pcall(function() return quarto.version >= "1.4" end)
  print("quarto.version >= '1.4': ok=" .. tostring(ok) .. " -> " .. tostring(r))
  local ok2, r2 = pcall(function() return pandoc.types.Version(quarto.version) end)
  print("pandoc.types.Version: ok=" .. tostring(ok2) .. " -> " .. tostring(r2))
  return doc
end
```

```
version values: 0.1.0
type: table
quarto.version >= '1.4': ok=false -> attempt to compare string with table
pandoc.types.Version: ok=false -> attempt to index a nil value (field 'types')
```

## Expected

`quarto.version` should carry the real binary version (from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`) and behave like a pandoc `Version` (comparable with strings and other Versions, `tostring` gives `"0.36.0"`, numeric indexing still works so `table.concat(quarto.version, ".")` keeps working). Ideally `pandoc.types.Version` should exist as well.

## Pointers

- `register_quarto_version` in `crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs` (around line 218) sets the literal `{0, 1, 0}`.

cc @atheriel

title: lua: `os.exit(1)` in a filter kills the whole q2 process instead of failing the document
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a larger report; see #939 for the full list of siblings.

## Problem

Quarto 1 filters use `os.exit(1)` to fail a render, because Quarto 1 replaces Lua's `error()` with a function that only logs. In q2, `os.exit(1)` inside a filter terminates the whole q2 process:

- no output is written for any page, including pages that already rendered successfully;
- there is no render summary;
- parse errors on pages not yet reached are never reported.

`error()` in q2 behaves well (fails that one document, continues with the rest, reports everything at the end), and `quarto.error(msg, el)` is better still, but neither exists in that form in Quarto 1, so ported filters will keep calling `os.exit`.

## Repro

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
filters:
  - die.lua
```

Three pages: `a.qmd` (title `A`), `b.qmd` (title `B`), and `c.qmd` containing a deliberate parse error (`*unclosed emphasis`).

```lua
-- die.lua
function Pandoc(doc)
  local title = pandoc.utils.stringify(doc.meta.title)
  print("filter running on " .. title)
  if title == "A" then
    io.stderr:write("fatal: validation failed on A\n")
    os.exit(1)
  end
  return doc
end
```

```
$ q2 render
Rendering project: /.../luaexit (type: website)
filter running on A
fatal: validation failed on A
filter running on B
$ echo $?
1
$ ls _site
(empty)
```

The Q-2-12 error in `c.qmd` is never shown. Compare with `error("validation failed on A")` in place of `os.exit(1)`:

```
$ q2 render
filter running on B
filter running on A
fatal: validation failed on A
warning: profile-pass skipped /.../c.qmd: Error: [Q-2-12] Unclosed Star Emphasis
...
error: while rendering /.../a.qmd
Error: Lua filter error: runtime error: [string "..."]:6: validation failed on A
Rendered 1 of 3 files to /.../_site — 2 errors
```

## Expected

`os.exit(n)` from a filter should fail the current document the way `error()` does (or the way `quarto.error` does), not abort the process. The exit status can still be non-zero at the end. At minimum, q2 should intercept `os.exit` in the filter sandbox and turn it into a document-level failure.

## Pointers

- Lua filter execution is in `crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs`; the native build uses the full Lua stdlib, so `os.exit` is the real libc exit.

cc @atheriel

title: lua: `quarto.doc.input_file` / `quarto.doc.output_file` are missing; filters cannot learn the current input path
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a larger report; siblings: #939 (`quarto.project`), #941 (`os.exit`), #942 (`quarto.version`).

## Problem

Quarto 1 exposes `quarto.doc.input_file` and `quarto.doc.output_file` to Lua filters. q2's `quarto.doc` has neither, and there is no other way for a filter to learn which file it is processing:

- `quarto.doc` has no path field. Its keys in 0.36.0 are `_dependencies, _resources, _text_includes, addHtmlDependency, addResource, add_html_dependency, add_resource, hasBootstrap, has_bootstrap, includeText, include_text, isFormat, is_format`.
- The injected metadata (`quarto`, `project`, `rendered`, `listing-item`) does not include a path.
- `PANDOC_STATE` is `nil`, so `PANDOC_STATE.input_files` is unavailable too.
- An element's `source_info` exposes only an integer `file_id` and byte offsets.
- The working directory is the project root for every page, so `pandoc.system.get_working_directory()` does not help.

Connect's `config-links` filter needs this to build a relative link from each page to the configuration appendix and to skip some pages by path.

## Repro

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
filters:
  - probe.lua
```

```lua
-- probe.lua
function Pandoc(doc)
  print("quarto.doc.input_file: " .. tostring(quarto.doc.input_file))
  print("quarto.doc.output_file: " .. tostring(quarto.doc.output_file))
  print("PANDOC_STATE: " .. tostring(PANDOC_STATE))
  return doc
end
```

```
$ q2 render
quarto.doc.input_file: nil
quarto.doc.output_file: nil
PANDOC_STATE: nil
```

## Expected

`quarto.doc.input_file` and `quarto.doc.output_file` populated as in Quarto 1 (absolute paths). Together with `quarto.project.directory` / `quarto.project.offset` this is what lets a filter compute per-page relative links.

## Pointers

- `crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_doc.rs` builds `quarto.doc`.

cc @atheriel

title: lua: `quarto.project` (directory, offset, output_directory, profile) is missing; `--profile` not visible as `QUARTO_PROFILE`
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a larger report; siblings: #940 (`quarto.doc.input_file`), #941 (`os.exit`), #942 (`quarto.version`), #943 (possessive apostrophes), #944 (case-only aliases), #945 (filter path resolution).

## Problem

Quarto 1 exposes a `quarto.project` table to Lua filters, with `directory`, `offset`, `output_directory`, and `profile`. q2 does not define `quarto.project` at all, so any Quarto 1 filter that indexes it fails:

```
attempt to index a nil value (field 'project')
```

There is no workaround that gives a filter the project directory:

- The working directory is the project root for every page, but a filter cannot distinguish "project root" from "single-file render".
- `PANDOC_SCRIPT_FILE` is set, so a filter can derive the project directory from its own location, but only when it knows where it sits in the project.
- The injected `project` metadata only contains `type`.

The active profile is also unreachable. `QUARTO_PROFILE` is visible via `os.getenv` only when it was set in the environment; with `--profile drafts` it is `nil`.

Connect's `config-links` filter reads the configuration appendix from the project directory, builds a relative link from each page to it, and relaxes its checks under the `drafts` profile.

## Repro

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
profile:
  group:
    - [drafts, release]
filters:
  - probe.lua
```

```lua
-- probe.lua
function Pandoc(doc)
  print("quarto.project: " .. tostring(quarto.project))
  print("QUARTO_PROFILE env: " .. tostring(os.getenv("QUARTO_PROFILE")))
  print("cwd: " .. pandoc.system.get_working_directory())
  local ok, err = pcall(function() return quarto.project.directory end)
  print("quarto.project.directory -> " .. tostring(ok) .. " " .. tostring(err))
  return doc
end
```

```
$ q2 render --profile drafts
quarto.project: nil
QUARTO_PROFILE env: nil
cwd: /.../repro
quarto.project.directory -> false [string "..."]:5: attempt to index a nil value (field 'project')

$ QUARTO_PROFILE=drafts q2 render
QUARTO_PROFILE env: drafts
```

The keys actually present on `quarto` in 0.36.0:

```
_diagnostics, attribution, base64, component, config, doc, error, include,
json, lmd, log, markdown, metadata, paths, utils, version, warn
```

## Expected

A `quarto.project` table matching Quarto 1's shape: `directory`, `offset` (relative path from the document's directory back to the project root), `output_directory`, and `profile` (a list of active profile names). Also, `QUARTO_PROFILE` should reflect `--profile` inside the Lua environment, since Quarto 1 filters read it through `os.getenv`.

## Pointers

- The `quarto` table is assembled in `crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs`; `quarto.doc` lives in `crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_doc.rs`.
- Profile resolution is in `crates/quarto-core/src/project/project_profile.rs`.

cc @atheriel

title: QuartoHub: have the Document name before the filename in the browser tab
description:
When editing a Quarto Hub document, the browser tab shows the filename and then the document title, e.g. `index.qmd — My doc — Quarto Hub`, which means when the tab is narrow, you just see the filename. With several documents open, the tabs are hard to tell apart.

Could we swap the filename and the title: `My doc — index.qmd — Quarto Hub` instead? That should give a better experience in finding the right tabs.

title: pampa: footnote text on the line after `[^1]:` reports Q-2-29 "Indented Footnote Content" although nothing is indented
description:
Reported by @atheriel while porting the Posit Connect documentation from Quarto 1.9.32 to q2 0.36.0. Reproduced on `main` at 3f7d4b0e8 (q2 0.36.0, macOS). Split out of a second batch of parsing reports; sibling: #946 (`$` in prose).

## Problem

A footnote label with its text on the following line reports `[Q-2-29] Indented Footnote Content Not Supported`, but nothing is indented:

```markdown
[^1]

[^1]:
Text.
```

```
Error: [Q-2-29] Indented Footnote Content Not Supported
   ╭─[ f1.qmd:3:6 ]
 3 │ [^1]:
   │ ──┬──┬
   │   ╰───── This footnote definition has indented content, which is not supported in quarto markdown.
   │      │
   │      ╰── Quarto markdown does not support indented footnote content. Use the div syntax instead: `::: ^ref ... :::`.
───╯
```

Pandoc reads `Text.` as a lazy continuation and makes it the footnote body. #202 established that q2 will not support Pandoc-style footnote continuations, so rejecting this input is expected. The problem is the message: it describes a different mistake. A reader who checks their file for indentation finds none and is stuck.

The same message also appears for a label with nothing after it at all:

```markdown
[^1]

[^1]:
```

So the diagnostic is really "footnote definition has no text on its line", and the indented case is one of three inputs that reach it.

## Repro

| Input (after `[^1]` + blank line) | Result |
|---|---|
| `[^1]:` newline `Text.` | Q-2-29, "indented content" |
| `[^1]:` newline `    Text.` | Q-2-29 (the case the message was written for) |
| `[^1]:` alone | Q-2-29, "indented content" |
| `[^1]: Text.` | OK |

## Expected

When the line after the label is not indented (or there is no following line), the message should say that the definition has no text on its line, and suggest:

- `[^1]: Text.` for a single-paragraph note, or
- the `::: ^1` block form for multi-paragraph notes.

The existing indented-content wording can stay for the indented case, or the two can share a neutral title like "Footnote definition has no content on its line" with the div-syntax hint. Either way, "indented" should only appear when the next line is actually indented.

## Pointers

- Diagnostics are table-driven from `crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/` (Q-2-29.json) via `crates/quarto-parse-errors/src/error_generation.rs`; the corpus guard for Q-2-29 presumably matches on the `[^1]:` parser state regardless of what follows. A guard on the next line's leading whitespace, or a second corpus entry, would split the cases.
- Docs: `docs/errors/markdown/Q-2-29.qmd`.

cc @atheriel

title: qmd writer turns a loose bullet list into a tight one when items contain a nested sublist
description:
A `BulletList` parsed as loose (each item's first block is `Paragraph`) round-trips as tight (`Plain`) when at least one item contains a nested sublist. The writer emits blank-line separators between top-level items but the re-parser does not treat the resulting source as loose, so the outer list collapses. Symptom: `items[[i]][[1]]$tag = "Plain"` after the round trip where the original was `"Paragraph"`.

````
$ printf -- '-   a\n\n    -   c\n    -   d\n\n-   b\n'

    -   c
    -   d

[ BulletList [[Para [Str "a"], BulletList [[Plain [Str "c"]], [Plain [Str "d"]]]], [Para [Str "b"]]] ]

$ printf -- '-   a\n\n    -   c\n    -   d\n\n-   b\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd

title: pandoc.read(text, "commonmark") from Lua, with source locations that resolve into the document
description:
## Summary

Add a `"commonmark"` reader format to the Lua `pandoc.read(text, format)`, backed by the existing `pampa::readers::commonmark` (comrak + `comrak-to-pandoc`), with source locations that resolve into the calling document. Today the second argument is parsed and validated, but the whitelist is `qmd`, `markdown` (an alias for `qmd`), `json` and `raw-json` (`SUPPORTED_READER_FORMATS` in `crates/pampa/src/options.rs`), and the dispatch in `crates/pampa/src/lua/readwrite.rs` has arms for `qmd` and `json` only. The commonmark reader's only caller is the pampa CLI's `--from commonmark`.

## Why

The qmd reader is stricter than CommonMark on purpose: reserved braces, bare brackets, quote balancing, `$` math. That is right for hand-written documents and wrong for strings that were never written as qmd. An lmd cell or a filter that builds content from data (a JSON schema's description fields, a CMS, a database) has exactly one way to get inlines from a string, `pandoc.read(s, "markdown")`, and on ordinary prose it either throws (`{env:VAR}`, `$HOME`, `"<name>"`, `["a", "b"]` all do) or silently changes the text (a bare `[...]` loses its brackets, Q-2-49). A sweep over ~1,100 schema-description strings in one data-driven page rejected 6 and altered 1. The workaround is to hand-build `Str`/`Code` inlines in Lua.

Pandoc's `pandoc.read` takes a reader name for this reason, and the parser is already in the tree, so the port cost is the Lua arm plus the source-location work below. There is independent value in having the commonmark reader hooked into the pipeline's source-location machinery regardless of Lua.

## What "good source locations" means here

Two things have to be true for a diagnostic raised about a node that came out of `pandoc.read` to point somewhere useful:

1. **The reader's spans must be mappable.** `readers/commonmark.rs` does produce a `SourceInfo::Original` for every block and inline (and token-level positions for `Str`/`Space` via the lockstep walker in `comrak-to-pandoc/src/text.rs`), but it stamps them with a `FileId` whose entry has no content. That is #883 and should land first; for an in-memory string there is otherwise nothing to map against.
2. **The spans must resolve into the document, not into a private context.** Nodes that `pandoc.read` returns today carry offsets relative to the string and are read by later transforms as offsets into the host document. That is #884. The qmd reader has the mechanism to avoid it: `readers::qmd::read(…, parent_source_info)` wraps every node span as a `SourceInfo::Substring` of the parent and reroots Err-path diagnostics the same way (`reroot_diagnostics_into_parent`). The commonmark reader has no such parameter.

## Proposed shape

- `readers::commonmark::read` gains a `parent_source_info: Option<SourceInfo>`; when present, every `sourcepos_to_source_info` result is `SourceInfo::substring(parent, start, end)` instead of `Original`. The conversion already funnels every position through `SourceLocationContext::sourcepos_to_source_info`, so this is one branch.
- The Lua binding constructs the parent for **both** readers. Options, from the discussion on #884: register the string as a synthetic file in the document's `SourceContext` at call time (needs the binding to reach the document context, which the Lua runtimes already thread for `quarto._diagnostics`), or build a `Generated` anchor from `filter_source_info(lua)` (chunk name and line of the calling Lua code) and make the parse a `Substring` of that. Either gives a diagnostic the frame "in a string passed to `pandoc.read` from `doc.qmd:14`".
- Add `"commonmark"` to `SUPPORTED_READER_FORMATS` and a dispatch arm. The commonmark reader should get the same post-read treatment the `json` arm gets (`desugar_document`) so that a `.list-table` div written in CommonMark-ish markup still becomes a table; decide and document whether heading ids and implicit figures (the two documented qmd-vs-commonmark differences in `comrak-to-pandoc/tests/integration/differential.rs`) apply.
- Forward the reader's diagnostics through `quarto._diagnostics` once locations are sound (`bd-fwswbxnl`).
- Register `"commonmark"` in `pandoc.readers` so Lua code can feature-test it.

## Known imprecisions to keep in mind (documented in `comrak-to-pandoc`)

- `Code` spans pair the stripped literal with a backtick-inclusive span, so content offsets inside a `Code` are not composable over its span.
- Link and image URLs carry `TargetSourceInfo::empty()`; no provenance.
- The text tiling has one stated blind spot (a known multi-character entity immediately followed by `&` or `\\`) that can produce a sub-token misattribution rather than the whole-node fallback.

None of these block the feature; they bound how precise an underline inside a `pandoc.read` string can be.

## Environment

Repo at `ad283a2cb`; q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021.

title: Nodes returned by pandoc.read inside an lmd cell get diagnostics located at string offsets in the host document
description:
## Summary

Diagnostics raised about AST nodes that `pandoc.read` returned inside an lmd cell are attributed to the host document at the node's *string-relative* offsets. The warning names the right file and the wrong line: it underlines whatever happens to sit at byte N of the document, where N is the byte offset inside the string that was passed to `pandoc.read`. In practice that is a line of the front matter.

## Repro

`loc.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: diagnostic location from pandoc.read
---

## Section one

Some paragraph text that occupies line 7.

More text on line 9.

## Section two, cell starts on line 13

```{lmd}
local doc = pandoc.read('Allowed kinds: ["skills", "commands"] only.', 'markdown')
return doc.blocks
```

Trailing paragraph on line 18.
````

```sh
q2 render loc.qmd --to html --json-errors
```

```json
{"kind":"warning","code":"Q-2-49","source_file":".../loc.qmd","start_line":2,"start_column":12, ...}
```

The human-readable form underlines `title: diagnostic location …` on line 2. The text the warning is about lives on line 14, inside the Lua string. Wrapping the call in `pcall` changes nothing (it is a warning, not an error).

The arithmetic matches exactly: in the string, `[` is at byte offset 15. In `loc.qmd`, byte 15 is line 2, column 12 (`---\n` is four bytes, then eleven more into the title line).

## Why

1. The `qmd` arm of `pandoc_read` (`crates/pampa/src/lua/readwrite.rs`) parses the string into a **fresh** `ASTContext` whose file 0 is named `<pandoc.read>`, with `parent_source_info: None`. Every node comes out as `SourceInfo::Original { file_id: FileId(0), start, end }` with offsets relative to the string.
2. The nodes cross into Lua as userdata with their `SourceInfo` intact (`el.source_info` is observable from Lua) and come back the same way when the cell returns them.
3. In the host document's `SourceContext`, `FileId(0)` is the document itself. Any pass that reads the node's span and maps it, here `transforms/reference_link_diagnostics.rs` emitting Q-2-49 via `source_info(label)`, lands on the host document at the string's offsets.

The lmd stage already knows this for its own desugaring pass: `relocate_to_cell` in `crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/lmd_execute.rs` carries the comment "a node `pandoc.read` returned carries an offset into that call's private source context" and relocates those diagnostics to the whole cell. Every *later* transform that reports on a node is unprotected. The same mechanism would affect Lua filters that return `pandoc.read` output, not only lmd cells.

Related: `bd-fwswbxnl` (the reader's *own* warnings from `pandoc.read` are dropped entirely, `Ok((pandoc, _context, _warnings))`) records the same underlying question, "how does `<pandoc.read>` text get a home in the document's `SourceContext`", and was deferred there. This issue is the user-visible half: the nodes that do come back are mislocated.

## Expected

One of, in order of preference:

- **Register the string as a file in the document's `SourceContext`** at call time (a synthetic path such as `<pandoc.read>` plus the call site, with the content), so that offsets resolve to that file and diagnostics can show the string's own text with an "in a string passed to `pandoc.read` from the lmd cell at loc.qmd:14" frame. The qmd reader already supports parsing *into* a parent via `parent_source_info`, producing `Substring` spans; the Lua binding would need to construct that parent (it has `filter_source_info(lua)` for the chunk name and line of the calling Lua code).
- Failing that, **strip the locations** of nodes returned by `pandoc.read` to `SourceInfo::generated(By::filter(path, line))` like nodes a filter builds by hand, so that downstream diagnostics fall back to the cell instead of pointing at a wrong line.

What should not happen is a confident, wrong location in the host document.

## Environment

q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021 (macOS arm64); repo at `ad283a2cb`.

title: commonmark reader registers its input twice and stamps nodes with the content-less FileId(0)
description:
## Summary

`pampa::readers::commonmark::read` registers its input in the `SourceContext` twice and then points every node's `SourceInfo` at the wrong entry: the one without content. Line/column mapping for commonmark-read nodes only works today because the sole caller (the pampa CLI's `--from commonmark`) passes a real path that the first registration reads back from disk. For an in-memory input (anything named like `<pandoc.read>`), no position in the resulting AST can be turned into a line and column.

## Where

`crates/pampa/src/readers/commonmark.rs`, `read`:

```rust
let mut context = ASTContext::with_filename(filename.to_string());   // (1) add_file(filename, None) -> FileId(0)
let normalized_filename = context.filenames[0].clone();
context
    .source_context
    .add_file(normalized_filename, Some(input.to_string()));          // (2) same path, with content -> FileId(1)
let file_id = FileId(0);                                               // (3) ...but nodes are stamped with FileId(0)

let source_ctx = SourceLocationContext::new(input, file_id);
let pandoc = convert_document_with_source(root, Some(&source_ctx));
```

`SourceContext::add_file` (quarto-source-map 0.3.0, `context.rs`) always pushes a new `SourceFile`; it does not dedupe by path. So after (2) the context holds two files with the same path: `FileId(0)` with `content: None` and a `file_info` only if `std::fs::read_to_string(path)` succeeded, and `FileId(1)` with the actual content. Every `SourceInfo::Original` the conversion produces names `FileId(0)`.

The qmd reader (`readers/qmd.rs`, same spot) avoids this by replacing the context before adding the file:

```rust
let mut context = ASTContext::with_filename(filename.to_string());
context.source_context = quarto_source_map::SourceContext::new();
context.source_context.add_file(normalized_filename, Some(input_str));
```

so its `FileId(0)` is the entry that has the content.

## Evidence that it is pinned rather than caught

`crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_diagnostic_path_normalization.rs`, `commonmark_reader_source_context_uses_forward_slashes`, asserts on `FileId(1)` and explains why:

> FileId(0) is the entry `ASTContext::with_filename` creates internally … The fix this test protects is commonmark::read's own second `add_file` call, which lands at FileId(1)

That test will need to move to `FileId(0)` with the fix (and could additionally assert the context holds exactly one file).

## Consequences

- With a real on-disk path: works by accident. `FileId(0)` got a `FileInformation` from re-reading the file, so `map_offset` succeeds; `FileId(1)` is dead weight.
- With an in-memory input and a synthetic name: `FileId(0)` has neither content nor `file_info`. A diagnostic or any `map_offset` against a commonmark node has an offset into a file the context cannot map. This is the path a Lua `pandoc.read(text, "commonmark")` would take (separate issue), and the reason to fix this first.
- Snapshot or provenance tooling that looks at `root_file_id()` of commonmark nodes gets the content-less entry.

## Fix

Mirror the qmd reader: build the context, replace `source_context` with a fresh one (or skip the `with_filename` registration), `add_file(normalized, Some(input))` once, and use the `FileId` that call returns instead of a hard-coded `FileId(0)`. Update the test above to assert a single file at `FileId(0)` with the normalized path and the content.

## Environment

Repo at `ad283a2cb` (2026-10-16); quarto-source-map 0.3.0.

title: pampa - Unsupported definition lists in quarto-web change AST after a QMD round trip
description:
This surfaced while round-tripping existing quarto-web documents through q2r and pampa, including [appendices.qmd](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/authoring/appendices.qmd#L42), [notebook-embed.qmd](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/authoring/notebook-embed.qmd#L175), and [journals/templates.qmd](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/journals/templates.qmd#L135). These documents use Pandoc-style definition lists. Pampa warns with Q-2-54 but accepts each definition as a paragraph containing its source text in a single literal `Str`. Writing and reparsing the accepted document changes that AST.

The writer escapes the leading colon, so the next parse treats the definition as ordinary paragraph text with separate words and spaces. Reparsing the emitted QMD produces no Q-2-54 warning, even though the definition has not been migrated to a supported definition-list representation. Definitions containing inline Markdown also lose that formatting during the initial fallback: in the excerpt below, the backticks around `typst-template.typ` become literal text, which the writer subsequently escapes. All three full documents reproduce the AST change and emit no Q-2-54 diagnostics when their written QMD is parsed again. The initial parse still emits the warning.

Getting the escaping correct seems a bit fraught so one possible option is to make Q-2-54 an error rather than a warning. That would reject these unsupported definition lists instead of accepting a literal-text fallback whose interpretation changes across the round trip. The diagnostic already identifies the supported `::: {.definition-list}` form and the `qmd-syntax-helper convert -r definition-lists` migration command.

The following is the actual `typst-show.typ` entry from [journals/templates.qmd](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/journals/templates.qmd#L151), isolated from the rest of the document. It reproduces both the AST change and the escaping of literal backticks, without nested lists or character references.

Verified with pampa at d3ed54fe4dfc87750d7593ba9b40f974b725752f. Warning's location and hints are abbreviated with `...` and Cargo status lines and ANSI color escapes are omitted.

````
$ printf -- 'typst-show.typ\n\n:   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in `typst-template.typ`.\n'
typst-show.typ

:   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in `typst-template.typ`.

$ printf -- 'typst-show.typ\n\n:   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in `typst-template.typ`.\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
Warning: [Q-2-54] Pandoc definition lists are not supported
...

[ Para [Str "typst-show.typ"], Para [Str ":   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in `typst-template.typ`."] ]

$ printf -- 'typst-show.typ\n\n:   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in `typst-template.typ`.\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
Warning: [Q-2-54] Pandoc definition lists are not supported
...

typst-show.typ

\:   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in \`typst-template.typ\`.

````

The warning above comes from parsing the original input before writing QMD. Reading the emitted QMD separately produces the changed AST without a warning:

````
$ printf -- 'typst-show.typ\n\n\\:   A show rule for the entire document that captures document metadata and passes it to the function defined in \\`typst-template.typ\\`.\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
[ Para [Str "typst-show.typ"], Para [Str ":", Space, Str "A", Space, Str "show", Space, Str "rule", Space, Str "for", Space, Str "the", Space, Str "entire", Space, Str "document", Space, Str "that", Space, Str "captures", Space, Str "document", Space, Str "metadata", Space, Str "and", Space, Str "passes", Space, Str "it", Space, Str "to", Space, Str "the", Space, Str "function", Space, Str "defined", Space, Str "in", Space, Str "`typst-template.typ`."] ]
````

Two additional probes exposed related writer behavior, but were not the original quarto-web failures:

- A definition body containing `: - first\n  - second` initially becomes literal paragraphs, but the continuation reparses as a bullet list after writing. Rejecting Q-2-54 would also avoid this fallback path.
- `  - item` parses without warnings as `Para [Str "  - item"]`, then writes as `  - item` and reparses as a bullet list. This character-reference case is independent of definition lists and would remain if Q-2-54 became an error but is also unlikely / self-inflicted.

title: pampa - shortcode backslashes double or make the QMD writer's output unparseable
description:
The QMD writer escapes both quotes and backslashes in shortcode arguments, but the quoted-string reader only unescapes quotes. A trailing backslash interferes with the closing quote, making the generated QMD unparseable. An internal backslash instead doubles on each round trip without a diagnostic. Both positional and keyword arguments are affected.

Verified with pampa at d3ed54fe4dfc87750d7593ba9b40f974b725752f. Cargo status lines and ANSI color escapes are omitted; diagnostics are retained. In pipelines, only stdout goes to the next command. Native AST output represents each literal backslash as `\\`.

The trailing-backslash case occurs in keyboard shortcuts:

````
$ printf -- '{{< kbd mac=Cmd-\\\\ >}}\n'
{{< kbd mac=Cmd-\\ >}}

$ printf -- '{{< kbd mac=Cmd-\\\\ >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
[ Para [Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__"] , [("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) [Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__-param"] , [("data-raw", "kbd"), ("data-value", "kbd"), ("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) [], Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__-param"] , [("data-raw", "mac = Cmd-\\"), ("data-key", "mac"), ("data-value", "Cmd-\\"), ("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) []]] ]

$ printf -- '{{< kbd mac=Cmd-\\\\ >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
{{< kbd mac="Cmd-\\" >}}

$ printf -- '{{< kbd mac=Cmd-\\\\ >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
Error: Parse error
   ╭─[ <stdin>:1:26 ]
   │
 1 │ {{< kbd mac="Cmd-\\" >}}
   │                          │ 
   │                          ╰─ unexpected character or token here
───╯
````

With several keyword arguments, this parse failure can surface as Q-2-52 (shortcode delimiters not separated by spaces), even though the required spaces are present.

The internal-backslash case, already recorded in [bd-5te3iryt](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/d3ed54fe4dfc87750d7593ba9b40f974b725752f/.braid/snapshot.jsonl#L331), remains parseable but changes the argument value. The final command shows the backslash count doubling again on a second write:

````
$ printf -- '{{< foo "a\\b" >}}\n'
{{< foo "a\b" >}}

$ printf -- '{{< foo "a\\b" >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
[ Para [Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__"] , [("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) [Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__-param"] , [("data-raw", "foo"), ("data-value", "foo"), ("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) [], Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__-param"] , [("data-raw", "a\\b"), ("data-value", "a\\b"), ("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) []]] ]

$ printf -- '{{< foo "a\\b" >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
{{< foo "a\\b" >}}

$ printf -- '{{< foo "a\\b" >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
[ Para [Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__"] , [("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) [Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__-param"] , [("data-raw", "foo"), ("data-value", "foo"), ("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) [], Span ( "" , ["quarto-shortcode__-param"] , [("data-raw", "a\\\\b"), ("data-value", "a\\\\b"), ("data-is-shortcode", "1")] ) []]] ]

$ printf -- '{{< foo "a\\b" >}}\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
{{< foo "a\\\\b" >}}
````

In the wild (the trailing-backslash case):

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/visual-editor/options.qmd#L25
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/visual-editor/options.qmd#L44

title: pampa: .definition-list and .list-table rewrites don't process their content (nested divs, implicit figures, reader warnings)
description:
## Summary

When pampa rewrites a `.definition-list` or `.list-table` div, it doesn't process the content of the result. Inside the resulting `DefinitionList` or `Table`:

- a nested `.definition-list` or `.list-table` div stays a div;
- a single-image paragraph with alt text doesn't become a `Figure`;
- the reader's other postprocess handlers don't run either. For example, the Q-2-50 doubled-brace fence warning isn't reported.

Pandoc does build nested structures here. It parses a definition list inside a definition, and a table inside a definition. So q2 should apply the structural desugaring set inside the rewritten content too.

## Reproduction

```markdown
::: {.definition-list}
* Outer term
  - ::: {.definition-list}
    * Inner term
      - Inner definition.
    :::
* Table term
  - ::: {.list-table}
    * - a
      - b
    * - 1
      - 2
    :::
:::

::: {.list-table}
* - ::: {.definition-list}
    * Cell term
      - Cell definition.
    :::
  - Plain cell
:::

::: {.definition-list}
* Figure term

  - Some text.

    ![An alt text](img.png)

:::
```

`pampa doc.qmd -t json` (built from `main` at 6582ddb3c; also reproduced with `q2` 0.36.0-nightly.20261022) gives:

- an outer `DefinitionList` whose first definition still contains `Div ["definition-list"]`, and whose second definition still contains `Div ["list-table"]`;
- a `Table` whose first cell still contains `Div ["definition-list"]`;
- a `DefinitionList` whose definition holds `Para [Image]`, not a `Figure`.

The same thing happens when the outer list is wrapped in a plain `::: {}` div.

The concrete-syntax handlers are skipped as well. This input reports no warning:

````markdown
::: {.definition-list}
* Term
  - ```{{python}}
    1 + 1
    ```
:::
````

Change `{.definition-list}` to `{}` and Q-2-50 ("Doubled curly braces are not supported") is reported.

## What pandoc does

Pandoc parses the equivalent `: ` definition-list syntax into nested nodes:

```
$ printf 'Outer term\n:   Inner term\n    :   Inner definition.\n' | pandoc -t native
[ DefinitionList
    [ ( [ Str "Outer" , Space , Str "term" ]
      , [ [ DefinitionList
              [ ( [ Str "Inner" , Space , Str "term" ]
                , [ [ Plain [ Str "Inner" , Space , Str "definition." ] ] ]
                )
              ]
          ]
        ]
      )
    ]
]
```

It also keeps a pipe table inside a definition as a `Table`, and turns an image paragraph inside a loose definition into a `Figure`. (pandoc 3.12.1)

## Cause

`desugar_div` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/desugar.rs` returns `FilterResult(vec![...], false)` for both rewrites. `false` means "don't recurse into the result". `topdown_traverse_blocks` visits a node before its children, so when the outer div is rewritten, nothing inside it is ever visited.

`desugar_div` is shared by both entry points:

- the reader's postprocess filter (`.with_div(...)` in `treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs`), where every other postprocess handler is also skipped inside the result;
- `desugar_blocks` / `desugar_document`, the non-reader path behind lmd cell results, `pandoc.read(…, "json")`, `--from json` and document import.

The doc comment says this is deliberate ("Neither rewrite recurses into its result, matching the reader"). But it contradicts the contract in `dev-docs/syntax-notes.md` § Structural desugaring contract: "All three apply at any depth (inside divs, blockquotes, list items), as pandoc and the reader both do." `the_set_applies_at_any_depth` only tests depth through a blockquote and a plain wrapper div, not through a rewritten div.

## Suggested fix

Return `FilterResult(..., true)` from both rewrites in `desugar_div`, so the traversal continues into the new `Table` / `DefinitionList`.

- **Termination:** the result isn't a `Div`, so `desugar_div` can't fire on it again.
- **No double processing:** the traversal is top-down, so the children haven't been processed yet when the outer div is rewritten.
- **Validation:** the shape checks only look at block kinds (`BulletList`, `Plain`/`Para` term). A `Para [Image]` definition becoming a `Figure` afterwards doesn't affect them.

Then:

- update the `desugar_div` doc comment, and the "Neither rewrite recurses" wording in the module docs;
- add tests for both entry points: a definition-list in a definition, a list-table in a definition, a definition-list in a list-table cell, an implicit figure in a loose definition, and Q-2-50 inside a definition;
- check that the incremental qmd writer still round-trips nested definition-list / list-table divs (`write_definitionlist` and the list-table writer recurse into their content).

## Context

Quarto 1 is getting the same `.definition-list` div syntax so authors can move to it ahead of a migration (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#15140, docs in quarto-dev/quarto-web#2305). Its Lua filter, like Quarto 1's existing `list-table` filter, already handles nested divs, following pandoc. A reviewer of that PR noticed the difference. We decided to follow pandoc's parsing behavior, which means fixing q2 rather than limiting Quarto 1 to one level.

Related: #846 (the desugaring contract for lmd results).

title: q2 render should take a lockfile in the output directory so two concurrent renders cannot interleave their writes
description:
## Summary

Two renders of the same project can run at the same time and write the same output directory: a `q2 preview --static` that re-renders on file changes, and a `q2 render` started by hand (or by an editor task, a CI step, a second terminal). Nothing stops the second one, and the two interleave their writes. Proposal: `q2 render` takes a lockfile in the output directory for the duration of a render and steps back, with a diagnostic, when another render already holds it. Quarto 1 never did this; it is cheap and catches the easy mistakes.

## What happened

A website project was being served with `q2 preview --static`, which watches the project and re-renders it when a source file changes. While it was running, I edited `_quarto.yml` and ran `q2 render` in another terminal. Both renders ran at once into `_site/`.

The render completed without diagnostics, but the search index was broken afterwards:

- `site_libs/quarto-search/pagefind/pagefind-entry.json` named an index hash (`en_3a8a4314f7`),
- the matching `pagefind.en_3a8a4314f7.pf_meta` file was missing from the directory,
- in the browser, every query returned "No results", with `Failed to load the meta index: Error: invalid gzip data` and `Pagefind: WASM Error (No pointer)` on the console (the server answered the missing file with a 404 text body, which the runtime tried to gunzip).

Stopping the preview and rendering once more fixed it. I could not reproduce the missing file with a single renderer, with or without incremental renders, so the cause is the interleaving: one render's search-index step wrote its files while the other was replacing the directory.

The search index is just the piece that broke visibly. Any whole-directory output (`site_libs/`, the Pagefind index, `llms-full.txt`, alias redirects) is open to the same interleaving, and the symptoms are confusing because the final log line of each render says it succeeded.

## Proposal

- When a render starts, create a lockfile in the output directory (for example `_site/.quarto-render.lock`, or next to the other render bookkeeping under `.quarto/`). Write the pid, the start time, and the command that holds it.
- If the lock exists and its holder is alive, do not render. Emit a diagnostic naming the holder ("another render of this project is running: `q2 preview` pid 12345, started 10:57:03") and exit non-zero. A `--wait` flag or a short bounded wait before giving up would cover the common case of a preview mid-render.
- If the lock exists but its pid is gone, treat it as stale: remove it, say so, and continue. A crash must not wedge the project.
- `q2 preview` holds the lock only while it is actually rendering, not while it is merely serving and watching, so a manual render between edits still works when the preview is idle.
- Release the lock on success, failure, and signal.

Races remain possible (two renders starting in the same instant, network file systems, lock files are not transactions), and that is acceptable. The goal is that the obvious mistake, a hand-run render against a watched project, fails loudly instead of corrupting the output silently.

## Environment

`q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021`, macOS.
