title: pampa: display math whitespace trimming diverges from pandoc 3.12 (oracle corpus 049)
description:
## Summary

Pandoc 3.12 trims leading and trailing newlines from display math. pampa keeps them. As a temporary deviation, we've excluded the one oracle-corpus fixture that catches this, `crates/pampa/tests/pandoc-match-corpus/markdown/049.qmd`. It was renamed to `049.qmd-FAILING`, the corpus's existing convention for known mismatches. This issue tracks deciding whether pampa should match pandoc 3.12 here, and re-enabling the fixture if it does.

## The difference

Input (`049.qmd`):

```
$$
1
  + 2
$$
```

| Reader | AST |
|---|---|
| pandoc ≤ 3.11 / pampa today | `Para [ Math DisplayMath "\n1\n  + 2\n" ]` |
| pandoc 3.12.1 | `Para [ Math DisplayMath "1\n  + 2" ]` |

Interior whitespace (the `  + 2` indentation) is kept by both. Only the newline right after the opening `$$` and the one right before the closing `$$` differ.

## How it surfaced

A local pandoc 3.12.1 is outside the calibrated oracle range (3.6–3.11), so the four oracle tests hard-fail by design. `cargo xtask pandoc-check` then showed that `test_html_writer`, `test_json_writer` and the commonmark corpus all pass against 3.12.1. In the markdown corpus, the only failure is `049.qmd`. With 049 parked, all four pass, and the calibrated ceiling moves to 3.12. CI still pins pandoc 3.11.

## To decide

1. **Should pampa trim?** That would match 3.12 and mean dropping support for the old ≤ 3.11 AST in this case. The oracle floor is 3.6, so the corpus can't expect both shapes at once. Matching 3.12 implies raising `PANDOC_ORACLE_MIN_VERSION` to 3.12 and moving CI's `PANDOC_VERSION` to 3.12. Alternatively, the fixture could be gated on the pandoc version.
2. **Downstream effects of trimming.** Math in the HTML writer (`\[...\]`), the Typst and LaTeX writers, the qmd writer round-trip, and any source-location or `data-loc` spans covering the math content all need checking.
3. **Where the trim happens.** In the tree-sitter → Pandoc conversion (matching pandoc's reader), or only in the writers?

Leaning: trim, and match pandoc. To be settled in a separate session.

title: Link validation only covers .qmd targets: directory URLs, .html paths and anchors are never checked
description:
## Summary

Link validation (`Q-13-4`, "Body link references missing document") only fires for links whose target is a `.qmd` source path. Links written as site-root directory URLs (`/guides/install/`), as `.html` paths, or with an anchor are rewritten page-relative and never checked, so a dead link renders silently. Directory URLs are the natural form for a site where every page is a `section/index.qmd`, and they are what you get when migrating from static-site generators whose pages are directories (Astro, Hugo, Docusaurus), so this is the form a migrated site is most likely to use everywhere.

A related consequence: in the `llms-txt` markdown mirror, a directory link stays `guides/install/`, pointing at the HTML page, while the `.qmd` form of the same link is rewritten to `guides/install/index.md`.

## Repro

`q2 create project website site --no-prompt`, then:

`_quarto.yml`
```yaml
project:
  type: website
  render:
    - "**/*.qmd"
website:
  title: "dirlinks"
  llms-txt: true
```

`guides/install/index.qmd`
```qmd
---
title: Install
---

## Requirements

Text.
```

`index.qmd`
```qmd
---
title: Home
---

1. [existing dir](/guides/install/)
2. [missing dir](/guides/nonexistent/)
3. [missing qmd](/guides/nonexistent.qmd)
4. [missing html](/guides/nonexistent.html)
5. [existing dir, good anchor](/guides/install/#requirements)
6. [existing dir, bad anchor](/guides/install/#no-such-section)
7. [existing qmd, bad anchor](/guides/install/index.qmd#no-such-section)
```

```sh
q2 render .
```

One diagnostic, for link 3 only:

```
Warning: [Q-13-4] Body link references missing document
  `guides/nonexistent.qmd` is not in the project index.
```

Rendered `index.html`:

| # | Written | Target exists | Rendered href | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/guides/install/` | yes | `guides/install/` | none (correct) |
| 2 | `/guides/nonexistent/` | no | `guides/nonexistent/` | **none** |
| 3 | `/guides/nonexistent.qmd` | no | `/guides/nonexistent.qmd` (left as is) | Q-13-4 |
| 4 | `/guides/nonexistent.html` | no | `guides/nonexistent.html` | **none** |
| 5 | `/guides/install/#requirements` | yes | `guides/install/#requirements` | none (correct) |
| 6 | `/guides/install/#no-such-section` | page yes, anchor no | `guides/install/#no-such-section` | **none** |
| 7 | `/guides/install/index.qmd#no-such-section` | page yes, anchor no | `guides/install/index.html#no-such-section` | **none** |

So the validator recognises `.qmd` targets and nothing else; anchors are not checked even on a validated `.qmd` target.

`index.md` (the llms-txt companion):

```markdown
1.  [existing dir](guides/install/)
...
7.  [existing qmd, bad anchor](guides/install/index.md#no-such-section)
```

Link 1 points the markdown reader at the HTML directory; link 7 was correctly redirected to the `.md` companion.

## Expected

- A site-root path ending in `/` resolves to `<path>/index.qmd` (or `index.md`) in the project index. If it is there, treat the link exactly like the `.qmd` form (validated, and rewritten to `index.md` in the markdown mirror). If it is not, `Q-13-4`.
- A site-root `.html` path resolves to the source that renders to it, with the same two outcomes.
- Anchors: a separate code for "document found, but it has no heading or id with that anchor", at least for targets in the project index where the headings are known.

Quarto 1 has no link checker, so this is not a parity bug; it is a coverage gap in a q2-only feature.

## Environment

q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021 (macOS arm64); repo at `ad283a2cb`.

title: _quarto.yml: unknown or misplaced keys under project:/website: are silently ignored (Quarto 1 fails validation)
description:
## Summary

`_quarto.yml` is not checked for unknown or misplaced keys. A typo under `website:` or `project:`, or a key nested under the wrong parent, renders silently with the option having no effect. Quarto 1 fails validation with the property name and location. q2 has the diagnostic for this (`Q-1-18` Unknown Property, "closed" schemas) and its doc even lists "a property that belongs to a different block" as a typical cause, but it does not fire for the project config.

How this was found: `llms-txt: true` placed under `format: html:` instead of `website:` produced nothing, no warning, and it took a trip to the docs to see why. (Quarto 1 is silent for that specific placement too, since `format.html` is open for pandoc metadata; the cases below are the ones where it does speak up.)

## Repro

A scaffold (`q2 create project website site --no-prompt`) with one of these configs:

**Unknown and misspelled keys under `website:`**

```yaml
project:
  type: website
website:
  title: "site"
  tocc: true
  llms-text: true
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
```

**Unknown key under `project:`**

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  tocc: true
website:
  title: "site"
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
```

**Known key under the wrong parent**

```yaml
project:
  type: website
website:
  title: "site"
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    llms-txt: true
```

```sh
q2 render site
quarto render site
```

| Config | Quarto 1 (99.9.9 dev) | q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021 |
|---|---|---|
| `website.tocc`, `website.llms-text` | `ERROR: … validation failed. (line 5, columns 3--7) property name tocc is invalid … (line 6) property name llms-text is invalid`, with the location `website:tocc` | renders, no output |
| `project.tocc` | `ERROR: … property name tocc is invalid … location project:tocc` | renders, no output |
| `format.html.llms-txt` | renders, no output | renders, no output |

## Expected

At least what Quarto 1 does: `Q-1-18` for unknown properties under the closed blocks (`project`, `website`, and the other top-level blocks that have schemas), as an error or at least a warning. A nice extra that Quarto 1 does not have: when the unknown key is a known key of a sibling block (`llms-txt` is `website.llms-txt`), say so in the hint.

## Environment

q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021 (macOS arm64); repo at `ad283a2cb`. Quarto 1 at 99.9.9 (dev build from `quarto-cli`).

title: HTML writer drops table column widths: <col /> without style="width"
description:
## Summary

Table column widths never reach the HTML output. The reader produces the right `ColWidth` values (both for `tbl-colwidths` and for `::: {.list-table widths="…"}`), the writer decides a `<colgroup>` is needed because of them, and then writes every column as a bare `<col />`. Quarto 1 writes `<col style="width: 20%">` for the same input.

The writer already knows: `pampa/src/writers/html.rs` has a test `colgroup_kept_when_any_width_set` whose comment says "The width itself isn't rendered yet — only the presence check" (bd-hixmy, from the table-default-rendering-parity plan, which scoped widths out). This issue is the user-visible symptom, filed so it is tracked somewhere findable: a docs site porting a fixed-layout config table (`table-layout: fixed` needs the `<col>` widths) had to reproduce them in CSS with `col:nth-child(n)` rules.

## Repro

`widths.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: column widths
---

## A tbl-colwidths on a pipe table

| Key | Description | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | b | c | d |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20,40,15,25]"}

## B pipe table with relative dash widths (line over 72 chars)

| Key | Description | Type | Default |
|------|--------------------------|-------|----------------|
| a | a long description that pushes this line well past the seventy-two column limit | c | d |

## D list-table with widths

::: {.list-table widths="20,40,15,25"}
* - Key
  - Description
  - Type
  - Default
* - a
  - b
  - c
  - d
:::
````

```sh
quarto render widths.qmd --to html --output-dir q1
q2 render widths.qmd --to html --output-dir q2out
```

`<col>` elements per section:

| Section | Quarto 1 (99.9.9 dev) | q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021 |
|---|---|---|
| A `tbl-colwidths` | `<col style="width: 20%">` `40%` `15%` `25%` | no `<colgroup>` at all, plus an empty `<caption> </caption>` |
| B dash-width pipe table | `<col style="width: 10%">` `47%` `12%` `29%` | no `<colgroup>` |
| D list-table `widths` | `<col style="width: 20%">` `40%` `15%` `25%` | `<colgroup>` with four bare `<col />` |

AST colspecs (`q2 render --to json` vs `quarto pandoc -t json`):

- A: q2 `ColWidth 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.15 / 0.25` (the reader folds `tbl-colwidths` into the colspec, which Quarto 1 only does later in a filter: its pandoc AST shows `ColWidthDefault`). So for A the reader is ahead of the writer, and only the writer is missing.
- D: q2 `ColWidth 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.15 / 0.25`. Same: writer only.
- B: q2 `ColWidthDefault` ×4, Quarto 1 / pandoc `0.109 / 0.473 / 0.127 / 0.291`. Pandoc's rule (relative widths from the separator-row dash counts when any line exceeds the column width) is not implemented in `treesitter_utils/pipe_table.rs` (`colspec.push((alignment, ColWidth::Default))`). That is a reader gap, mentioned here only so the three cases are in one place; split it out if you prefer.

## Expected

`<col style="width: NN%">` per column whenever the colspec has a `ColWidth::Percentage`, matching Quarto 1 / pandoc's HTML writer (percentages rounded to integers, as pandoc does). Section A should also not emit an empty `<caption>` when the caption block only carries attributes.

## Environment

q2 0.35.0-nightly.20261021 (macOS arm64); repo at `ad283a2cb`. Quarto 1 at 99.9.9 (dev build from `quarto-cli`).

title: pandoc.read from Lua leaks "[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Unhandled node kind: -" to stderr for every pipe-table delimiter dash
description:
## Summary

Calling `pandoc.read(text, "markdown")` from an `{lmd}` cell (and presumably from a Lua filter) on text that contains a pipe table prints one line per dash of the delimiter row to stderr:

```
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
```

A two-column table (`|---|---|`) prints six lines; a four-column one prints twelve. The table itself renders correctly, so this is noise, but it is unconditional and unformatted (no diagnostic code, no location, not affected by `--strict` or `-v`), and on a page that builds a large table from data it drowns real diagnostics.

## Repro

`repro.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: pandoc.read of a pipe table
---

| a | b |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |

```{lmd}
return pandoc.read("| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n", "markdown").blocks
```
````

```sh
q2 render repro.qmd --to html
```

stderr:

```
Rendering single file: …/repro.qmd
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: -
```

`repro.html` contains two correct `<table>`s. The literal pipe table in the body prints nothing; only the one parsed through `pandoc.read` does.

## Where it comes from

- The message is the catch-all arm of the tree-sitter node dispatch in `pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter.rs` (`_ => writeln!(buf, "[TOP-LEVEL MISSING NODE] Warning: Unhandled node kind: {}", node.kind())`). The `-` nodes are the children of `pipe_table_delimiter_cell`; `process_pipe_table_delimiter_cell` in `treesitter_utils/pipe_table.rs` handles them explicitly (`else if node == "-"`), so the dispatch appears to reach the fallback for each leaf before the cell processor consumes them. The reader's output is right either way.
- Every reader entry point in the pipeline passes a throwaway buffer to `readers::qmd::read` (`Vec::new()` or `std::io::sink()`), which is why a document's own pipe tables never show this. `pandoc_read` in `pampa/src/lua/readwrite.rs` passes `std::io::stderr()` as that buffer, so the same lines reach the terminal.

Two possible fixes, not exclusive: have `pandoc.read` use a sink like every other caller (or route the buffer into the diagnostic collector), and stop emitting the fallback line for the delimiter-row dashes, since they are not actually unhandled.

## Environment

`q2 0.33.0` (macOS, arm64); repo inspected at `e308835bd`. Found while porting a docs site whose config tables are built by an lmd function via `pandoc.read` (see #846 for why `pandoc.read` is the route in use).

title: lmd: list-table and definition-list divs built from AST nodes in a cell are not desugared
description:
## Summary

A `.list-table` or `.definition-list` div that an `{lmd}` cell builds from AST nodes (`pandoc.Div` + `pandoc.BulletList`) is never desugared into a `Table` / `DefinitionList`. It reaches the HTML writer as a div containing nested bullet lists. The same markup written literally in the document body converts fine.

The desugaring lives in the reader's postprocess step (`pampa/src/pandoc/treesitter_utils/postprocess.rs`, `transform_divs` / `validate_list_table_div` / `is_valid_definition_list_div`), so it only ever sees blocks that came out of the qmd reader. Blocks that lmd cells return at `lmd-execute` (which runs after the engine, before `ast-transforms`) are spliced in without that step. The natural fix seems to be running the same div transform over each cell's returned blocks (or as a stage right after `lmd-execute`); `transform_divs` is already public and used from `pampa`'s CLI.

This matters for the use lmd was built for: a Lua function that builds a table from data (porting an Astro/Hugo "ConfigTable"-style component) has no clean way to produce a table. Building a `pandoc.Table` by hand is far more verbose than the list-table div; `pandoc.read` of generated markdown works but defeats the point of building nodes.

## Repro

`repro.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: list-table and definition-list divs from lmd
---

## 1. Literal list-table (control)

::: {.list-table}
* - Key
  - Value
* - `a`
  - one
:::

## 2. list-table div built from AST nodes in an lmd cell

```{lmd}
local function row(cells)
  local items = {}
  for _, c in ipairs(cells) do table.insert(items, { pandoc.Plain(c) }) end
  return { pandoc.BulletList(items) }
end
local rows = {
  row({ {pandoc.Str("Key")}, {pandoc.Str("Value")} }),
  row({ {pandoc.Code("b")}, {pandoc.Str("two")} }),
}
return pandoc.Div({ pandoc.BulletList(rows) }, pandoc.Attr("", {"list-table"}))
```

## 3. Literal definition-list (control)

::: {.definition-list}
* Term
  * A definition.
:::

## 4. definition-list div built from AST nodes in an lmd cell

```{lmd}
local item = {
  pandoc.Plain({ pandoc.Str("Term") }),
  pandoc.BulletList({ { pandoc.Plain({ pandoc.Str("A definition.") }) } }),
}
return pandoc.Div({ pandoc.BulletList({ item }) }, pandoc.Attr("", {"definition-list"}))
```
````

```sh
q2 render repro.qmd --to html
```

Renders without diagnostics. In `repro.html`:

| Section | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| 1. literal list-table | `<table>` | `<table>` |
| 2. AST-built list-table | `<table>` | `<div class="list-table"><ul><li><ul>…` |
| 3. literal definition-list | `<dl>` | `<dl>` |
| 4. AST-built definition-list | `<dl>` | `<div class="definition-list"><ul><li>…` |

The node shapes in 2 and 4 match what the reader produces for 1 and 3 before postprocess (the validators' documented structure), so once `transform_divs` runs over them they should convert.

## Related: the same markup inside a markdown fragment

The obvious workaround, writing the list-table literally inside a fragment, is also blocked, for the opposite reason: the fragment *is* parsed by the reader with postprocess, so it becomes a `Table`, and the desugarer then reports

```
Warning: lmd cell could not be desugared
  lmd: `Table` nodes are not supported inside markdown fragments yet
  The cell is left as written and will not run.
```

for

````qmd
```{lmd}
return {=:
::: {.list-table}
* - Key
  - Value
* - `b`
  - two
:::
:=}
```
````

So today the only route from an lmd cell to a table is `pandoc.read(markdown_string, "markdown")`, which does run postprocess and produces a table.

## Environment

`q2 0.33.0` (macOS, arm64); repo inspected at `e308835bd`.

title: Monitor wasm-pack: cargo install broken by zip crate mass-yank; CI uses taiki-e prebuilt binary
description:
## Summary

Our CI installs `wasm-pack` via `taiki-e/install-action@wasm-pack` (prebuilt binary) instead of `cargo install wasm-pack`, because `cargo install wasm-pack` stopped working on 2026-10-16. This issue tracks the upstream situation so we know when (and whether) to revisit.

Upstream tracking issue: https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack/issues/1608

## What happened

On 2026-10-16 the `zip` crate maintainers yanked every published version except 9.0.3 and 9.0.4 (134 of 136 versions), ahead of publishing security advisories. See [zip-rs/zip2#1075](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/issues/1075). The advisories cited so far:

- [GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627): SUID/SGID bits preserved on extraction
- [GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26): `ZipArchive::extract` creates symlinks pointing outside the destination
- [GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp): Unix permissions applied through symlinks on extract

The maintainer said more advisories will be published later this month.

`wasm-pack 0.15.0` depends on `binary-install 0.4.1`, which requires `zip ^2.1.3`. No unyanked 2.x exists, so a fresh `cargo install wasm-pack` fails to resolve. `binary-install` is archived, so a fix has to come from wasm-pack itself.

## Why the prebuilt binary is acceptable for now

The taiki-e binary is the same wasm-pack 0.15.0 source, built with `zip 2.4.2` from wasm-pack's own lockfile, so the vulnerable zip code is present. Practical exposure in our CI is low:

- `binary-install` never calls the high-level `ZipArchive::extract` API the advisories are about. It walks entries itself, filters with `enclosed_name()`, and writes only the specific binaries it wants with a fixed 0755 mode.
- wasm-pack only reaches the zip code path for Windows binaryen downloads and chromedriver (`wasm-pack test`). Everything else it fetches is `.tar.gz`.
- Our workflows preinstall both tools wasm-pack would otherwise download (`wasm-bindgen-cli` at the lockfile version via cargo, `binaryen@132.0.0` via npm). wasm-pack prefers PATH copies when versions match, so in CI it downloads nothing.

## What to watch for

- A wasm-pack release that drops or replaces `binary-install` (resolving the upstream issue above). Once it ships, the taiki-e manifest picks it up automatically since we don't pin a version.
- The additional zip advisories the maintainer said are coming. If any affect the entry-iteration path (not just `extract()`), re-evaluate the "low exposure" reasoning above.
- Whether we want to pin `taiki-e/install-action` to a commit SHA for supply-chain hygiene (independent of the zip question).

## Related

Our own `zip` dependency was bumped from 6.0.0 (also yanked) to 9.0.4 in the same change that switched the workflows.

title: Computational figure filenames regress to positional auto-naming, losing Q1's label-based stability (knitr; Jupyter has the same gap unimplemented)
description:
### Summary

Computational figure filenames lose their label-based stability compared to Quarto 1.x. In Quarto 1.x, a labelled executable chunk's output filename is derived from the author's `label:` option — `#| label: fig-cars` on an R chunk yields `fig-cars-1.svg`; the same principle applies to Jupyter, which names outputs `<label>-output-<n>.<ext>` (e.g. `fig-visualization-output-1.png`). Different concatenation convention per engine, but in both cases **the label, not the chunk's position in the document, determines the artifact's filename** — which is what makes the name stable across edits (reordering sections, inserting a chunk earlier in the file, etc. doesn't change it).

In q2, the knitr chunk's `label:` option never reaches the engine — it's consumed upstream (to drive q2's own crossref numbering) and stripped from the code text before knitr ever executes it. knitr falls back to its generic positional default, the same name it would produce for an *unlabelled* chunk (`unnamed-chunk-1-1.svg` instead of `fig-cars-1.svg`), even though the chunk is labelled. Any file or document that references the artifact by its expected, label-derived name breaks.

### Reproduction

`chapter1.qmd`:

```r
```{r}
#| label: fig-cars
#| fig-cap: "A plot of the cars dataset"
plot(cars)
```
```

Another file in the same project hand-references the artifact chapter1 produces, exactly as Quarto 1.x would name it:

```markdown
![First appendix panel](chapter1_files/figure-typst/fig-cars-1.svg){#fig-appendix-panel-a}
```

**Expected** (matches `quarto render`, Quarto 1.x): `chapter1.qmd` execution produces `chapter1_files/figure-typst/fig-cars-1.svg`, and the reference above resolves.

**Observed** (`q2 render`): the same chunk instead produces `chapter1_files/figure-typst/unnamed-chunk-1-1.svg`. The hand-authored reference to `fig-cars-1.svg` now points at a file that doesn't exist, which fails at compile time (missing-image error) for any format that isn't forgiving about broken image links (e.g. Typst).

Found via the `typst-testing/p8-orange-book-base` smoke-all fixture (`crates/quarto/tests/smoke-all/typst/orange-book/`), which reuses the same figure across `chapter2.qmd`, `appendix.qmd`, and `appendix-b.qmd` by referencing it directly by its expected filename — a pattern Quarto 1.x's naming convention is specifically designed to support.

### Why this matters beyond the immediate 404

Stable, label-derived artifact filenames are a real, relied-upon Quarto 1.x behavior — they let other documents, includes, and hand-authored references point at a generated artifact by a name that won't shift as the document changes. Falling back to positional auto-naming (`unnamed-chunk-N`) removes that guarantee silently: the render succeeds for the originating document and only breaks downstream, wherever something else references the artifact by name.

### Tracking

Root-caused and being fixed via internal strand `bd-2lxj10z0`.

title: Writer emits decoded entity characters raw, so ZeroWidthSpace output fails to re-parse
description:
Since the named-entity decode (bd-named-entities-w6xbfftj, #488) the reader folds `​` into a `Str` as a literal U+200B, but the qmd writer emits that character verbatim instead of re-encoding it as an entity or numeric reference. U+200B is not accepted by the grammar's prose regexes (PANDOC_COMBINING_MARKS covers only `\p{M}` plus ZWNJ/ZWJ), so pampa's own output fails to re-parse; inside a heading superscript the failure cascades into an unclosed-superscript error and spurious fenced-div close errors.

````
$ printf -- 'a​b\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
[ Para [Str "a​b"] ]

$ printf -- 'a​b\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
a​b

$ printf -- 'a​b\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>/dev/null | od -c | head -2
0000000    a 342 200 213   b  \n
0000006

$ printf -- 'a​b\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>/dev/null | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
Error: Parse error
   ╭─[ <stdin>:1:2 ]
   │
 1 │ a​b
   │    
   │  ── unexpected character or token here
───╯
````

In the wild:
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/index.qmd#L26

title: An em dash in a frontmatter value is written as `---`, which truncates the YAML on re-read
description:
Since #290 the qmd writer emits every em dash in a markdown-parsed frontmatter string as `---`. The reader then cuts the YAML at that point: `extract_between_delimiters` in `crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs` splits the `quarto_minus_metadata` text on every `---` and keeps the second piece, so a `---` anywhere inside a value ends the block there instead of only at the closing delimiter line. How that surfaces depends on the scalar shape the writer chose. A single-line value is written as a plain scalar, so the re-read keeps the text before the dash, drops every later key, and raises no diagnostic. A multi-line value is written as a double-quoted scalar with `\n` escapes, so the cut leaves the quote unterminated and the re-read fails with `Q-0-99`. A `---` typed directly into a value hits the same split without the writer's help.

#### Single-line value, silent truncation on re-read:

````
$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "Hello — world"\nauthor: Z\n---\n\nx\n'
---
description: "Hello — world"
author: Z
---

x

$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "Hello — world"\nauthor: Z\n---\n\nx\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
---
description: Hello --- world
author: Z
---

x

$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "Hello — world"\nauthor: Z\n---\n\nx\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>/dev/null | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
[ Para [Str "x"] ]

$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "Hello — world"\nauthor: Z\n---\n\nx\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>/dev/null | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t json 2>/dev/null | jq -c .meta
{"description":{"c":[{"c":"Hello","s":7,"t":"Str"}],"s":4,"t":"MetaInlines"}}
````

#### Multi-line value, `Q-0-99` on re-read:

````
$ printf -- '---\ndescription: |\n  Hello —\n  world.\n---\n\nx\n'
---
description: |
  Hello —
  world.
---

x

$ printf -- '---\ndescription: |\n  Hello —\n  world.\n---\n\nx\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
---
description: "Hello ---\nworld."
---

x

$ printf -- '---\ndescription: |\n  Hello —\n  world.\n---\n\nx\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1 | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
Error: [Q-0-99] Failed to parse YAML frontmatter: Parse error: while scanning a quoted scalar, found unexpected end of stream at byte 13 line 1 column 14
 2 │ description: "Hello ---\nworld."
````

#### A `---` typed directly into a value, reader only:

````
$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "a --- b"\n---\n\nx\n'
---
description: "a --- b"
---

x

$ printf -- '---\ndescription: "a --- b"\n---\n\nx\n' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
Error: [Q-0-99] Failed to parse YAML frontmatter: Parse error: while scanning a quoted scalar, found unexpected end of stream at byte 13 line 1 column 14
 2 │ description: "a --- b"
````

In-the-wild occurrence in `quarto-dev/quarto-web`. This is the multi-line form: the em dash on line 4 reads fine, the writer emits it as `---` inside a double-quoted scalar, and the re-read errors. It is the only em dash in any quarto-web frontmatter, so the silent single-line form has no in-the-wild case there.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/acb4d86cc60763908d4f6f68f713c3760fd4a98b/docs/blog/_archive/posts/2026-04-14-chrome-headless-shell/index.qmd#L4

title: `tree-sitter-qmd` - grid table detection and specific errors
description:
My current understanding is that grid tables will not be supported by the parser and users should migrate away via qmd-syntax-helper. If that is not the case feel free close and ignore the following. 

Currently at best a grid table will parse as a sequence of paragraphs containing literal `+`, `-`, `|` runs. If exported as qmd the output is escaped and the grid table syntax is broken.

Alternatively, often the parser gets confused by the syntax and will throw an unrelated error due to unclosed / unpaired delimiters or other perceived issues.

Would it be possible to include a basic "detector" in the parser that identifies a block of text as a grid table, consumes the entire block without trying to further parse things and then emit a parser error specific to not supporting grid tables.

It seems reasonable to be able to recognize the `+[-=+]{3,}+` opening border followed by `|`-delimited cell rows and the matching closing border, but I'm sure there are plenty of edge cases.


Below are a couple examples of the current parsing issues:

### paragraph fallback

```

title: q2 preview (CLI) silently ignores render-components: — feature is hub-client-only
description:
Tracked internally as braid strand **bd-ue80chl0** (discovered during the mermaid work, bd-5m4ga0s1 / #401). Filing here for visibility since the fix belongs with the render-components feature.

## Symptom

A document with a `render-components:` entry in its front matter loads user TSX component overrides in **hub-client**, but under **`q2 preview`** (the CLI) the entries are silently dropped — no warning, no error, the built-in components just render instead. The two preview surfaces diverge without any signal to the author.

How it surfaced: verifying a prototype doc that overrides `CodeBlock` via `render-components`. Under `q2 preview` the diagram rendered with the *built-in* mermaid component's markers (`quarto-mermaid-…` SVG id, `mermaid-diagram` class) rather than the prototype's (`mmd-…` id, inline styles) — the user override never loaded.

## Why it happens

The custom-components pipeline is a two-process design:

1. A **parent** reads `render-components` from the document meta, resolves the TSX paths, transpiles them with `@babel/standalone`, and posts the compiled code into the sandboxed iframe via a `LOAD_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS` message.
2. The **iframe** (shared `@quarto/preview-renderer` package, `q2-preview/entry.tsx` → `loadCustomComponents`) imports the code as blob ESM modules and layers the exports over the built-in registry (`mergedPreviewRegistry`).

The iframe half is shared between hub-client and the CLI preview SPA and fully supports the feature. **Only hub-client implements the parent half** (`hub-client/src/components/render/ReactRenderer.tsx`: meta walk → `resolveComponentPath` → `transpileTSX` → `customComponentsCode` prop). The CLI SPA's parent (`q2-preview-spa/src/PreviewApp.tsx`) never passes `customComponentsCode` to `Q2PreviewIframe` at all — it doesn't read the YAML key and has no transpiler in its bundle.

## Impact

- Documents authored against hub-client's render-components behavior render differently (built-ins only) under `q2 preview`, silently.
- Pre-existing; unrelated to #401 (which actually softened the mermaid-specific case: the built-in mermaid component now renders diagrams the dropped override used to handle).

## Possible resolutions

1. **Implement the parent half in the CLI SPA**: read `render-components` from the AST meta, fetch TSX sources from the preview file server, transpile, and post the same `LOAD_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS` message hub-client sends. Cost: `@babel/standalone` is a heavy addition to the SPA bundle — precompiling server-side in the Rust preview binary is an alternative worth weighing.
2. **Declare the feature hub-client-only** and document it — and ideally emit a visible warning in `q2 preview` when a document carries `render-components`, so the divergence is at least no longer silent.

title: brand: inline `brand:` block in document front matter always fails with Q-14-1
description:
## Bug description

Any inline `brand:` block in the YAML front matter of a `.qmd` fails with `[Q-14-1] Invalid theme configuration` and the message "brand block must be plain YAML, not Pandoc inlines/blocks". A single plain colour is enough to trigger it. The same block in `_quarto.yml` renders, so the defect is about the front-matter context, not the block itself.

Front-matter strings are parsed as markdown and stored as `PandocInlines`. The reader that handles a `brand:` path tolerates that variant; the walker that rebuilds plain YAML for an inline block rejects it.

The same markdown parsing has a second effect: `brand: _brand.yml` in front matter renders, but emits a `Q-1-20` warning, because the leading underscore of `_brand.yml` is read as an unclosed emphasis mark. This is the same class as #457, for a key that table does not yet cover.

Per-colour `light`/`dark` values are not implemented either. That is #580. This issue hides it whenever the brand is inline, because the error here is raised before the brand is deserialized.

## Steps to reproduce

An inline block, with no light or dark involved.

````qmd
---
format: html
brand:
  color:
    background: "#b22222"
---

Hello.
````

```bash
q2 render index.qmd
```

The documented brand-file form, which warrants the second half of this report.

````qmd
---
format: html
brand: _brand.yml
---

Hello.
````

## Actual behavior

The inline block fails, with the span on the colour value.

```text
Rendering single file: /work/index.qmd
Error: [Q-14-1] Invalid theme configuration
   ╭─[ /work/index.qmd:5:17 ]
   │
 5 │     background: "#b22222"
   │                 ────┬────
   │                     ╰────── brand block must be plain YAML, not Pandoc inlines/blocks
───╯

1 error
```

The same block in `_quarto.yml` renders, and the generated stylesheet contains `--bs-body-bg: #b22222`.

The brand-file form renders and warns.

```text
Rendering single file: /work/index.qmd
Warning: [Q-1-20] Failed to parse metadata value as markdown
   ╭─[ /work/index.qmd:3:8 ]
   │
 3 │ brand: _brand.yml
   │        ┬────┬────┬
   │        ╰──────────── This is the opening '_' mark.
   │             │    │
   │             ╰─────── Could not parse '_brand.yml' as markdown
   │                  │
   │                  ╰── I reached the end of the block before finding a closing '_' for the emphasis.
───╯
ℹ [Q-2-5] Unclosed Underscore Emphasis
ℹ Add the `!str` tag to treat this as a plain string, or fix the markdown syntax

1 warning
```

## Expected behavior

An inline `brand:` block in front matter renders as the same block in `_quarto.yml` does, and `brand: _brand.yml` produces no warning. Brand values are machine-facing configuration and are not markdown.

## Your environment

- Docker image.
- Host: macOS 15 (darwin 25.6.0), arm64.
- Source read at `main` `328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1`, unchanged since `v0.26.0` for every file cited below.

## Root cause

Front matter is converted by `rawblock_to_config_value` with `InterpretationContext::DocumentMetadata`.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs#L548-L551

In that context an untagged string with no key-path annotation takes the context default and is parsed as markdown.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs#L410-L420

A successful parse of a single paragraph yields `ConfigValueKind::PandocInlines`, which is what every leaf of the brand block becomes.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/pandoc/meta.rs#L169-L175

`extract_single_brand_ref` reads that value in one of two ways. The path form goes through `config_value_as_text`, which falls back to `as_plain_text()` and therefore accepts `PandocInlines`. That is why `brand: _brand.yml` still works, and why its markdown warning is the only trace left.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs#L649-L657
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs#L719-L749

The inline form instead calls `config_value_to_yaml_value`, which walks the typed tree and treats `PandocInlines` as an error. This is where `Q-14-1` is raised, at the colour leaf.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs#L760-L791

`_quarto.yml` is unaffected because project config is read with `InterpretationContext::ProjectConfig`, which keeps strings as `Scalar(String)`.

Because the leaves really are parsed as markdown, a brand value containing `*` or `_` is rewritten before anything downstream sees it. The `Q-1-20` warning is the visible half of that; a value that parses cleanly is changed silently.

The documented inline example is here.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/docs/guides/authoring/brand.qmd#L113-L121

title: lua: resolve_path returns a different directory inside a loaded file
description:
## Bug description

`quarto.utils.resolve_path` resolves a relative path against the current script directory. Quarto 1 keeps the extension root in effect for the whole extension. q2 moves the script directory to whichever file is executing, so a relative path inside a file that the extension loaded gains a segment: `_modules/greet.lua` comes back as `_modules/_modules/greet.lua`.

Nothing errors. `resolve_path` returns a path, it just points at a file that does not exist, so the failure surfaces later and somewhere else.

## Current state

`resolve_path("_modules/greet.lua")`, called from one extension:

| Called from | Quarto 1 | q2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the top-level script | `_modules/greet.lua` | `_modules/greet.lua` |
| a file the script loaded | `_modules/greet.lua` | **`_modules/_modules/greet.lua`** |

Every other call site agrees between the two engines: filter load time and call time, shortcode load time and call time, and paths into a subdirectory.

## Steps to reproduce

Reproduction: https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-issues-experiments/tree/main/q2-588

The extension contributes a shortcode rather than a filter, because a q2 filter cannot load a sibling file at all. See #587.

`_extensions/rp/_modules/probe.lua` records what `resolve_path` returns at load time:

```lua
return { resolved = quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/greet.lua") }
```

`_extensions/rp/rp.lua` asks the same question from the top-level script and from the loaded file:

```lua
local top = quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/greet.lua")
local by_require = require("_modules/probe").resolved
local by_dofile = dofile(quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/probe.lua")).resolved
```

```bash
q2 render index.qmd --to html
```

## Actual behavior

```text
top-level  : /work/_extensions/rp/_modules/greet.lua            exists
via-require: /work/_extensions/rp/_modules/_modules/greet.lua   MISSING
via-dofile : /work/_extensions/rp/_modules/greet.lua            exists
```

Quarto 1 returns the same existing path on all three rows.

The third row is a control. It shows that q2 already returns the extension root from inside a loaded file when the file is loaded with `dofile`, and is explained under Root cause.

## Expected behavior

`resolve_path` returns the same path from both call sites, resolved against the extension root, as Quarto 1 does.

## Your environment

- Docker image `quarto-dev/q2:0.26.0`.
- Host: macOS 15 (darwin 25.6.0), arm64.
- Quarto 1 compared at 99.9.9, local build of `abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7`.
- Source read at `main` `328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1`, unchanged since `v0.26.0` for every file cited below.

## Root cause

`resolve_path` joins its argument onto the top of the script-dir stack.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs#L490-L511

`register_scoped_require` pushes the loaded file's own directory onto that same stack while the file executes, and pops it afterwards. That push is what moves the script directory.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs#L260-L271

Quarto 1 never changes the script directory when it loads a file. Its `scriptFile` stack moves only for shortcodes and wrapped filters, so the extension root stays in effect inside a loaded file.

q2 already settled this contract for `dofile` in #112, where the push and pop were removed. The header comment in `dofile_wasm.rs` still records it: the overrides handle file input and output only, and do not modify the script-dir stack. That is why the `dofile` row above is correct.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/lua/dofile_wasm.rs#L1-L14

Commit `6ff4221e` (#450) added `register_scoped_require` after this decision. With this function, a loaded file can load the other files in the same directory by name alone. To do this, the function puts the directory of the loaded file on the script-dir stack. This is the same stack movement that #112 removed from `dofile`. `resolve_path` reads the same stack. As a result, the movement also changes the path that `resolve_path` returns.

title: lua: require is unavailable in Lua filters, but works in shortcodes
description:
## Bug description

Extensions commonly split a filter across several `.lua` files and load them with `require`. Nothing about those files is special: they are plain Lua files shipped inside the extension directory, sitting next to the filter script, conventionally under `_modules/`.

A Lua filter contributed by an extension cannot load them. The same `require` line in a shortcode script, in the same extension, resolves, and Quarto 1 resolves it on both paths.

The filter environment does not install the script-directory aware `require`, so a filter runs with the stock Lua `require` and an untouched `package.path`.

`quarto.utils.resolve_path` itself is unaffected and returns the same correct absolute path under both engines. `dofile(quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/greet.lua"))` loads the file in a filter and in a shortcode alike, on Quarto 1 and on q2, so it stands in for `require` in an extension's top-level script.

## Current state

| Loader | Quarto 1 filter | Quarto 1 shortcode | q2 filter | q2 shortcode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `require("_modules/greet")` | works | works | **fails** | works |
| `dofile(quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/greet.lua"))` | works | works | works | works |

The absolute form `require(quarto.utils.resolve_path("_modules/greet.lua"):gsub("%.lua$", ""))`, which extensions commonly use, fails in a q2 filter for the same reason.

## Steps to reproduce

Reproduction: https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-issues-experiments/tree/main/q2-587

One extension contributes both a filter and a shortcode. Each runs the same line.

`_modules/greet.lua` is an ordinary Lua file in the extension directory. The `_modules/` folder is a naming convention, nothing more.

`_extensions/parity/_modules/greet.lua`:

```lua
return {
  greeting = function()
    return "greet-module-loaded"
  end,
}
```

`_extensions/parity/parity-filter-strict.lua`:

```lua
local mod = require("_modules/greet")

return {
  {
    Pandoc = function(doc)
      doc.blocks:insert(pandoc.Para(pandoc.Str("filter-require: OK " .. mod.greeting())))
      return doc
    end,
  },
}
```

```bash
q2 render index-strict.qmd --to html
```

## Actual behavior

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD010 -- verbatim q2 output, tabs kept as emitted -->

```text
Rendering single file: /work/index-strict.qmd
Error: Lua filter error: runtime error: [string "/work/_extensions/parity/parity-filter-strict..."]:6: module '_modules/greet' not found:
	no field package.preload['_modules/greet']
	no file '/usr/local/share/lua/5.4/_modules/greet.lua'
	no file '/usr/local/share/lua/5.4/_modules/greet/init.lua'
	no file '/usr/local/lib/lua/5.4/_modules/greet.lua'
	no file '/usr/local/lib/lua/5.4/_modules/greet/init.lua'
	no file './_modules/greet.lua'
	no file './_modules/greet/init.lua'

	can't load C modules in safe mode
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD010 -->

The searcher list is the stock Lua one. No Quarto entry appears in it.

`index.qmd` runs both paths in one render, each `require` wrapped in `pcall`, and writes the verdicts into the document:

```text
filter-require: FAIL
shortcode-require: OK greet-module-loaded
```

Quarto 1 reports `OK greet-module-loaded` on both lines.

## Expected behavior

The filter loads the file, as the shortcode already does and as Quarto 1 does on both paths.

## Your environment

- Docker image `quarto-dev/q2:0.26.0`.
- Host: macOS 15 (darwin 25.6.0), arm64.
- Quarto 1 compared at 99.9.9, local build of `abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7`.
- Source read at `main` `328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1`, unchanged since `v0.26.0` for every file cited below.

## Root cause (LLM)

`register_scoped_require` installs the script-directory aware loader, which resolves a file against the script-dir stack.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/lua/quarto_api.rs#L206-L306

It is registered in the shortcode environment.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/lua/shortcode.rs#L115-L118

`create_filter_environment` registers the `quarto` API, the attribution stubs, and `quarto.doc`, then pushes the script directory that `resolve_path` reads. It does not register the loader.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/pampa/src/lua/filter.rs#L160-L181

Filters are not staged into a temporary directory, so the file sits next to the filter and the pushed script directory is correct.

title: brand: per-colour `light`/`dark` values are documented but not implemented
description:
## Bug description

The brand documentation says that any colour in `color` or `typography` may be given as an object with `light` and `dark` keys. No such shape exists in the type model, so a brand that uses it fails to render. `BrandColor` fields are `Option<String>` and the struct denies unknown fields, so a map value cannot deserialize. `BrandTypographyOptions.color` has the same shape.

This affects a `_brand.yml` file and an inline `brand:` block alike, because both reach the same deserializer.

The error is also reported without the `Q-14-1` code and without a source snippet, although the message names a line and column in `_brand.yml`.

The light/dark seam itself works: a brand given as two files renders both variants.

An inline `brand:` block in front matter fails earlier, for an unrelated reason, and hides this defect in the inline case. That is #581.

## Steps to reproduce

`_brand.yml`:

```yaml
color:
  background:
    light: "#b22222"
    dark: "#22b222"
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
format: html
brand: _brand.yml
---

Hello.
````

```bash
q2 render index.qmd
```

## Actual behavior

```text
Rendering single file: /work/index.qmd
Error: brand resolution: Invalid theme configuration: failed to parse _brand.yml: color.background: invalid type: map, expected a string at line 3 column 5

1 error
```

Two controls render, which bounds the defect.

The same files with `background: "#b22222"` and no light/dark pair.

Two brand files selected with `brand: {light: light-brand.yml, dark: dark-brand.yml}`, which produces `--bs-body-bg: #b22222` in `index_files/styles.css` and `--bs-body-bg: #22b222` in `index_files/styles-dark.css`.

## Expected behavior

The brand renders, the light value lands in the light stylesheet and the dark value in the dark one, matching what the two-file form already does.

## Your environment

- Docker image.
- Host: macOS 15 (darwin 25.6.0), arm64.
- Source read at `main` `328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1`, unchanged since `v0.26.0` for every file cited below.

## Root cause

`BrandColor` gives every colour slot the type `Option<String>`, and the struct carries `deny_unknown_fields`, so `background: {light: …, dark: …}` has nowhere to go.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs#L128-L164

The typography slot has the same limitation. The one custom deserializer in the crate widens the shorthand `base: Open Sans` into `{family: …}`; it does not accept a light/dark pair, and the colour field it wraps is still `Option<String>`.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs#L290-L311
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-brand/src/types.rs#L318-L349

A `_brand.yml` is handed straight to `serde_yaml`, which is where the map value fails.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-brand/src/lib.rs#L27-L32
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs#L462-L503

The failure is wrapped by `brand_err`, which sets `location: None`.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-sass/src/config.rs#L820-L825

It is then wrapped again as a plain stage error, so it never passes through `sass_error_to_parse_error`, the converter that attaches the `Q-14-1` code and binds the source file for the snippet. The theme-config path in the same stage does use that converter, which is why an inline block reports a code and a span while a brand file does not.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-core/src/stage/stages/compile_theme_css.rs#L495-L500
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/crates/quarto-core/src/theme_diagnostic.rs#L53-L82

The documented example comes from `cc910a26` ("website - brand stub"), a single commit that added 1005 lines to the page, describing Quarto 1 behaviour that Quarto 2 has not ported.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/328e176fb024ef27738cef33f1cf72f8cf1b8ee1/docs/guides/authoring/brand.qmd#L156-L203

title: Wire most workspace TS test suites into CI
description:
### Context
CI currently runs the TypeScript tests for `hub-client` (via `ts-test-suite.yml` → `npm run test:ci`). The other packages in the npm workspace are built in CI but their own test suites aren't run yet. This looks like a leftover from when TS testing first moved into its own workflow (`bf7e8f42`, "attempt to move ts testing into own GHA workflow") — hub-client got wired up and the rest hasn't been added since.

Most of these suites are healthy today, so this is mostly a matter of connecting them up.

### Suites not currently run in CI (checked locally)

Green as-is:
- `preview-renderer` (208), `preview-runtime` (65), `quarto-automerge-schema` (52), `q2-preview-spa` (8), `quarto-sync-client`, `trace-viewer` (10), `wasm-js-bridge` (10), `q2-demos/kanban` (35)

Needs a small touch before gating in:
- `quarto-hub-mcp` — passes except for a couple of deps not installed in my local checkout; likely green under a clean CI `npm ci`
- `sync-test-harness` — one test sensitive to the same sync/peer-connection flakiness we see in e2e
- `annotated-qmd` — 2 of 156 fail; tracked separately (bd-1d6io)

### A couple of related notes
- `*.integration.test.ts` files are excluded from several packages' default `vitest run`, so they don't run anywhere yet (e.g. most of `q2-preview-spa`'s files).
- Rust doctests aren't run either — nextest doesn't execute them and there's no `cargo test --doc` step. Worth a separate decision.

### Suggested direction
Run the workspace suites in CI (e.g. `npm test --workspaces --if-present`), starting with the green ones so CI stays green, and fold in the others as they're ready. The integration-test and doctest items can be handled separately.

title: TS Engines which claim files will spawn Deno in Pass-1
description:
Pass-1 needs to be pure Rust code with no spawning of slow sub-processes such as Deno.

However in the Quarto 1 API, both `claimsFile` and `markdownForFile` are dynamic JavaScript calls with no trivial way to specify them statically.

So if TS engines are used that claim files and convert them, that's happening in Deno today. 

It's slow and error-prone - but at the same time, it's ahead of q2, which does not have spin/percent script, or ipynb support yet.

Structurally,
* #416 

provides the format conversion stage in the pipeline. It's just that it shouldn't spawn Deno.

We'll remove the ability to claim and parse files via TS in the following plans (merged but not fully reviewed or implemented):

* `2026-07-07-plan7a-static-content-pattern-claims.md`
* `2026-07-08-plan7b-native-content-processors.md`
* `2026-07-08-plan7c-ipynb-content-processor.md`

These establish a registry of converters, written in Rust, from a native format to qmd.

Currently those converters are
* spin, via treesitter-r
* percent (porting TS parser from Quarto 1)
* ipynb - new design with provenance but otherwise ported from Quarto 1.

Converters can take extra parameters; e.g. Python and Julia both use percent scripts but look for different languages in them.

title: SPA can fail to update at login page
description:
Repeated logins, even after leaving the page open for an extended period of time, kept producing the old SPA error message (the one from #435). This indicates that the new SW refresh was not being triggered.

Rendered moot for now by https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/pull/446, but this still needs to be investigated.

title: include-in-header resolves relative to each input file, not project root
description:
**Severity:** high — silent content loss, warning only.

In Quarto 1.x, a path in a project-level `_quarto.yml` is resolved relative to the **project root**.
q2 resolves it relative to the **directory of each input file**, so any input in a subdirectory gets
a "file not found" warning and is rendered **without** the header include.

Found while migrating a real website project to q2: with ~90 pages in subdirectories, the analytics
script and a `rel="me"` link ended up silently missing from all of them, while the project still
reported a successful build.

| Environment | Version |
| ----------- | ------- |
| `q2 --version` | `q2 (quarto 2) 0.11.0` |
| `quarto --version` (reference) | `1.10.18` |
| Platform | macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64 |

### Repro

```
p/
├── _quarto.yml
├── custom-header.html
├── index.qmd
└── sub/
    └── index.qmd
```

`_quarto.yml`

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  render:
    - index.qmd
    - sub/index.qmd
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      - custom-header.html
```

`custom-header.html`

```html
<!-- hdr -->
```

`index.qmd` and `sub/index.qmd` are any minimal documents.

```
$ q2 render .
```

### Actual

```
Warning: [Q-5-4] Include file not found
     ╭─[ p/_quarto.yml:10:9 ]
     │
  10 │       - custom-header.html
     │         ─────────┬────────
     │                  ╰────────── Could not read include file 'p/sub/custom-header.html'
     │                              for `include-in-header`: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)
─────╯

Rendered 2 of 2 files to p/_site — 1 warning
```

`_site/sub/index.html` does not contain `<!-- hdr -->`. `quarto 1.10.18` on the same input emits it
in both outputs and produces no warning.

### Expected

The path should resolve relative to the project root (matching `quarto` 1.x behaviour), so
`_site/sub/index.html` also contains `<!-- hdr -->`.

### Notes on workarounds

- A leading slash (`- /custom-header.html`) does **not** help: both engines interpret it as a
  filesystem-absolute path (`quarto` fails with
  `Error resolving header-includes- unable to open file /custom-header.html`).
- A per-directory `_metadata.yml` carrying `include-in-header: ../custom-header.html` **is** honoured
  by q2 for that subdirectory, but in the same test a project-root `_metadata.yml` was **not**
  applied to project-root inputs (`_site/index.html` had no `<!-- hdr -->`, and no warning was
  emitted). That may be a second, separate bug — I did not chase it down.
- The workaround adopted in the affected project is a symlink per subdirectory pointing at the
  project-root file, which satisfies both engines.

title: code-fold: true silently overrides execute: echo: false
description:
### Summary

`code-fold: true` silently overrides `execute: echo: false`. The source is shown even though the author asked to hide it.

Quarto 1.x treats `echo: false` as authoritative — the cell is not echoed at all, and `code-fold` has nothing to fold. In q2 0.20.0 the source block is emitted with syntax highlighting regardless.

This matters for generated reports where the prose is written by code (`IPython.display.Markdown`): the reader gets highlighted source instead of the rendered content, with no warning.

### Reproduction

`fold.qmd`:

```yaml
---
title: t
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
engine: jupyter
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{python}
print("OUTPUT")
```
```

```
q2 render fold.qmd
```

**Observed** — `fold.html` contains both the output and a `<pre class="sourceCode python">` block with the source.

**Expected** — only the output; `echo: false` should win, as in Quarto 1.x.

### Isolation

Without `code-fold: true` the same document honours `echo: false` correctly (no `sourceCode python` in the output), so the two options interact rather than `echo` being broken on its own.

### Environment

- q2 0.20.0 (`q2-0.20.0-darwin_arm64.tar.gz`, checksum verified)
- macOS 15.x, Apple Silicon
- Python 3.14 venv with `jupyter_client`, `nbclient`, `ipykernel`, `matplotlib`; kernel discovered via `JUPYTER_PATH`

### Note on two adjacent observations

While isolating this, two other behaviours differed from Quarto 1.x. Reporting them here as context rather than as separate issues, since they may well be intentional at this stage:

1. A `.qmd` with `{python}` cells and no `engine:` key falls back to the markdown engine and renders without executing anything, silently. Quarto 1.x infers the jupyter engine from the presence of code cells. Adding `engine: jupyter` fixes it. The silent part is what surprised me — nothing in `-v` output says execution was skipped.
2. `embed-resources: true` appears not to be applied yet: the output has no inlined CSS and figures stay as external files in `<stem>_files/`. Assuming this is simply not implemented yet.

title: Listing contents: globs matched against project index instead of listing directory
description:
**Severity:** low — spurious warnings only, output is correct.

A listing in a subdirectory with `contents: ["*.qmd"]` should match `.qmd` files in that
subdirectory. q2 appears to expand the glob against the whole project index and then re-prefix the
matches with the listing's directory, producing entries that never existed and then warning that
they are missing.

Found while migrating a real website project to q2, where this produced ~20 spurious `[Q-13-4]`
warnings, one per (project-root page × listing directory) combination.

| Environment | Version |
| ----------- | ------- |
| `q2 --version` | `q2 (quarto 2) 0.11.0` |
| `quarto --version` (reference) | `1.10.18` |
| Platform | macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64 |

### Repro

```
p/
├── _quarto.yml
├── index.qmd
├── about.qmd
└── sub/
    ├── index.qmd
    └── p1.qmd
```

`_quarto.yml`

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  render:
    - index.qmd
    - about.qmd
    - sub/index.qmd
    - sub/*.qmd
```

`sub/index.qmd`

```yaml
---
title: Sub
listing:
  contents:
    - "*.qmd"
    - "!index.qmd"
---
```

`sub/p1.qmd` is any minimal document with a `date:`. `about.qmd` lives at the project root and is
never referenced from `sub/`.

```
$ q2 render .
```

### Actual

```
Warning [Q-13-4]: Body link references missing document
'sub/about.qmd' is not in the project index.
ℹ Check the spelling, or confirm the target file is included in the render set.
```

(emitted twice)

### Expected

No warning. The glob should resolve within `sub/`, and `about.qmd` at the project root is unrelated
to the listing.

title: [Q-1-20] Failed to parse metadata value as markdown fires on structural YAML (paths/globs)
description:
**Severity:** low — spurious warnings only.

Several YAML keys hold **paths and globs**, not prose, and should never be parsed as markdown.
q2 warns on them and suggests adding `!str`, which would be an unusual thing to write into an
ordinary `_quarto.yml` / frontmatter.

Found while migrating a real website project to q2.

| Environment | Version |
| ----------- | ------- |
| `q2 --version` | `q2 (quarto 2) 0.11.0` |
| `quarto --version` (reference) | `1.10.18` |
| Platform | macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64 |

### Repro A — `metadata-files`

```yaml
---
title: Imprint
metadata-files:
  - _metadata/legal-page-metadata.yml
---
```

```
Warning: [Q-1-20] Failed to parse metadata value as markdown
 4 │   - _metadata/legal-page-metadata.yml
   │                     ╰────────────────── Could not parse
   │                        '_metadata/legal-page-metadata.yml' as markdown
ℹ Add the `!str` tag to treat this as a plain string, or fix the markdown syntax
```

### Repro B — listing `contents` glob

```yaml
---
title: Publications
listing:
  contents:
    - "*.qmd"
    - "!index.qmd"
---
```

```
Warning: [Q-1-20] Failed to parse metadata value as markdown
 6 │     - "*.qmd"
   │       ──┬──
   │         ╰──── Could not parse '*.qmd' as markdown
```

### Expected

Structural keys (`metadata-files`, `listing.contents`, and similar path/glob-valued fields) should
be excluded from markdown parsing.

description:

title: feature: "raw" JSON format
description:
`pampa`'s `-t native` and `-t json` are written with Pandoc in mind, and so they don't support pampa's syntax extensions:

````
$ echo 'Hello. {#free-floating-attribute} Here?' | pampa -t json
Error: [Q-3-32] Standalone attribute not supported in JSON format
   ╭─[ <stdin>:1:9 ]
   │
 1 │ Hello. {#free-floating-attribute} Here?
   │         ────────────┬───────────
   │                     ╰───────────── Cannot render standalone attributes in JSON format
───╯
✖ Standalone attributes should be attached to elements during parsing
ℹ This may indicate a parsing issue or unsupported syntax

$ echo 'Hello. {#free-floating-attribute} Here?' | pampa -t native
Error: [Q-3-32] Standalone attributes not supported in native format
   ╭─[ <stdin>:1:9 ]
   │
 1 │ Hello. {#free-floating-attribute} Here?
   │         ────────────┬───────────
   │                     ╰───────────── Cannot render standalone attribute in native format
───╯
✖ Standalone attributes (e.g., in table cells or headings) are not representable in Pandoc's native format
ℹ Use JSON output format to see attribute details
````

As a result, we don't have any "parserless syntax" for those extensions. We need to fix this.

title: code highlighting and WYSIWYG thoughts
description:
1. Vscode/monaco themes are the same as [“text mate themes”](https://macromates.com/manual/en/themes)
2. Textmate themes are very expressive (although still depend on how languages annotate spans on code blocks), its probably possible to convert themes from other theming systems into text mate themes, but not vice versa
3. I want WYSIWYG to be possible (editor looks identical to rendered) and using text mate themes with Monaco for editing and e.g. [Shiki for rendering](https://shiki.matsu.io/packages/monaco) would work. Alternatively, If we want true WYSIWYG we could render code blocks using non-editable monaco editors, although that would be sort of wasteful of people's computational resources.
4. In general, I advocate for us to think about how renderable things can be edited and to put that rendering and editing tech into user space so we can make it user customizable and extensible

title: `detect_error` dedup loses specific Q-codes when GLR has forked earlier in the parse
description:
It is possible to create circumstances where the tree sitter parser detects multiple errors at the same location - claude believes that this is occuring due to the GLR engine forking due to earlier errors (but I have not verified this).

The issue then becomes the errors with the same  `(row, column)` are deduplicated in a way that neither `state` nor `sym` is taken into account. As a result, when the surviving versions disagree on lookahead, the dedup picks one essentially arbitrarily and this can result in a generic "Parse error" rather than a more specific Q-code from the corpus. 

I am not sure if it is possible to construct a situation where multiple errors with distinct Q-codes can be generated and how that should be handled.


## Example

```
# Heading {key=val .class}

Second *bad paragraph.
```

```bash
printf  "%s\n" "# Heading {key=val .class}" "" "Second *bad paragraph." \
  | pampa --no-prune-errors -t native
```

```
Error: [Q-2-3] Key-value Pair Before Class Specifier in Attribute
   ╭─[ <stdin>:1:20 ]
   │
 1 │ # Heading {key=val .class}
   │            ───┬─── ───┬──
   │               ╰──────────── This key-value pair cannot appear before the class specifier.
   │                       │
   │                       ╰──── This class specifier appears after the key-value pair.
───╯

Error: Parse error
   ╭─[ <stdin>:3:23 ]
   │
 3 │ Second *bad paragraph.
   │                       ┬
   │                       ╰── unexpected character or token here
───╯
```

## Control

```
First good paragraph.

Second *bad paragraph.
```

```bash
printf  "%s\n" "First good paragraph." "" "Second *bad paragraph." \
  | pampa --no-prune-errors -t native
```

```
Error: [Q-2-12] Unclosed Star Emphasis
   ╭─[ <stdin>:3:23 ]
   │
 3 │ Second *bad paragraph.
   │ ───┬──                ┬
   │    ╰───────────────────── This is the opening '*' mark.
   │                       │
   │                       ╰── I reached the end of the block before finding a closing '*' for the emphasis.
───╯
```

## Claude's assessment on what is happening under the hood

Running pampa with `-v` on the reproduction input shows that after the attribute-list error in paragraph 1, GLR forks:

```
detect_error lookahead:attribute_class
recover_to_previous state:2590, depth:2
process version:0, version_count:2, state:0, row:0, col:25
process version:1, version_count:2, state:2590, row:0, col:19
```

Both versions continue parsing forward through the blank line and into paragraph 3, and both reach the unclosed `*` at the same source position. Each emits its own `detect_error` event:

```
process version:0, version_count:2, state:1922, row:2, col:22
detect_error lookahead:_commonmark_single_quote_string_token2

process version:1, version_count:2, state:1922, row:2, col:22
detect_error lookahead:_close_block
```

Both events have `(state=1922, row=2, col=22)` but different lookahead symbols:

- version 0: `(state=1922, sym=_commonmark_single_quote_string_token2)` — no entry in `crates/pampa/resources/error-corpus/_autogen-table.json`, so Merr falls through to the generic "Parse error" fallback at `error_generation.rs:243-249`.
- version 1: `(state=1922, sym=_close_block)` — matches the `Q-2-12` corpus entry at `_autogen-table.json` line ~2236 and would produce the specific diagnostic seen in the control case.

The collector in `produce_diagnostic_messages` (`error_generation.rs:39-62`) is:

```rust
let mut seen_errors: HashSet<(usize, usize)> = HashSet::new();
for parse in &tree_sitter_log.parses {
    for process_log in parse.processes.values() {
        for state in process_log.error_states.iter() {
            if seen_errors.contains(&(state.row, state.column)) {
                continue;
            }
            seen_errors.insert((state.row, state.column));
            ...
```

The dedup key is just `(row, column)`. Whichever GLR version's `detect_error` event is visited first in the HashMap iteration claims that source position; the other version's event is silently dropped before it ever reaches `lookup_error_entry`.

`parse.processes` is a `HashMap<usize, TreeSitterProcessLog>` keyed on GLR version number, iterated via `.values()`. Rust's standard `HashMap` randomizes iteration order across processes, but with only two integer keys (`0` and `1`) on this build the order is effectively pinned in practice — running the reproduction ten times in a row produces the generic "Parse error" output every time, indicating version 0 (the non-corpus-matching version) consistently wins the dedup.

title: pampa - certain parse errors prevent recovery into subsequent blocks, suppressing all later diagnostics
description:
The underlying issue appears to be that for certain error types the parser cannot recover to continue parsing subsequent blocks. Once such an error is hit, no useful diagnostics are produced for the remainder of the document, including additional errors in the same block and any errors in later blocks. The first error in the first block typically still gets a specific diagnostic (e.g. `Q-2-5 Unclosed Underscore Emphasis`), but everything after it is silently dropped.

For inline constructs specifically, this should be recoverable in principle. Inline syntax (emphasis, quotes, code spans, etc.) cannot span a block boundary, so an unclosed inline delimiter is fully resolved at the end of its block: the block ends, the delimiter is left unmatched, and parsing of the next block should be able to proceed normally. Recovery does work this way for some error types but not for others. An unclosed inline emphasis in an early block currently halts useful parsing for the rest of the input (Example 1), whereas other error families recover and the parser progresses into later blocks. The attribute-list ordering error in [#230](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/230) is an example of the latter: the parser recovers far enough to flag a later block, even though that case surfaces a separate problem with how the resulting diagnostic is dispatched.

All examples below run on `main`, invoked with `--no-prune-errors -t native` so no diagnostics are filtered.

## Example 1: multiple errors in the same paragraph, plus another error in a second paragraph

```
This is the _first *paragraph_.

This is the _2nd paragraph
```

```bash
printf  "%s\n" "This is the _first *paragraph_." "" "This is the _2nd paragraph" \
  | pampa --no-prune-errors -t native
```

```
Error: [Q-2-5] Unclosed Underscore Emphasis
   ╭─[ <stdin>:1:32 ]
   │
 1 │ This is the _first *paragraph_.
   │            ─┬                  ┬
   │             ╰───────────────────── This is the opening '_' mark.
   │                                │
   │                                ╰── I reached the end of the block before finding a closing '_' for the emphasis.
───╯
```


## Example 2: control — clean first paragraph, unclosed delimiter in the second paragraph

```
First good paragraph.

Second *bad paragraph.
```

```bash
printf  "%s\n" "First good paragraph." "" "Second *bad paragraph." \
  | pampa --no-prune-errors -t native
```

```
Error: [Q-2-12] Unclosed Star Emphasis
   ╭─[ <stdin>:3:23 ]
   │
 3 │ Second *bad paragraph.
   │ ───┬──                ┬
   │    ╰───────────────────── This is the opening '*' mark.
   │                       │
   │                       ╰── I reached the end of the block before finding a closing '*' for the emphasis.
───╯
```

## POC fix

A proof-of-concept fix exists on the forked branch [`poc/downstream-block-diagnostics-reparse`](https://github.com/rundel/q2/tree/poc/downstream-block-diagnostics-reparse). 

It works around the parser limitation at the `pampa` level rather than changing the grammar. When a parse already has errors, it re-parses the document once per remaining failing block, each time masking the already-handled prefix to blank lines (preserving byte offsets and rows) so the next still-broken block becomes the document's first block and reports its own diagnostic. This feels (very) hacky but works - something cleverer with offsets should be possible but would be more work. This surfaces diagnostics per failing block instead of only the first. It is diagnostics-only (no AST recovery), and block resync is based on a blank-line heuristic (which feels fragile but seems to hold up pretty well in practice).

Nothing blows up with the existing tests and based on an automated pass through quarto-web nothing obviously went wrong there either.

Happy to turn this into an actual PR if it seems worth while.

description:
The list of projects for a quarto-hub instance is represented as an automerge document so that users can share their project list across different browsers.

Currently, this management happens entirely at client side. This is operationally the easiest option because it doesn't require server-side management of a (user_id, project_list_document) table.

Unfortunately, this means that LLM agents do not have access to a user's list of projects. This means that a user can't ask an LLM about a project by name (because the LLM doesn't know what projects are available).

title: local-first flow into quarto-hub.com
description:
@vezwork, you have the vision here, please write it out :)

---

When they visit quarto-hub.com for the first time (and subsequent times) people should be able to use quarto-hub.com as a static (offline) app without signing in.  (indexxeddb only storage, no sync server connection)

People will be able to create projects, edit them, preview; generally take advantage of all the front end features of the app without logging in. Once they want to start syncing and sharing, they can choose to sign in. This is an onboarding ramp into signing up for the full syncing(+other server side stuff) features, still giving users good utility, and not costing us almost anything. This is a unique opportunity because we have a mostly local first architecture already, enterprise SaaS apps cannot do this. 

Requires two changes:
1. Remove auth gating, moving auth gating to behind a "I want to start syncing / start sharing" button or something
2. Local project set v.s. central project set. Carlos wants the sync server to store a centralized `user id -> project set` map, for convenience of having the same projects across browsers

description:
Speaker notes defined with `::: {.notes}` appear as regular visible text on the slide instead of being routed to the RevealNotes speaker window.

Minimal example:

```qmd
---
format: revealjs
---

## My slide

Content here.

::: {.notes}
These should be hidden.
:::

`RevealNotes` plugin is loaded in `RevealjsReactAstSlideRenderer.tsx`, but `renderBlock`'s `case 'Div'` has no class guard for `notes` — all divs render unconditionally. Likely affects `format: q2-slides` too.
