title: `renderings: [light, dark]` shows both outputs in HTML, dashboard and Reveal.js
description:
### Bug description

I found this while trying the Quarto CLI metrics dashboard (`quarto-dev/internal-metrics`, internal to the organisation) on q2.
It draws every chart twice with `#| renderings: [light, dark]`, so each figure follows the light and dark toggle.

q2 runs the cell and keeps both outputs, but never chooses between them.
In `html` and `dashboard`, both images show at once, with no `light-content` or `dark-content` class.
In `revealjs`, both images stay on the slide.
`typst` keeps the light image, as Quarto 1 does.

Quarto 1 does the choice in a post filter: HTML gets both outputs with a mode class, and Typst and Reveal.js keep the output for `brand-mode`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/2a6d12a851b255e29a185e15c58f1b0ac6df23c4/src/resources/filters/quarto-post/cell-renderings.lua#L49-L67

edit: The q2 filter catalog marks that filter as not ported, and notes that it needs the `brand-mode` parameter:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/claude-notes/research/2026-07-09-q1-filter-catalog.md?plain=1#L263

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
format: html
---

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

for colour in ("red", "blue"):
    plt.figure()
    plt.plot([1, 2, 3], color=colour)
    plt.show()
```
````

With q2:

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
grep -c '<img' index.html
grep -c 'light-content' index.html
```

With Quarto 1:

```sh
quarto render index.qmd
grep -c '<img' index.html
grep -c 'light-content' index.html
```

Set `format:` to `dashboard`, `revealjs` or `typst` for the other rows below.

### Actual behavior

| Format | Quarto 1 | q2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `html` | 2 images, `light-content` and `dark-content` | 2 images, no class |
| `dashboard` | 2 images, `light-content` and `dark-content` | 2 images, no class |
| `revealjs` | 1 image (light) | 2 images |
| `typst` | 1 image (light) | 1 image (light) |

### Expected behavior

The same choice as Quarto 1.
HTML formats keep both outputs and add `light-content` and `dark-content`, so only the one for the active mode shows.
Reveal.js keeps the output for `brand-mode`, which is `light` by default.
The catalog note suggests this fits the `code-block-generate` and `code-block-render` pair.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: A resource reached through a symbolic link stops an in-place render with "not under any allowed root"
description:
### Bug description

While building a scratch copy of the dashboard from #1131, I linked its shared `assets/` folder instead of copying it.
q2 then refused to render, because the logo sits behind that link.
Nothing needs to be written for that file: in an in-place render, the logo is already where the page expects it.

The output sink already knows this case, and skips a copy whose source and destination are the same file:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/output_sink.rs#L379-L388

The allowed-root check runs first, though.
It resolves the link in the destination's parent folder, finds the real folder outside the root, and stops the render before the skip is reached:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/output_sink.rs#L341-L367

### Steps to reproduce

```text
shared/logo.svg
site/images -> ../shared
site/index.qmd
```

`site/index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
title: Hello
format:
  dashboard:
    logo: images/logo.svg
---

## Row

Hello.
```

```sh
cd site
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with:

```text
error: <dir>/site/index.qmd: output destination <dir>/shared/logo.svg is not under any allowed root (<dir>/site)
1 error
```

Quarto 1 renders the page, and the logo keeps its `images/logo.svg` source.

### Expected behavior

The render succeeds, as in Quarto 1.
Checking for a same-file copy before the allowed-root check would keep the guard for real writes, and let this case through.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: `q2 render` ignores `NO_COLOR` and prints colour codes and hyperlinks in its diagnostics
description:
### Bug description

The script I use to check the dashboard from #1131 against q2 saves each render log to a file, and those logs are full of escape sequences.
With Quarto 1, `NO_COLOR=1` gives me plain logs, but q2 ignores it.

`q2 render` already has a test for `NO_COLOR` and for a terminal on stderr, and uses it for the summary line with the error and warning counts:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs#L632-L638

The diagnostics themselves are printed with colour hard-coded to `true`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs#L1442-L1445

That flag drives both the colours and the OSC 8 file links:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto/src/commands/render.rs#L1740-L1742

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`, which includes a file that does not exist, so both tools stop with an error:

```qmd
---
title: Hello
---

{{< include missing.qmd >}}
```

```sh
NO_COLOR=1 q2 render index.qmd 2>log
python3 -c "d = open('log').read(); print(d.count('\x1b['), d.count('\x1b]8;'))"
NO_COLOR=1 quarto render index.qmd 2>log
python3 -c "d = open('log').read(); print(d.count('\x1b['), d.count('\x1b]8;'))"
```

### Actual behavior

| | q2 | Quarto 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stderr to a file | 162 colour sequences, 2 OSC 8 links | 2 colour sequences |
| stderr to a file, `NO_COLOR=1` | 162 colour sequences, 2 OSC 8 links | none |

Quarto 1 also colours a log file, but `NO_COLOR` turns every escape off.
In q2 it changes nothing.

### Expected behavior

No escape sequences when `NO_COLOR` is set, as in Quarto 1, and none when stderr is not a terminal, as the summary line already does.
Passing `stderr_use_color()` in place of `true` to `format_render_diagnostics_text` would cover both.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: A dashboard `logo` without `logo-alt` gives an unlabelled link and a `Q-10-2` warning about template variables
description: ### Bug description The dashboard from #1131 sets a `logo` and no `logo-alt`, and each q2 render ends with two template warnings about it. The warnings point at a real problem, but they do not say what it is. Without `logo-alt`, both q2 and Quarto 1 write the logo as the only content of a link, with `alt=""`. An empty `alt` marks the image as decorative, so the link has no accessible name, and a screen reader announces it as an unlabelled link. q2 notices that `alt` is missing, but reports it as a template detail. The navbar code adds an `alt` key to each logo variant only when `logo-alt` is set: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/dashboard/navbar.rs#L218-L225 The template then reads that key for both images, and the missing key becomes an undefined-variable warning: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/template.rs#L541-L542 ### Steps to reproduce Put any `logo.svg` next to `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- title: Hello format: dashboard: logo: logo.svg --- ## Row Hello. ``` ```sh q2 render index.qmd quarto render index.qmd grep -o ']*navbar-logo[^>]*>' index.html ``` ### Actual behavior q2 prints: ```text Warning [Q-10-2]: Undefined variable: rendered.dashboard.logo.light.alt Warning [Q-10-2]: Undefined variable: rendered.dashboard.logo.dark.alt 2 warnings ``` Quarto 1 prints nothing. Both write the same links, with no accessible name: ```html ``` ### Expected behavior The logo link has an accessible name even without `logo-alt`, for example from the document `title` or from the brand's `meta.name`. When no name can be found, a single warning tells the author to set `logo-alt`, in place of two warnings about `rendered.dashboard.logo.*.alt`. ### Your environment - q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`. - Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261. - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: `--output-dir` fails in a project that sets `project.output-dir`
description:
### Bug description

To compare q2 with Quarto 1 on the dashboard from #1131, I wanted the q2 output in its own folder, away from the `_site/` that Quarto 1 publishes.
The project sets `output-dir: _site`, and `q2 render index.qmd --output-dir out` stops on the first support file.
The relative and the absolute form of the path give the same error.

The page itself follows the option: when `--output-dir` is given, the project `output-dir` is skipped:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/render_to_file.rs#L763-L784

The writes, though, go through a resource resolver whose `site_root` is still the project `output-dir`, and that root is the only place the output sink accepts.
A comment in the same file describes this stock resolver and moves `site_root` for docx, typst and similar formats, but HTML keeps it:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/render_to_file.rs#L695-L716

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-core/src/resource_resolver.rs#L318-L323

### Steps to reproduce

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: default
  output-dir: _site
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
title: Hello
---

Hello.
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd --output-dir out
quarto render index.qmd --output-dir out
```

### Actual behavior

q2 writes nothing:

```text
Rendering project: <dir> (type: default)
error: <dir>/index.qmd: output destination <dir>/out/index_files/quarto/quarto-theme-d9a3a2debf57bcb1.css is not under any allowed root (<dir>/_site)
Rendered 0 of 1 files to <dir>/_site — 1 error
```

The summary line names `_site`, not `out`.
Quarto 1 writes `out/index.html` and `out/index_files/`, and leaves `_site/` alone.

### Expected behavior

`out/` gets the page and its support files, as with Quarto 1, and the summary names `out`.
Building the resolver with `site_root` set to the `--output-dir` value whenever the option is given would cover it.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: Code cells get none of the Quarto 1 execute variables, including `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO`
description:
### Bug description

I found this also when trying out q2 on `quarto-dev/internal-metrics`.
It keeps every colour and font in `_brand.yml`.
Its Python helper reads the resolved brand for each mode from the file named by `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO` (`format.render.brand.<mode>.data`), and themes every plotnine chart and great_tables table from it.
Under q2 the variable is not set, so every cell that needs the brand fails, and the dashboard does not render.

Quarto 1 sets 4 variables before it runs code, `QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT`, `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH`, `QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE` and `QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO`, which points to a JSON file with `document-path` and the resolved `format`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/fa74261d160f06163cbcfd7f296a4410f207d61c/src/execute/environment.ts#L12-L41

q2 sets none of them.
The engine protocol plan mentions the `EXECUTE_INFO` file only as a detail of the Quarto 1 Jupyter engine, and does not carry it over:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/claude-notes/plans/2026-04-16-plan1a-protocol.md?plain=1#L282

A workaround is to read `_brand.yml` from Python and split the light and dark values by hand.
The dashboard then renders on q2, but the code repeats what Quarto already does, such as finding the brand file and taking brands from extensions.

Related: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1130

### Steps to reproduce

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
format: html
---

```{python}
import os

for name in ("QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO", "QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT", "QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH", "QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE"):
    print(name, "=", os.environ.get(name))
```
````

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

q2 prints `None` for all 4 variables:

```text
QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO = None
QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT = None
QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH = None
QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE = None
```

Quarto 1 sets all 4:

```text
QUARTO_EXECUTE_INFO = <temp>/quarto-session…/adfd53d0bcf12ea4
QUARTO_PROJECT_ROOT = <dir>
QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH = <dir>
QUARTO_DOCUMENT_FILE = index.qmd
```

### Expected behavior

Code cells get the same 4 variables as in Quarto 1, so existing documents keep working.
If q2 prefers another way to give a kernel the resolved brand for each mode, and the document and project paths, that would do too, as long as it is stable and documented.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: A dashboard theme file listed after `brand` cannot use `$brand-*` variables
description:
### Bug description

The metrics dashboard from #1131 has one more blocker on q2, this time in its theme.
It sets `theme: [cosmo, brand, style.scss]`, and `style.scss` uses a palette colour from `_brand.yml` for the navbar, `$navbar-bg: $brand-quarto-navy;`, so the logo stays readable.
q2 cannot compile that theme for a dashboard: `$brand-quarto-navy` is undefined.
Quarto 1 compiles it, and swapping the order to `[cosmo, style.scss, brand]` gets past the error in both.

The difference comes from an extra step in the Quarto 1 dashboard format.
On top of the `brand` entry in `theme:`, it pushes the `_brand.yml` SCSS bundle once more, which defines the `$brand-*` defaults ahead of the theme files:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/fa74261d160f06163cbcfd7f296a4410f207d61c/src/format/dashboard/format-dashboard.ts#L191-L194

The q2 port of the dashboard SCSS stops at the dashboard layer, which Quarto 1 adds just above:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/8f17e950d26c68daae6e794c5fa513a96c0dae68/crates/quarto-sass/src/compile.rs#L118-L127

Plain `html` never had the extra bundle, so there the same theme fails in Quarto 1 too, and q2 already agrees with it.

### Steps to reproduce

`_brand.yml`:

```yaml
color:
  palette:
    navy: "#1f4e79"
```

`custom.scss`:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$navbar-bg: $brand-navy;
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
title: Hello
brand: _brand.yml
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: [cosmo, brand, custom.scss]
---

## Row

Hello.
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
grep -o 'navbar-bg:[^;]*' index_files/libs/bootstrap/*.css
```

### Actual behavior

q2 stops with:

```text
Error: [Q-14-6] Theme SCSS compilation failed
   ╭─[ <dir>/index.qmd:6:12 ]
   │
 6 │     theme: [cosmo, brand, custom.scss]
   │            ─────────────┬─────────────
   │                         ╰─────────────── compiling the theme SCSS bundle failed:
Error: Undefined variable.
    ╷
864 │ $navbar-bg: $brand-navy;
    │             ^^^^^^^^^^^
    ╵
```

With Quarto 1 the render goes through, and `navbar-bg: #1f4e79` ends up in the light and the dark bundle.

| Format | `theme:` | Quarto 1 | q2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dashboard` | `[cosmo, brand, custom.scss]` | renders | `Undefined variable` |
| `dashboard` | `[cosmo, custom.scss, brand]` | renders | renders |
| `html` | `[cosmo, brand, custom.scss]` | `Undefined variable` | `Undefined variable` |
| `html` | `[cosmo, custom.scss, brand]` | renders | renders |

Adding light and dark colours to `_brand.yml` changes nothing in this table.

### Expected behavior

Dashboards keep the Quarto 1 behaviour, so existing themes compile unchanged.
One way is for `builtin_user_layers` to include the brand layers whenever `config.dashboard_layer` is on.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.43.0-nightly.20261109` (nightly built from 8f17e95), and `q2 v0.42.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: knitr capture reports every chunk error as rlang_error (knitr wraps errors via rlang::entrace)
description:
## Summary

When rlang is installed, knitr runs every chunk error through `rlang::entrace()`. That function wraps the original error in a new condition of class `rlang_error`. Our knitr capture code (`crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/resources/rmd/capture.R:150`) records `ename = class(p)[[1]]`, so every captured error is reported as `rlang_error`. The user's actual class, such as `simpleError` or a custom class, is lost.

Since rlang is installed in almost every real R setup, this affects most users.

## Reproduction

With R, knitr, rmarkdown, jsonlite and rlang installed:

```
cargo nextest run -p quarto-core --lib -E 'test(knitr::capture_tests::capture_classifies_pieces)'
```

```
panicked at crates/quarto-core/src/engine/knitr/capture_tests.rs:170:13:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "rlang_error"
 right: "simpleError"
```

Fails with both:
- R 4.6.0, knitr 1.51, rlang 1.2.0, evaluate 1.0.5
- R 4.6.0, knitr 1.52, rlang 1.3.0, evaluate 1.0.5 (latest CRAN as of 2026-11-09)

## Cause

`knitr:::knit_handlers` appends `rlang_entrace_handler` (`list(error = function(e) rlang::entrace(e))`) to the chunk's `calling_handlers` whenever `knitr:::has_rlang` is TRUE. Reproduced with evaluate alone:

```r
h <- evaluate::new_output_handler(
  calling_handlers = list(error = function(e) rlang::entrace(e)))
e <- evaluate::evaluate('stop("boom")', output_handler = h)[[2]]
class(e)        # "rlang_error" "error" "condition"
class(e$error)  # "simpleError" "error" "condition"
```

A custom error class is also replaced: with `stop(structure(class = c("myError", "error", "condition"), ...))`, `class(e)` is `rlang_error` and `class(e$error)` is `myError`.

## Suggested fix

In `capture.R`, when `p` inherits from `rlang_error` and has an `$error` field, read `ename` from `class(p$error)[[1]]`. Otherwise fall back to `class(p)[[1]]`. Then decide whether `evalue` and `call` should also come from `p$error`.

A related question: knitr also changes the error text to rlang's format (`Error:\n! boom` instead of `Error in …: boom`). The test only checks `starts_with("Error")`, so it still passes, but we should decide whether that text is what we want to show.

## Why CI didn't catch this

No CI workflow installs R, and every test in `capture_tests.rs` skips itself through `r_available()` when R is missing. These tests therefore only run on developer machines that have R. It's worth adding R (with knitr and rlang) to at least one CI leg.

Found while investigating pandoc 3.13 test failures; this failure is unrelated to pandoc.

title: Listing sort: "date" orders items by the date text, so M/D/YYYY dates sort wrong
description:
## Summary

A listing with `sort: "date"` orders its items by the text of the `date:` value, not by the date. With dates such as `5/5/2023`, the order is wrong. q2 reads the dates correctly for display and for `data-listing-date-sort`, and gives no warning.

## Versions

- q2 0.44.0-nightly.20261110
- Quarto 1.10.18 (expected output)
- macOS, arm64

## Repro

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  render:
    - "*.qmd"
    - "posts/*.md"
```

`index.qmd`:

```yaml
---
title: Posts
listing:
  contents: "posts/*.md"
  sort: "date"
  fields: [title, date]
---
```

`posts/alpha.md`:

```markdown
---
title: "Alpha"
date: 01/5/2024
---

Text.
```

`posts/bravo.md`:

```markdown
---
title: "Bravo"
date: 5/5/2023
---

Text.
```

`posts/charlie.md`:

```markdown
---
title: "Charlie"
date: 6/1/2023
---

Text.
```

Command:

```bash
q2 render
```

## Expected (Quarto 1)

Oldest first:

| Item | Shown date | `data-listing-date-sort` |
|---|---|---|
| Bravo | May 5, 2023 | 1683262800000 |
| Charlie | Jun 1, 2023 | 1685595600000 |
| Alpha | Jan 5, 2024 | 1704434400000 |

## Actual (q2)

| Item | Shown date | `data-listing-date-sort` |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha | Jan 5, 2024 | 1704412800000 |
| Bravo | May 5, 2023 | 1683244800000 |
| Charlie | Jun 1, 2023 | 1685577600000 |

This is the text order of `01/5/2024`, `5/5/2023`, `6/1/2023`. The shown dates and the sort attributes are correct, so q2 parses the dates. Only the order of the items uses the raw text.

## Notes

- With ISO dates (`2024-01-05`), q2 and Quarto 1 give the same order. We changed our posts to ISO dates as a workaround.
- The same happens with a list sort such as `sort: ["date", "title desc"]`.

title: Grid listing ignores image-height, so thumbnails render at full size
description: ## Summary In a `grid` listing, q2 ignores `image-height`. Quarto 1 gives each thumbnail an inline height (150px by default, or the `image-height` value) and the class `card-img`. q2 gives neither, so a large image shows at its full size. In our site, the thumbnails overlapped the next cards and made the page about 2,000px wide. ## Versions - q2 0.44.0-nightly.20261110 - Quarto 1.10.18 (expected output) - macOS, arm64 ## Repro `_quarto.yml`: ```yaml project: type: website render: - "*.qmd" - "posts/*.md" ``` `default.qmd`: ```yaml --- title: Default height listing: contents: "posts/*.md" type: grid fields: [image, title] --- ``` `explicit.qmd`: ```yaml --- title: Explicit height listing: contents: "posts/*.md" type: grid image-height: 100px fields: [image, title] --- ``` `posts/alpha.md`, with `posts/wide.png` as any large image (we used 1600x1000): ```markdown --- title: "Alpha" image: wide.png --- Text. ``` Command: ```bash q2 render ``` ## Expected (Quarto 1) ```html ``` ## Actual (q2) ```html ``` There is no warning. ## Workaround A stylesheet rule on the listing page: ```css .quarto-grid-item .card-img-top img.thumbnail-image { height: 150px; width: 100%; object-fit: cover; } ```

title: Extension theme paths are read as markdown on pages that run code, so underscores are dropped (Q-14-4)
description:
## Summary

On pages that run code, q2 reads the paths in an extension's `theme:` list as markdown. If the resolved path contains two underscores, the text between them becomes emphasis and the underscores are dropped. q2 then looks for a file that does not exist and stops with `Q-14-4`.

Pages without code cells resolve the same path correctly. Quarto 1 renders all pages.

## Versions

- q2 0.44.0-nightly.20261110
- Quarto 1.10.18 (expected output)
- macOS, arm64

## Repro

```
_quarto.yml
_extensions/acme/demo/_extension.yml
_extensions/acme/demo/_colors.scss
_extensions/acme/demo/main.scss
plain.qmd
code.qmd
rcode.qmd
```

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  render: ["*.qmd"]
format: demo-html
```

`_extensions/acme/demo/_extension.yml`:

```yaml
title: demo
contributes:
  formats:
    html:
      theme: [main.scss, _colors.scss]
```

`_extensions/acme/demo/_colors.scss`:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$accent: #447099;
```

`_extensions/acme/demo/main.scss`:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/
.x { color: $accent; }
```

`plain.qmd`:

````markdown
---
title: Plain
---

No code.
````

`code.qmd`:

````markdown
---
title: Code
---

```{python}
print(1)
```
````

`rcode.qmd`:

````markdown
---
title: Code
engine: knitr
---

```{r}
1
```
````

Command:

```bash
q2 render
```

## Expected (Quarto 1)

`quarto render` renders all three pages with the theme from both `main.scss` and `_colors.scss`.

## Actual (q2)

`plain.qmd` renders. `code.qmd` (Jupyter) and `rcode.qmd` (knitr) both fail:

```
Error [Q-14-4]: Theme file not found
the `theme:` entry resolves to `<project>/extensions/acme/demo/colors.scss`, which does not exist.
```

```
Rendered 1 of 3 files to <project>/_site — 2 errors
```

The resolved path is `_extensions/acme/demo/_colors.scss`. The text `_extensions/acme/demo/_` is read as emphasis, so both underscores are removed. Rendering each page alone gives the same result.

## Notes

- A file name with no leading underscore (`colors.scss`) works, because the path then has only one underscore. We use this rename as a workaround.
- The `!path` tag (`[main.scss, !path _colors.scss]`) does not help in q2. Quarto 1 rejects the tag with `YAMLException: unknown tag !<!path>`, so it is also not a portable workaround.
- We found this with a docs theme extension that loads a `_posit-colors.scss` partial next to its main theme file.

title: A list-table cell holding a paragraph is written tight and re-reads as plain
description:
Since the CommonMark loose/tight change (370123a8aefb144ea32c8443c2ee0e1b32309e7d, #1098), a list-table row whose cells are separated by a blank line reads with `Para` cells. `write_list_table` writes a cell's first `Plain` and `Para` identically and never puts a blank line between cells, so the row comes back tight and the `Para` cell re-reads as `Plain`. Ordinary bullet lists keep the distinction (`list_is_tight`), so the loss is specific to the list-table cell writer.

Input:

````sh
$ printf -- '::: {.list-table}\n\n* * a\n  * b\n\n* * x\n\n  * ```\n    code\n    ```\n\n:::\n'
````

````markdown
::: {.list-table}

* * a
  * b

* * x

  * ```
    code
    ```

:::
````

Reader (the `x` cell is a `Para`):

````sh
$ printf -- '...' | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
````

````haskell
[ Table ( "" , [] , [] ) (Caption Nothing []) [(AlignDefault, ColWidthDefault), (AlignDefault, ColWidthDefault)] (TableHead ( "" , [] , [] ) [Row ( "" , [] , [] ) [Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Plain [Str "a"]] , Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Plain [Str "b"]] ] ]) [TableBody ( "" , [] , [] ) (RowHeadColumns 0) [] [Row ( "" , [] , [] ) [Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Para [Str "x"]] , Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [CodeBlock ( "" , [] , [] ) "code"] ] ]] (TableFoot ( "" , [] , [] ) [] ) ]
````

Writer (no blank line between the `x` cell and the code cell):

````sh
$ printf -- '...' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>&1
````

````markdown
::: {.list-table}

* - a
  - b
* - x
  - ```
    code
    ```
:::
````

Round trip (the `x` cell is now `Plain`):

````sh
$ printf -- '...' | cargo run --bin pampa -- -t qmd 2>/dev/null | cargo run --bin pampa -- 2>&1
````

````haskell
[ Table ( "" , [] , [] ) (Caption Nothing []) [(AlignDefault, ColWidthDefault), (AlignDefault, ColWidthDefault)] (TableHead ( "" , [] , [] ) [Row ( "" , [] , [] ) [Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Plain [Str "a"]] , Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Plain [Str "b"]] ] ]) [TableBody ( "" , [] , [] ) (RowHeadColumns 0) [] [Row ( "" , [] , [] ) [Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Plain [Str "x"]] , Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [CodeBlock ( "" , [] , [] ) "code"] ] ]] (TableFoot ( "" , [] , [] ) [] ) ]
````

The only difference between the two reads:

````diff
- Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Para [Str "x"]]
+ Cell ( "" , [] , [] ) AlignDefault (RowSpan 1) (ColSpan 1) [Plain [Str "x"]]
````

Related: #1098 introduced the looseness rule that exposes this. #1151 fixes a sibling writer round trip from the same change (adjacent lists inside a list item) but only touches `write_bulletlist` / `write_orderedlist` and the raw-block separator, not `write_list_table`, so it does not cover this case. #174 was the same Para to Plain symptom for ordinary bullet lists.

In the wild (quarto-web grid tables with a code-block cell; `qmd-syntax-helper convert -r grid-tables` turns them into list tables with blank-line-separated cells):

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/781af76ce83db51b4b02ddcb5a871de1b20f2cba/docs/computations/caching.qmd#L17
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/781af76ce83db51b4b02ddcb5a871de1b20f2cba/docs/manuscripts/next-steps.qmd#L12
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/blob/781af76ce83db51b4b02ddcb5a871de1b20f2cba/docs/faq/rmarkdown.qmd#L41

title: Book project: citations stay as @key in HTML output (Typst works)
description: ## Summary In a `type: book` project rendered to HTML, citations are left as raw `@key` text and no bibliography is produced. The same project renders correctly to Typst, and the same bibliography setup works in a `type: website` project and in a single document. ## Reproduction `_quarto.yml`: ```yaml project: type: book book: title: "Book" chapters: - index.qmd - ch1.qmd bibliography: refs.bib ``` `index.qmd`: ```markdown # Preface {.unnumbered} Intro ``` `ch1.qmd`: ```markdown # One As in @knuth84. ``` `refs.bib`: ```bibtex @book{knuth84, author={Knuth, Donald}, title={The TeXbook}, year={1984}, publisher={Addison-Wesley}} ``` ```bash q2 render --to html ``` ## Actual `_book/ch1.html` contains `@knuth84`. No "Knuth (1984)" and no references section. Putting `bibliography: refs.bib` in the chapter's own front matter does not change the result. ## Expected "Knuth (1984)" linking to a bibliography entry, as with `q2 render --to typst` on the same project and as in Quarto 1. ## What works - `q2 render --to typst` on the same book: citation and bibliography resolve. - A `type: website` project with the same `bibliography`: citation resolves to a link to `#ref-knuth84`. ## Possibly related In a slightly larger book (3 chapters with `{#sec-...}` and `{#fig-...}` labels), HTML rendering also prints `unresolved crossref` warnings for labels that are defined in another chapter, although the links in the HTML output are correct. I did not narrow this down separately. Related, closed: #1026 (citations in HTML stay as `@key` when `bibliography` is set), which looks like the same symptom fixed for single documents. Found with `q2` 0.43.0 built from `origin/main` at 929891fa5 (2026-11-10). Also reproduces with the installed 0.40.0.

title: output: asis is ignored: printed markdown renders as a code block
description:
## Summary q2 ignores `#| output: asis`. The printed markdown shows as text in a code block. Quarto 1 adds the printed markdown to the document, so it renders as headings, formatted text, divs, tabsets, and code blocks. ## Versions - q2 0.44.0-nightly.20261110 - Quarto 1.10.18 (expected output) - macOS, arm64, Jupyter `python3` kernel ## Repro `index.qmd`, with no `_quarto.yml`: ````markdown --- title: Asis --- ```{python} #| echo: false #| output: asis print("## Generated heading\n") print("Some **bold** text.\n") print("::: {.callout-note}\nA note.\n:::") ``` ```` Command: ```bash q2 render index.qmd ``` ## Expected (Quarto 1) An `

` "Generated heading", a paragraph with `bold`, and a note callout. ## Actual (q2) ```html 
## Generated heading

Some **bold** text.

::: {.callout-note}
A note.
:::
``` There is no warning. ## Notes - We use `output: asis` to make a tabset of install commands from an API at render time. There is no workaround in the project that keeps the content dynamic.

title: Two-space hard line breaks: rendered and documented as unchanged, but stated as unsupported
description:
q2 0.42.0 on Windows 11. A line ending in two spaces produces a hard break: ``` line one·· line two ``` (`·` marks a trailing space.) `q2 render` gives `

line one
line two

`, with no diagnostic. The migration guide agrees with this: "Things that are the same" lists "two-space and backslash line breaks". But in quarto-cli #8984 the stated decision is "we're not going to support the two-space syntax in q2" (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/8984#issuecomment-4893814466, 2026-07-06). Which is intended? - If the syntax is going away, it currently has no diagnostic and no row in the migration guide. It would be a quiet difference of the kind the guide tries to avoid, and a hard one to spot, since the characters are invisible. - If the decision changed, nothing is wrong in q2, and a note on #8984 would settle it for people reading that thread.

title: `q2 add` ignores the schema version of `.quarto-source.yml` and reads a newer record as version 1
description:
### Bug description

The `version` key at the top of `.quarto-source.yml` is the schema version of the record itself.
q2 writes `version: 1`, and the comment on `SourceRecord::version` says to bump it on an incompatible change.

`installed_state()` in `crates/quarto/src/commands/add/record.rs` never compares that schema version with `RECORD_VERSION`.
A record that a newer q2 wrote with schema version 2 is read with the schema version 1 rules.
Its file hashes are checked as if they meant the same thing, and `q2 add` then replaces it with a schema version 1 record.

A record that q2 can't parse at all is already treated as a local edit, so a newer schema version could go the same way, or get its own message.
The development version of Quarto Wizard, which writes the same record, refuses a schema version above 1 today.
It will follow whatever q2 settles on.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p demo/_extensions/demo project
printf 'title: Demo\nauthor: Acme\nversion: 1.1.0\ncontributes:\n  filters:\n    - filter.lua\n' > demo/_extensions/demo/_extension.yml
printf 'function Para(el) return el end\n' > demo/_extensions/demo/filter.lua
printf 'project:\n  type: default\n' > project/_quarto.yml
cd project
q2 add ../demo --no-prompt
# Record schema version: 1 -> 2, as if a newer q2 had written it.
perl -pi -e 's/^version: 1$/version: 2/' _extensions/demo/.quarto-source.yml
# Extension version: 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0, so that q2 add has an update to install.
perl -pi -e 's/version: 1.1.0/version: 1.2.0/' ../demo/_extensions/demo/_extension.yml
q2 add ../demo --no-prompt
grep '^version' _extensions/demo/.quarto-source.yml
```

### Actual behaviour

`q2 add` reports `[Update]  1.1.0  ->  1.2.0`, and the record is back at schema version 1 (`version: 1`).

For comparison, a schema version that isn't a number (`version: two`) gives:

```text
Error: Installed extensions have local changes
Installing would replace files that changed since `q2 add` installed them:

_extensions/demo:
  .quarto-source.yml (unreadable install record)

Nothing was written. Re-run with --force to replace them.
```

### Expected behaviour

A record with a schema version above `RECORD_VERSION` is not read with the schema version 1 rules.
`q2 add` refuses to replace it without `--force`, and says that the record comes from a newer version of q2.

### Your environment

- q2 0.43.0 (release binary, `darwin_arm64`).
- macOS 27.2.

title: `q2 add` drops keys it doesn't know when it rewrites `.quarto-source.yml`
description:
### Bug description

When `q2 add` replaces an installed extension, it writes `.quarto-source.yml` again from `SourceRecord`, which has no field for keys it doesn't define.
Any other key in the old record is lost.

If a newer q2 adds a field to the record, an older q2 removes it on its next `q2 add`.
The same happens to a key that another tool writes.
Keeping those keys would let third-party tools work with the same record and schema as q2.

I found this with the development version of Quarto Wizard, the VS Code extension for Quarto extensions.
It now writes this record in the q2 format, and can change what it writes to fit q2.
For now it adds a `quarto-wizard:` block, which the reproduction below uses.

In the code, `installed_state()` in `crates/quarto/src/commands/add/record.rs` parses the old record but returns only the state.
`write_record()` in `crates/quarto/src/commands/add/install.rs` then builds a new record from the plan's provenance.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p demo/_extensions/demo project
printf 'title: Demo\nauthor: Acme\nversion: 1.0.0\ncontributes:\n  filters:\n    - filter.lua\n' > demo/_extensions/demo/_extension.yml
printf 'function Para(el) return el end\n' > demo/_extensions/demo/filter.lua
printf 'project:\n  type: default\n' > project/_quarto.yml
cd project
q2 add ../demo --no-prompt
printf 'quarto-wizard:\n  track: branch\n  commit: 3f2a9c1e5b7d4a60918c2d4e6f8a0b1c3d5e7f90\n' >> _extensions/demo/.quarto-source.yml
perl -pi -e 's/version: 1.0.0/version: 1.1.0/' ../demo/_extensions/demo/_extension.yml
q2 add ../demo --no-prompt
cat _extensions/demo/.quarto-source.yml
```

### Actual behaviour

The second `q2 add` reports `[Update]  1.0.0  ->  1.1.0`, and the record no longer has the `quarto-wizard:` block:

```yaml
version: 1
source: ../demo
kind: local-dir
files:
  _extension.yml: 8a3dea3a3ef366964ed5ace2f52ef4b47652cb88355c870972a22750b0b037fe
  filter.lua: 165d5ece3c1227c751f4f2bd3186827d2ce6b6ce3709a270161fee63a27bae77
```

### Expected behaviour

`q2 add` updates the fields it owns (`version`, `source`, `kind`, `ref`, `files`) and keeps every other key as it was.

### Your environment

- q2 0.43.0 (release binary, `darwin_arm64`).
- macOS 27.2.

title: Document `.quarto-source.yml` as a format other tools can rely on
description:
### Description

#### Context

`q2 add` writes `.quarto-source.yml` next to each extension.
Today the format lives in the `SourceRecord` struct and one line of the user guide.

Other tools can work with the same file.
The development version of Quarto Wizard, the VS Code extension for Quarto extensions, already writes it in the q2 format, so that an extension installed by one tool can be updated by the other.
To follow the format, it has to read the q2 source.

#### Proposal

Publish a short specification of the record, with a JSON Schema next to it.
It would cover:

- each field and what it means;
- the schema `version` policy: what bumps it, and what a reader does with a newer one;
- the rule for keys a tool doesn't know: kept as they are on rewrite;
- the hash rules: sha256 of the bytes of each file as they are on disk, `/` paths relative to the extension folder, the record itself left out.

#### Why

Without a written contract, every other tool has to guess, and a change in q2 can break it without notice.
The two following come from that gap:
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1175
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1176

#### Benefits

People using q2 can mix tools on one project: install from the command line, update from the editor, or the other way round.
Local edit detection keeps working whichever tool wrote the record.
Tools such as Quarto Wizard can validate against the published schema and follow its changes.
A future official q2 extension for Positron and VS Code could rely on the same specification.
A future `q2 update` gets a stable base too.

title: Record what an update follows and the installed commit in `.quarto-source.yml`
description:
### Description

#### Context

The record has `source`, `kind`, and an optional `ref`.
`ref` is what the user typed, not what was installed.
A plain `owner/repo` installs the head of the default branch.
The record doesn't say which commit that was, nor whether a later update should follow the branch or the latest release.
A future `q2 update` can't tell whether the branch has moved.

Other tools need the same two facts.
The development version of Quarto Wizard keeps them for now in its own `quarto-wizard:` block, and would move to keys that q2 defines.

#### Proposal

Add two optional keys to schema version 1 of the record:

```yaml
version: 1
source: acme/demo
kind: github
track: branch   # tag | branch: what an update follows
commit: 3f2a9c1e5b7d4a60918c2d4e6f8a0b1c3d5e7f90   # full SHA of what is installed
files:
  _extension.yml: <sha256>
  filter.lua: <sha256>
```

Both are optional, so the readers of today still accept the file.
q2 writes `commit` when it knows it, for example for an `@<sha>` install, and `track` from how the user installed.

#### Why

What an update follows and what is installed both describe the install, and the record is where q2 keeps that.

#### Benefits

`q2 update` can tell from the record alone whether a branch has moved.
A committed record shows exactly which commit a project uses.
Other tools, such as Quarto Wizard or a future official q2 extension for Positron and VS Code, can read the same keys instead of keeping their own.

Related:

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1177

title: Install the default branch through `archive/HEAD` instead of trying `main` then `master`
description:
### Description

#### Context

For a plain `owner/repo`, `crates/quarto-source-fetch/src/target.rs` tries `archive/refs/heads/main`, then `archive/refs/heads/master`.
When the default branch has another name, q2 either fails, or installs a branch that isn't the default.

https://github.com/mcanouil/q2-default-branch-demo shows the second case.
Its default branch is `develop`, with the `demo` extension at version 2.0.0.
An older `main` branch has the same extension at version 1.0.0.

```text
$ q2 add mcanouil/q2-default-branch-demo --trust --no-prompt
The following changes will be made in .:
  Demo  [Install]      1.0.0  (filter)
```

q2 installs version 1.0.0 from `main`.
The record it writes has no `ref` and no commit, so nothing shows later that the install came from a branch that isn't the default:

```yaml
version: 1
source: mcanouil/q2-default-branch-demo
kind: github
files:
  _extension.yml: b57dd1f9313c1b622ed19918e48134119762128b5612b709918317c10b63cef3
  demo.lua: 2150321a3a3a341aebde685226d403639b195ff507c1a45b9b6ab23fc4ee5f26
```

#### Proposal

Download `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/archive/HEAD.tar.gz` for the default branch.
GitHub answers with a redirect that names the commit at the head of the default branch:

```text
$ curl -sI https://github.com/mcanouil/q2-default-branch-demo/archive/HEAD.tar.gz | grep -i '^location'
location: https://codeload.github.com/mcanouil/q2-default-branch-demo/tar.gz/0cb98bf577f198e0417d163bc589e8dfb9ae2e96
```

`archive/refs/heads/main` redirects to `.../tar.gz/refs/heads/main`, with no commit.

#### Why

It removes the guess at the branch name, and needs no API call or token.

#### Benefits

`q2 add owner/repo` installs the default branch of any repository, whatever its name.
q2 learns the installed commit for free, which https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1178 needs.
Other tools that install from GitHub, such as Quarto Wizard, can use the same URL and get the same commit for the same input.

Related:

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/14821#issuecomment-6577471347
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues/1178

title: pasting some Unicode text (e.g. table-flip emoticons) breaks parsing and rendering
description:
## What happened

Copying and pasting emoticons from https://looks.wtf/flipping-tables/ into a Quarto Hub document breaks parsing and rendering of the document.

For example, `(╯°□°)╯︵ ┻━┻` didn't render until it was wrapped in backticks as inline code.

## Steps to reproduce

2. Paste one of the emoticons from https://looks.wtf/flipping-tables/ into the body text.
3. Look at the preview or rendered output.

title: Dashboard value boxes keep the Bootswatch colours when the theme includes `brand`
description:
### Bug description

With #1132 fixed, the metrics dashboard renders on q2 with its brand, except for the value boxes.
They keep the cosmo colours instead of the brand's `success`, `warning` and `info`.

The dashboard SCSS picks each value box colour through `theme-override-value($theme-name, …)`, and cosmo has its own value box colours in that table:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a76c96abfe2effc9872b572b201d6f772a89161e/resources/scss/bootstrap/_bootstrap-functions.scss#L103-L116

Quarto 1 skips that table for a branded theme, because its brand layers start with `$theme: "brand" !default;`.
The theme name is then `brand`, which has no entry, so the value boxes fall back to `$success` and the other brand colours:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/fa74261d160f06163cbcfd7f296a4410f207d61c/src/core/sass/brand.ts#L588-L598

q2's brand layers do not set `$theme`, so the name stays `cosmo`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a76c96abfe2effc9872b572b201d6f772a89161e/crates/quarto-sass/src/brand_layer.rs#L65-L96

### Steps to reproduce

`_brand.yml`:

```yaml
color:
  palette:
    green: "#009e73"
  success: green
```

`index.qmd`:

```qmd
---
title: Hello
brand: _brand.yml
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: [cosmo, brand]
---

## Row

::: {.valuebox color="success"}
Opened

42
:::
```

```sh
q2 render index.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
grep -rho '\.card\.valuebox\.bslib-card\.bg-success{[^}]*}' index_files
```

### Actual behavior

q2 compiles the cosmo colour:

```css
.quarto-dashboard .card.valuebox.bslib-card.bg-success{background-color:#3aa716 !important}
```

Quarto 1 compiles the brand colour:

```css
.quarto-dashboard .card.valuebox.bslib-card.bg-success{background-color:#009e73 !important}
```

The `warning` and `info` boxes differ in the same way.

### Expected behavior

Value boxes use the brand colours, as in Quarto 1.
`brand_to_layers` could start with a layer whose defaults are `$theme: "brand" !default;`, as Quarto 1 does.

### Your environment

- q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.45.0-nightly.20261112` (nightly built from a76c96a), and `q2 v0.44.0`.
- Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261.
- OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64).
- Terminal, no IDE.

title: `Q-2-49` warns on a span with an empty attribute block, `[text]{}`
description: ### Bug description Each value box number in the metrics dashboard from #1131 comes from Python as `Markdown("[" + value + "]{}")`, and every render warns 12 times with `Q-2-49`. The `{}` is there to make it a span, but the warning says the group "has no attribute block". Pandoc reads `[10]{}` as a `Span` with an empty attribute, while a bare `[10]` stays literal text. q2 renders `[10]{}` as `10`, like Quarto 1, so the output is right and only the warning is off. An empty `{}` is admittedly an edge case, but it is a handy way to get a plain `` in the HTML DOM, for example to target the value from CSS or JavaScript, and generated Markdown like this produces it easily. The check looks at the parsed attribute, which is empty in both cases, so `[10]{}` and `[10]` look the same to it: https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/blob/a76c96abfe2effc9872b572b201d6f772a89161e/crates/quarto-core/src/transforms/reference_link_diagnostics.rs#L114-L121 ### Steps to reproduce `index.qmd`: ```qmd --- title: Hello --- A [10]{} B and [x]{.y} C. ``` ```sh q2 render index.qmd quarto render index.qmd ``` ### Actual behavior q2 renders `10` and warns: ```text Warning: [Q-2-49] `[10]` has no attribute block, so it renders as an empty span and the brackets are discarded — the reader sees `10`. Write `\[10\]` to keep the brackets literal, or `[10]{.class}` if a span was intended. ╭─[ /index.qmd:5:3 ] │ 5 │ A [10]{} B and [x]{.y} C. │ ───┬── ``` Quarto 1 renders the same `10` with no warning. ### Expected behavior No `Q-2-49` when the source has an attribute block, even an empty one, since `{}` already says that a span is intended. ### Your environment - q2: `q2 (quarto 2) 0.45.0-nightly.20261112` (nightly built from a76c96a), and `q2 v0.44.0`. - Quarto 1 for comparison: development build of quarto-dev/quarto-cli@fa74261. - OS: macOS 27.2 (arm64). - Terminal, no IDE.

title: Code cells run in the project directory, not the document's directory; `execute-dir` is ignored
description:
### Bug description

In a project, q2 runs a document's code cells with the project root as the working directory.
Quarto 1 runs them in the document's own directory, unless `execute-dir: project` says otherwise.
A page in a subdirectory that opens a file by a relative path therefore fails under q2.

`execute-dir: file` and `--execute-dir <dir>` don't change this.

`QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH` is set correctly, which gives a workaround (below).

In Great Docs' own docs, `user-guide/table-previews.qmd` and `user-guide/table-explorer.qmd` read
`../assets/data/students.csv`, and both pages fail. User guides commonly load example data this way.

### Steps to reproduce

````sh
mkdir -p cwd-repro/sub && cd cwd-repro
printf 'project:\n  type: website\n' > _quarto.yml
printf -- '---\ntitle: Home\n---\n\nHome.\n' > index.qmd
printf 'x\n1\n' > sub/data.csv
cat > sub/page.qmd <<'EOF'
---
title: Page
---

```{python}
import os
print("cwd:", os.getcwd())
print("QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH:", os.environ.get("QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH"))
print(open("data.csv").read())
```
EOF
q2 render
````

### Actual behavior

The page fails and `q2 render` exits 1:

```
Error: Execution failed in jupyter: code cell at /private/tmp/cwd-repro/sub/page.qmd:6:2 raised FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data.csv'
Rendered 1 of 2 files to /private/tmp/cwd-repro/_site — 1 error
```

With the last line changed to `print("exists:", os.path.exists("data.csv"))`, so that the page
renders, it shows:

```
cwd: /private/tmp/cwd-repro
QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH: /private/tmp/cwd-repro/sub
exists: False
```

The output is the same with any of these:

- `execute-dir: file` under `project:` in `_quarto.yml`, where Quarto 1 documents it
- `execute-dir: file` at the top level of `_quarto.yml`
- `q2 render --execute-dir /path/to/cwd-repro/sub`
- `cd sub && q2 render page.qmd`

### Expected behavior

As in Quarto 1.9.37, which renders the page and exits 0:

```
cwd: /private/tmp/cwd-repro/sub
QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH: /private/tmp/cwd-repro/sub
x
1
```

- By default, run code cells in the document's directory.
- Honor `project: execute-dir: file | project`, and `--execute-dir`.
- If q2 means to change the default, it would help to say so in the Quarto 1 differences docs, and
  to make `execute-dir` work so projects can opt back in.

Workaround: a hidden first cell that changes directory.

````markdown
```{python}
#| include: false
import os
os.chdir(os.environ["QUARTO_DOCUMENT_PATH"])
```
````

I've only tried the Jupyter engine.

title: `io.popen` in a Lua extension hangs a website render when pages render in parallel (macOS)
description:
### Bug description

A Lua shortcode or filter that calls `io.popen` can hang `q2 render` forever, at 0% CPU, when pass 2
renders several pages at once. The same calls made through `pandoc.pipe` (or
`pandoc.system.command`) never hang.

Many extensions in the wild shell out through `io.popen`, typically to run `git`, `python` or a CLI
tool. Great Docs did too: it has moved its bundled extensions to `pandoc.system.command`, but sites
that use third-party extensions can still hang.

### Steps to reproduce

Run this in an empty directory. It writes a website with an index page and 60 pages, each with ten
`{{< pop >}}` shortcodes. The shortcode runs a short shell command through `io.popen`.

```sh
mkdir -p popen-hang/_extensions/pop && cd popen-hang
printf 'project:\n  type: website\n' > _quarto.yml
printf 'title: pop\nversion: 0.0.1\ncontributes:\n  shortcodes:\n    - pop.lua\n' > _extensions/pop/_extension.yml
cat > _extensions/pop/pop.lua <<'LUA'
return {
  ["pop"] = function(args)
    local h = io.popen("sh -c 'sleep 0.01; echo hi' 2>&1")
    local out = h:read("*a")
    h:close()
    return pandoc.Str(out)
  end
}
LUA
printf -- '---\ntitle: Home\n---\n\nHome.\n' > index.qmd
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  { printf -- '---\ntitle: p%s\n---\n' "$i"; for j in $(seq 1 10); do printf '\nx {{< pop >}}\n'; done; } > "p$i.qmd"
done
q2 render
```

### Actual behavior

`q2 render` never finishes, on every run, and uses no CPU. These are the results for other sizes:

| Project | Result |
|---|---|
| 2 pages, 10 calls each | renders in about 1 s |
| 9 pages, 80 calls each | hangs (killed after 90 s) |
| 60 pages, 10 calls each (above) | hangs |
| 1 page, 600 calls | renders in about 35 s (about 60 ms a call) |
| `q2 render p1.qmd` with 100 calls | renders |
| 60 pages, 10 calls each, using `pandoc.pipe("sh", {"-c", "sleep 0.01; echo hi"}, "")` | renders 61 of 61 pages in about 3 s |

So the hang needs several pages rendering concurrently; the number of calls alone doesn't cause it.
`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` doesn't help.

`sample` on the hung process shows several `quarto-pass2-N` threads (there are 12, one per core)
blocked here:

```
io_popen  (liolib.c:300)
  fflush(NULL)
    _fwalk  (libsystem_c.dylib)
      sflush_locked  (libsystem_c.dylib)
        flockfile  (libsystem_c.dylib)
          _pthread_mutex_firstfit_lock_slow  (libsystem_pthread.dylib)
            __psynch_mutexwait  (libsystem_kernel.dylib)
```

Lua's `l_popen` is `(fflush(NULL), popen(c, m))`, so every `io.popen` first walks and locks every
open `FILE`. In a debugger, the `FILE` the threads wait on has already been closed (`_flags=0`,
`_file=-1`) but its lock is still held. This looks like a race in macOS libc between a concurrent
`pclose`/`fclose` and `fflush(NULL)`, which Lua's stock `io.popen` hits once several Lua states run
it on different threads of one process. I haven't tried Linux.

### Expected behavior

The render finishes, as it does with `pandoc.pipe`, and as it does with Quarto 1 (which runs one
Pandoc process per page).

Two possible fixes:

- Replace `io.popen` and `os.execute` with versions that spawn through q2's Rust process code, as
  `pandoc.pipe` does. q2 already wraps both in `guard_stock_spawn`
  (`crates/pampa/src/lua/process_view.rs`), so this is where they would go.
- Or serialize the stock `popen`, `pclose` and `fflush(NULL)` across all Lua states with one global
  lock.

I gather a fix through the Lua file-system work is underway. This issue records the repro and the
stack in the meantime.

title: Freeze: `execute: freeze` and `--use-freezer` are silently ignored; requirements from Great Docs
description:
### Description

q2 doesn't implement `execute: freeze` yet. I know freeze is planned as a later epic built on the
execution records (the `.ipynb` format in
`claude-notes/plans/2026-10-28-execution-records-epic.md`). This issue is to (1) report two silent
no-ops in the meantime, and (2) list what Great Docs needs from freeze, as input to that design.

### Current behavior

- **`execute: freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml` is accepted without a warning** and does nothing: every
  render runs every cell, and nothing is written to `_freeze/`.
- **`q2 render --use-freezer` is accepted without a warning** and does nothing. The flag is parsed
  (`crates/quarto/src/main.rs`) but never read, and `use_freeze: false` is hard-coded where pass 2
  builds its `RenderOptions` (`crates/quarto-core/src/project/pass2_renderer.rs`).

A project that relies on freeze therefore builds fine on a machine that has every dependency, and
then fails, or slowly recomputes everything, in CI.

Execution records already get close. With `execute: {record: true, record-sources: "q2,engine"}`
in `_quarto.yml`, a second `q2 render` reuses each page's record from
`.quarto/execution-records/` instead of running its cells, and re-runs only the pages whose code
changed. That's essentially `freeze: auto`. With `record-sources: "q2"` alone, nothing runs, which is
the CI case. Records also survive moving the project to another directory. Two things I noticed:

- Removing `record: true` while keeping `record-sources` makes every record stale ("the document's
  code or options changed since it was recorded"), so it re-runs the cells, or with `q2` alone
  shows no output. The plan says `record` is excluded from the document hash, so this may be a bug.
- `q2 render page.qmd` reuses the record. Quarto 1 re-executes a page rendered on its own, even
  when it's frozen, and that's how a single page is refreshed.

### What Great Docs needs

Great Docs builds a Quarto project from a package's docs. Its freeze support works like this today:

- Great Docs turns on `execute: freeze: auto` by default. A page can set `freeze: true`, so it runs
  only when asked to, or `freeze: false`, so it runs on every build.
- Every build restores `docs/_freeze/` into the generated project before `quarto render`, and copies
  the updated cache back afterwards. Authors commit `docs/_freeze/`, so in CI, pages with heavy or
  private dependencies (model training, API calls, databases) don't run.
- `great-docs freeze <page>` renders one page with `quarto render <page>`, which executes it even if
  it's frozen, then saves the cache back to `docs/_freeze/`.
- Versioned docs keep a separate cache per version, which Great Docs copies between build
  directories, so a cache has to be relocatable, with nothing absolute inside it.

For that to work under q2, it needs:

1. **A committed, shareable location.** `.quarto/` is usually gitignored, and the records guide
   currently says a record "is not something to commit". Freeze is the durable use. Either a
   `_freeze/`-style directory, or a documented way to point the record location somewhere
   committable.
2. **`freeze: auto` semantics.** Reuse when the page's code and execution options are unchanged;
   re-run otherwise. Records' staleness rules look right for this; prose edits not invalidating is
   an improvement on Quarto 1.
3. **`freeze: true` semantics.** Never execute in a project render. The current
   `record-sources: "q2"` behavior (show no output, with a warning, when the record is stale) is
   fine, as long as the warning is visible and maybe opt-in to an error for CI.
4. **A way to force re-execution of one page**, ideally the Quarto 1 rule that rendering a named file
   executes it. Then `great-docs freeze` and `quarto render page.qmd` keep their meaning.
5. **A migration story for Quarto 1's `_freeze/`.** Importing it is out of scope in the epic, which
   is fine. A note in the docs saying "re-render frozen pages once with q2" would be enough, as long
   as the q2 cache doesn't collide with an existing `_freeze/` directory.
6. **Until then, a warning** when `execute: freeze` or `--use-freezer` is used, pointing to
   execution records, so the no-op isn't silent.

A short design note on how freeze will map onto records (location, the keys, single-file renders),
before it's built, would let us plan the Great Docs side.

Related: #45 (hub: freeze updates with incoming syntax errors?).

title: A page that fails to parse is left out of a website render, links to it break, and `post-render` doesn't run
description:
### Bug description

When one page of a website fails to parse, q2 renders the other pages and leaves that page out of
the site entirely. The parse error itself is clear and has a location. What follows is not:

1. **The error is labeled a warning.** It prints as
   `warning: profile-pass skipped <file>: Error: [Q-2-7] …`, but the summary counts it as an error.
2. **The follow-on warnings blame the wrong file.** Every sidebar entry and link to the dropped page
   gets a Q-13-1 or Q-13-4 warning saying it "is not in the project index" and to "check the
   spelling". The real cause is that the target failed to parse.
3. **Links to the dropped page stay `.qmd`.** The rendered HTML keeps `href="bad.qmd"`, in the body
   and in every page's sidebar, so they're broken links in the published site.
4. **`post-render` doesn't run**, and `q2 render` exits 1. The `_site` directory is left with the
   pages that rendered, but no post-processing. That's neither the full site nor a clean failure.
5. **A single-file render fails because of other pages.** `q2 render good.qmd` reports
   `bad.qmd`'s error and exits 1, even though `good.qmd` rendered.

q2's parser is stricter than Pandoc's, so many pages that Quarto 1 renders fail to parse under q2.
That makes this path common for existing sites. Great Docs' own docs have about 90 such pages under
q2. Great Docs' post-render scripts build shared sidebars, clean the search index and write page
tags, so skipping them breaks the whole site rather than one page. Great Docs also renders single
pages (`great-docs freeze`, example checks, an editor preview) and can't tell success from failure
from the exit status.

Related: #232 (parse errors prevent recovery) and #233 ("Sibling page failed to parse").

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir parse-drop && cd parse-drop
cat > _quarto.yml <<'EOF'
project:
  type: website
  post-render: post.py
website:
  sidebar:
    contents:
      - index.qmd
      - good.qmd
      - bad.qmd
EOF
printf 'from pathlib import Path\nPath("post-render-ran.txt").write_text("yes\\n")\n' > post.py
printf -- '---\ntitle: Home\n---\n\nSee [the good page](good.qmd) and [the bad page](bad.qmd).\n' > index.qmd
printf -- '---\ntitle: Good\n---\n\nFine.\n' > good.qmd
printf -- '---\ntitle: Bad\n---\n\nEdit `pyproject.toml`'"'"'s settings.\n' > bad.qmd
q2 render; echo "exit=$?"
ls _site post-render-ran.txt
grep -o 'href="[^"]*bad[^"]*"' _site/index.html _site/good.html
q2 render good.qmd; echo "exit=$?"
```

`bad.qmd` fails because of the apostrophe after the code span. That error is expected; this issue is
about what happens to the rest of the render.

### Actual behavior

```
Rendering project: /private/tmp/parse-drop (type: website)
warning: profile-pass skipped /private/tmp/parse-drop/bad.qmd: Error: [Q-2-7] Unclosed Single Quote
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/parse-drop/bad.qmd:5:34 ]
   │
 5 │ Edit `pyproject.toml`'s settings.
   │                      ┬           ┬
   │                      ╰────────────── This is the opening quote. If you need an apostrophe, escape it with a backslash.
   │                                  │
   │                                  ╰── I reached the end of the block before finding a closing "'" for the quote.
───╯

Warning: [Q-13-1] Sidebar references missing document
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/parse-drop/_quarto.yml:9:9 ]
   │
 9 │       - bad.qmd
   │         ───┬───
   │            ╰───── `bad.qmd` is not in the project index.
───╯
ℹ Check the spelling, or confirm the target file is included in the render set.

Affected files: /private/tmp/parse-drop/good.qmd, /private/tmp/parse-drop/index.qmd
Warning: [Q-13-4] Body link references missing document
   ╭─[ /private/tmp/parse-drop/index.qmd:5:50 ]
   │
 5 │ See [the good page](good.qmd) and [the bad page](bad.qmd).
   │                                                  ───┬───
   │                                                     ╰───── `bad.qmd` is not in the project index.
───╯
ℹ Check the spelling, or confirm the target file is included in the render set.

Rendered 2 of 3 files to /private/tmp/parse-drop/_site — 1 error, 3 warnings
exit=1
```

- `_site` has `good.html` and `index.html`, and no `bad.html`.
- `post-render-ran.txt` doesn't exist.
- `index.html` and `good.html` link to `bad.qmd`.
- `q2 render good.qmd` prints the same `bad.qmd` error and Q-13-1 warning, renders `good.html`,
  reports "Rendered 1 of 3 files … 1 error, 1 warning" and exits 1.

With the apostrophe escaped (`` `pyproject.toml`\'s ``), all three pages render, `post-render` runs
and the exit status is 0. Quarto 1.9.37 renders the original project, including `bad.html`, runs
`post-render` and exits 0.

### Expected behavior

- Print a page that failed to parse as an error, and say the page was not rendered.
- Have the Q-13-1 and Q-13-4 warnings say the target failed to render, or leave them out when
  their target failed, instead of suggesting a spelling mistake.
- Make the outcome of a failed page consistent. Either the render fails without leaving a partial
  site, or it finishes the site, `post-render` included, and exits non-zero. An option to choose
  (something like `--keep-going`) would suit tools like Great Docs, which want the full site plus a
  list of failed pages.
- For `q2 render <files>`, base the exit status on the named files, and report other pages' parse
  errors as warnings at most.
